company-research.notes: Scope: 14 capability records for company research. Verification method (2026-10-22): every URL cited in reference_scope and lawful_implementation_path was re-fetched with curl (raw HTML stripped to text, PDF converted with pdftotext) and with WebFetch. WebFetch returned HTTP 403 for all capitaliq.spglobal.com release notes, the IBKR Campus page, the IBKR UK product page, the IBKR TWS API pages and the TWS llms.txt, and timed out on the three nseindia.com pages; for these the quotes were checked against the curl-retrieved text, which returned HTTP 200 with full content. FRED's legal page failed under curl and was checked with WebFetch. Bloomberg function mnemonics come only from two university library guides (York, HBS; labelled academic) and two Bloomberg-hosted Pro Tips pages (vendor_marketing); no Bloomberg official function documentation was reachable. Key findings: (1) SEC companyfacts aggregates only non-custom taxonomy facts, so as-filed statements require parsing each filing's XBRL instance. (2) The companyfacts 'filed' field is a date only. (3) Verifier finding: the submissions JSON acceptanceDateTime carries a 'Z' suffix but did not equal true UTC on three samples checked against EDGAR filing index 'Accepted' times (Eastern): the JSON value lagged true UTC by the Eastern UTC offset (4 h in EDT, 5 h in EST). Point-in-time knowledge time must come from the EDGAR 'Accepted' Eastern time converted with America/New_York rules, and the Apple acceptance test was rewritten with exact UTC timestamps. (4) The SEC frames API returns the last filed fact, so it is not point-in-time and must not be used in backtests. (5) NSE terms prohibit systematic or automated data collection and also prohibit using website data or content for 'gaming, virtual trading or simulation activities', so India filings and ownership need a licensed feed with simulation rights; owner-downloaded NSE files cannot feed backtests or paper trading. (6) FRED terms prohibit storing, caching or archiving content and use in developing or training ML/AI systems, so DCF risk-free inputs come from the US Treasury and ECB curves. (7) The fetched interactivebrokers.com TWS API index has no entry containing 'fundamental', but it points to a complete index at ibkrcampus.com that returned 403, so the absence is not proven. (8) Capital IQ Pro's September 2026 release added three selectable TEV options, DCF for non-banking companies only, point-in-time trading comps and formula-based Excel exports; these are functional-parity targets, and our EV formulas are not claimed to match CIQ's methodology. (9) ESAP is not live: Accountancy Europe states go-live is mandated by 10 July 2027, with core financial and sustainability data under the Accounting and CSRD directives from January 2028. filings.xbrl.org is the interim free ESEF source and states that it is incomplete (Germany and Ireland gaps). Parity statements in parity_dimensions.functional are targets and remain unproven until each record's acceptance criteria pass. Priorities: identity resolution and the US filings feed are P0; the rest of company research is P1, and spreadsheet/API access and document Q&A are P2.

data-providers.notes:
Scope: 14 provider/dataset-family records for the provider registry area, aligned with book ch.11 (source registry fields, deny-until-rights-resolved) and ch.23 (display/non-display/storage/redistribution/AI-processing distinctions), and with config/deployment_record.example.json (market_data_entitlements, model_processing_rights_verified).

Verification method (2026-10-22): all 52 distinct URLs cited by the researcher were re-fetched. 41 were downloaded with curl and every quoted phrase was string-matched against the page text; SEC pages (curl received HTTP 403 'Request Rate Threshold Exceeded' without a declared User-Agent), FRED pages (curl connection failures) and the JS-rendered Tiingo pricing page were checked with WebFetch; the Alpha Vantage terms PDF was converted with pdftotext. Redirects observed: openfigi.com/api -> /api/overview; docs.benzinga.com -> /introduction/welcome; ECB disclaimer -> /services/using-our-site/disclaimer/html/index.en.html; NSE market-data pages -> /static/market-data/...; massive.com/pricing?type=business served the same content as massive.com/pricing. Three extra verification fetches were made: one filings.xbrl.org API record (field names) and HEAD/GET probes of filings-2019/2020/2021.json. The unfetchable list is the researcher's and was not re-checked.

Evidence added during verification: FMP personal licence forbids copying or downloading content without prior written approval and defines Commercial Use to include analysis supporting data-driven decision-making; EODHD states it does not use exchange data feeds for pricing data (VWAP over 100+ sources); OpenFIGI includeUnlistedEquities also returns delisted equities; SEC processing delays may be longer at peak filing times; filings.xbrl.org reserves the right to apply rate limits and asks for a User-Agent with contact e-mail; Alpha Vantage economic/commodity APIs bind users to FRED terms; Kite caps modifications at 25 per order; IBKR Network B subscription and 100 free snapshot quotes per month; RBI may block access by Internet address; FRED throttling non-compliance can cause a temporary block; Fiscal Data default page size 100 and meta total-count.

Findings that change design decisions (verified): (1) Massive Market Data is display-only unless a subsequent agreement says otherwise; non-display use or investment-strategy derivation requires a licence, so individual plans cannot feed autonomous signals; business feed expansions are listed at $499 to $1,999/month plus exchange fees. (2) NSE's website terms prohibit scraping, storing without permission, and use for gaming, virtual trading or simulation; lawful India paths are NSE Data & Analytics agreements, Zerodha Kite Connect (Rs 500/month; 1/3/10 req/s) and IBKR NSE subscriptions (free delayed data is 15 minutes behind). (3) IBKR API market data requires IBKR PRO, a funded non-demo account, USD 500 minimum equity (USD 100 for Indian residents with IB India), the Market Data API Acknowledgement; users are Professional by default; API data is off-platform; no delayed US equity quotes; the free US stream (Cboe One + IEX) is non-consolidated; line allowance = max(100, commissions/8, equity*100/1e6) plus USD 30 boosters of 100 lines each (max 10). (4) FMP requires deletion of all data including cached data on termination, notification of storage locations, a display agreement, and written approval before copying or downloading content. (5) Eurostat keeps no past versions, so vintages must be self-snapshotted; the ECB API returns all previous versions with includeHistory=true. (6) RBI DBIE has no documented API and RBI's website disclaimer restricts caching; manual import only. (7) SEC fair access: 10 requests/s per user regardless of machines, declared User-Agent; FRED 120 requests/min, third-party 'Copyright' series restricted; OpenFIGI 25 or 250 mapping requests per 60 s window; FIGIs are public domain. (8) None of the fetched vendor terms address sending licensed data to third-party cloud LLMs; default deny.

Records align with book Chapters 9, 12 and 13, with repository ADR-0009, ADR-0011 and ADR-0012, and with contracts/broker_port.py.

Researcher's method caveats:
- WebFetch returned 403 for most interactivebrokers.com pages. The official IBKR docs were retrieved as their published .md versions under https://www.interactivebrokers.com/docs/tws-api/doc/... and /docs/web-api/.... interactivebrokers.github.io (legacy, marked deprecated) and ibkrguides.com were also fetched.

The researcher then fetched only URLs already known, so these areas are not covered: UK settlement timing, EU and India IBKR commission schedules, Kite pricing and contract notes, licensed corporate-action datasets, and exchange data-licence terms.
- The EMSX API details come from a readthedocs guide (c) 2017 Terrence C. Kim. Bloomberg authorship is not confirmed, and the content may be dated. Those references are labelled source_type 'other'. Bloomberg and LSEG product pages are labelled vendor_marketing.

Verifier pass (2026-10-22): all 72 distinct URLs cited in reference_scope and lawful_implementation_path were re-fetched, mostly with curl. 71 returned HTTP 200. The SEC EDGAR APIs page returned 403 to curl and was read via WebFetch. Results:
- 63 URLs supported every claim attributed to them as written.
- 9 URLs supported their quotes only in part, or were mislabelled or misattributed. Each was corrected; see verification.removed_claims.
- No reference entry had to be deleted outright.

What a retail IBKR account exposes, per fetched docs:
- Available: the TWS API via TWS or IB Gateway, and the Web API trading API ('available to all IBKR clients free of cost'). Also the Flex Web Service, Client Portal statements, the Corporate Action Manager and TCA.
- FIX: available, but requires 10,000 USD minimum equity and carries a minimum commission of 1,500 USD/month for the first session.
- Not assumed for retail: the Account Management API, documented for introducing brokers and financial advisors.
- Unverified for an individual account: Pre-Trade Compliance and Org Portal trading limits.

Settlement facts verified:
- US: T+1 compliance date 28 May 2024 (SEC).
- India: NSE runs T+1 with a T+0 settlement type.
- EU: T+2 since 2015. Regulation (EU) 2025/2075 applies from 11 October 2027 (national central bank register; the EUR-Lex text was not readable).

instruments.notes:
Research date 2026-10-22. Book chapters read: 01, 02, 03, 11, 33 (docs/book). The records cover these book requirements: the instrument master in ch. 3 (never key on a display ticker, versioned provider mappings, non-overlapping effective intervals, stop the route on a mapping disagreement), the time and calendar rules in ch. 3 (immutable calendar versions, UTC storage, DST) and the rights-in-pipeline rule in ch. 11.

Evidence handling (researcher):
(1) Every reference_scope and lawful_implementation_path URL was fetched in the research session. Some were fetched with WebFetch, others with curl because WebFetch could not render them (NSE JSON and CSV endpoints, NSE terms and data policy pages, the ESMA FIRDS file index, LSEG-API-Samples notebooks). PDFs were extracted locally with pdftotext.
(2) The shared WebSearch budget ran out partway through, so several gaps remain open questions: the LSE holiday and half-day calendar, the BSE holiday and scrip master, the DTCC settlement calendar, the SEBI India T+1 rule, the ESMA EU T+1 date and RIC licensing terms.
(3) The NSE terms of use prohibit 'systematic or automated data collection activities (including scraping, data mining, data extraction and data harvesting)'. The NSE retrievals were one-off research checks of formats and dates. They are not a proposed ingestion method. Every record routes NSE data through licensed NSE Data products or broker APIs.
(4) Bloomberg function mnemonics are cited only where a fetched page states them. DVD and CACS come from one HBS library guide; a second HBS page gives CACT for the corporate actions menu. The conflict is recorded as unverified. SECF and CDR are not cited.
(5) Capital IQ identifier coverage differs between library guides: SMU lists CUSIP and SEDOL for S&P Capital IQ; INSEAD's download table lists tickers, CUSIPs, CIK and GVKEY but not SEDOL. S&P's own product pages returned 403 or rendered with JavaScript only.
(6) Latency targets in acceptance criteria are proposed project budgets, not vendor-published figures.

macro-rates-fx.notes:
14 records: 1 at P0, 12 at P1 and 1 at P2. The P0 record is official FX reference rates (ECB, H.10, FBIL), which Ch 3 needs for base-currency valuation. The P2 record is market-implied policy-rate paths, which needs licensed CME data.

Sources and fetching
- The researcher's shared WebSearch budget ran out partway through; later evidence came from direct WebFetch or curl of known official URLs.
- Retrieved with curl instead of WebFetch (cited at exact URLs): ECB Data API endpoints (EXR, YC parameters and spot/forward rates, EST, MNA includeHistory), the ECB API help text, the Treasury XML feed for October 2026, the BEA release_dates.json, the MOSPI calendar PDF and the BLS API v2 response. The Datastream fact sheet and HKEX circular PDFs were text-extracted with pdftotext.
- ECB vintage history is shallow: an includeHistory=true query for euro area GDP growth returned one version per observation, all VALID_FROM 2026-07-15. Eurostat states it keeps only the latest dataset version. Our own snapshots are the only public path to euro area and India vintages found.

Vendor function names and scope
- Bloomberg names come only from fetched pages: ECO and EVTS on the enterprise event-driven-feeds page; ECST, WECO, ECFC and ECMX on a University of Michigan library guide. No other Bloomberg function name is used. The policy-expectations record maps to the economics page's generic statement 'Interest rate probability models are updated daily'; Bloomberg's function name for it is unverified.
- The Datastream evidence is a 2022 Refinitiv fact sheet hosted by the University of Zurich, not an LSEG-hosted page.
- S&P Capital IQ Pro scope rests only on a 2023 press release (40+ indicators, 200+ countries, ChartIQ charting).
- IBKR scope rests on ibkrguides pages (Event Calendar, FXTrader, Risk Navigator), the deprecated GitHub TWS API docs, and the gdcdyn page listing Econoday under Complimentary Services as Free. IBKR pricing and market-data pages returned 403, so IBKR fees and redistribution terms are unverified.
- Usability and latency comparisons with vendor products are not claimed unless a fetched page states them.

Rights findings that change the design
- ECB: free reuse including commercial, source quoted, statistics unmodified; derived analytics must be labelled derived. ECB reference rates are 'for information purposes only'; restricted to valuation and reporting.
- NY Fed: notice and disclaimer required whenever reference rate data is used or distributed; storage and derivative works permitted; redistribution must carry the same permissions.
- FRED: prominent notice; data-owner permission for copyrighted series beyond personal use; no AI-processing provisions.
- Bank of England: no API; electronic storage acceptable under its copyright conditions.
- India: FBIL and RBI DBIE are JavaScript-only to the fetcher; their terms are unverified and their records are gated off until rights are recorded (Ch 11).

Chapter and requirement links (checked against the repo): DAT-03, RES-02 and DOM-02 in docs/requirements/register.md; Ch 3 eq. 3.2; Ch 17 (consensus snapshot precedence, regime limits); Ch 21 (FX forward relation, automatic currency borrowing disabled, S18).

Gaps not researched: UK ONS release calendar and BoE MPC calendar; per-country euro sovereign curves; RBI forecaster survey; CCIL and NSE INR curves; IMF, OECD and World Bank data; CME licensing terms; BEA data API; fees and terms for Trading Economics and LSEG.

market-data.notes:
Scope: 13 capability records covering Level 1 quote status, consolidated vs venue quotes, time & sales, intraday bars, daily bars with corporate-action adjustment, depth, charting/studies, watchlists, alerts, point-in-time screening, an entitlement/fee registry, India (NSE/BSE) and Europe (venues + EU tape). The records tie back to book chapters 01, 02, 05, 11 and 22: quote status and age, missing is not zero, completed bars only, versioned corrections, and a source registry before ingestion.

Evidence: IBKR documentation was fetched as .md pages from https://www.interactivebrokers.com/docs/... . Bloomberg evidence comes from professional.bloomberg.com product pages (marketing), the NYU library guide (mnemonics GP and EQS), a Bloomberg 'Functions for the Market' PDF hosted by the Bodleian Library, and MathWorks documentation for the PiTDate/AsOf override. No other Bloomberg mnemonics are claimed except MAPS, which appears on the Bloomberg charts page. LSEG evidence comes from the official LSEG Data Guide chapters 4 and 10 on developers.lseg.com. S&P evidence comes from Capital IQ Pro release notes and an S&P-hosted watchlists/alerts help page.

Key findings that affect design:
(1) IBKR Level 1 data is aggregated snapshots, not tick-by-tick; TWS API documents 250 ms for US stocks. The Web API interval is not documented on any fetched page.
(2) IBKR provides no data for securities that no longer trade, which creates a survivorship gap.
(3) IBKR's TRADES bars are split-adjusted only; ADJUSTED_LAST bars are adjusted for both splits and dividends.
(4) IBKR does not provide studies or indicators through its API.
(5) IBKR classifies every user as Professional by default, and API data counts as off-platform.
(6) The US CT Plan replaces the CTA and UTP plans on the Operative Date, planned for 2027-04-01. Its fees: non-professional on a sliding scale from USD 0.90 to 0.25; Tape A professional at a flat USD 26.
(7) The SEC xbrl/frames API returns, per entity, the last-filed fact that most closely fits the requested calendar period, so it is not point-in-time. Point-in-time reconstruction has to use the companyfacts/companyconcept 'filed' date.
(8) NSE's non-display policy explicitly covers automated trading and derived data used for internal analysis.
(9) ESMA authorised EuroCTP (trade press, 28 July 2026), and a distributor named 14 Sep 2026 as the go-live date. One regional news article (29 Sep 2026) reports the tape went live on 14 Sep 2026. This has not been confirmed from ESMA or EuroCTP pages, which returned 403 or no content.

Verification pass (2026-10-22): an adversarial re-fetch of all 66 cited URLs. Every reference_scope quote was found on its page; one quote's wording was corrected (ibkrguides Level II page). Fifteen lawful-path or rights claims were attached to pages that do not contain them; these were corrected or moved to the page that does. Unsupported specifics were removed: the Web API 500 ms interval, USD 35 Benzinga, the 'lines/2' pacing figure, error code 100, quote booster, calendar-month billing and paper-account data sharing, the 60 s scanner refresh, and 'fair-access guidance'. The IEX DEEP description was corrected: DEEP is price-aggregated, DEEP+ is order-by-order. Five URLs were added after being fetched. Acceptance criteria were tightened so that each one names a concrete fixture or threshold. model-providers.notes:
Checked the Chapter 19 model names and prices on 2026-10-22 against the official pages (all re-fetched by the verifier):
- 'GPT-6.1-sol', 'GPT-6-luna', 'GPT-6-astra' do not appear verbatim with that capitalisation. The API ids are lowercase `gpt-6.1-sol`, `gpt-6-luna` and `gpt-6-astra` (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing). The display names are 'GPT-6.1 Sol', 'GPT-6 Luna' and 'GPT-6 Astra' (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models).
- The short-context (≤272K input tokens) Standard prices on the OpenAI pricing page match the book: gpt-6.1-sol $2.00/$10.00, gpt-6-luna $0.10/$0.50, gpt-6-astra $10.00/$50.00 per 1M tokens. The same table has separate long-context (>272K input tokens) prices, which the book does not mention; whether the long-context rate applies to all tokens of the request was not captured.
- The OpenAI models page says 'If you're not sure where to start, use GPT-6 Astra, our flagship model for complex reasoning and coding'. The pricing page states 'Priority processing was renamed Fast mode on July 30, 2026'.
- 'Grok 4.7' appears verbatim at https://docs.x.ai/developers/models: 'For everything else, including code, use Grok 4.7. It is the most capable model we've built.' Its API id is `grok-4.7`.
- grok-4.7 costs $2.00 input / $6.00 output (cached input $0.50) below 200k prompt tokens, which matches the book. At 200k prompt tokens or more it costs $4.00/$12.00 (cached $1.00), and every token in that request is billed at the higher rate. The book does not mention this band.
- The book's Eq. 19.1 examples ($6.00/day and $5.20/day) are arithmetically correct before C_tools and C_retries.
- The book's source URLs S25-S28 (docs/book/33-primary-source-register.md) were all fetched successfully by the verifier.

Other findings that affect the book or the register:
1. The xAI docs name the company 'SpaceXSI' on the security FAQ and regional-endpoints pages, while API hosts and contact addresses use x.ai. Record the contracting entity from current terms before production.
2. Gemini publishes scheduled price increases on its pricing page (Gemini 4 Argon on 2026-12-01; Gemini 3.8 Flash on 2027-01-01). So tariffs must be effective-dated, and register AI-02's 'no hard-coded prices' needs effective dates, not just versions.
3. Gemini documents the Interactions API as recommended for new projects and calls generateContent 'legacy' (still fully supported). Interactions are stored by default: 55 days on the paid tier, 1 day on the free tier. Adapters must send store=false for restricted data. Explicit context caching is unavailable on Gemini 4 Argon onward and in the Interactions API.
4. Anthropic's retention page says conversation content is not retained by default, except Covered Models (Fable 5.1, Mythos 5.1, Fable 5, Mythos 5), which require 30-day retention and are not available under ZDR unless expressly authorized. Anthropic forced tool use (tool_choice any/tool) is rejected on Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1, including on the token counting endpoint.
5. No provider fetched here offers in-region processing in India; OpenAI lists India as storage-only. Only OpenAI documents EU processing. Anthropic offers inference_geo us or global only. xAI offers a US endpoint only, for grok-4.7 and grok-4.6.
6. Rate-limit headers are documented by OpenAI and Anthropic, and Mistral documents one (X-RateLimit-Remaining). None were found for xAI or Gemini. Overload codes: OpenAI 503 server_is_overloaded, Anthropic 529 overloaded_error, Gemini 503 service_unavailable. xAI documents no 5xx codes.
7. Batch discounts: OpenAI 50% (batch guide), Anthropic 50%, Gemini 50%, xAI 20% (listed models only), Mistral 50% (marketing FAQ).
8. Verifier corrections: xAI does document a text tokenizer (POST /v1/tokenize-text, https://docs.x.ai/developers/rest-api-reference/inference/other); the OpenAI model object includes an optional shutdown_date; xAI catalog price fields are documented in USD cents per 100 million tokens.

Evidence caveats:
- Most non-Anthropic quotes come from WebFetch's summarising model, not raw page text. Items marked 'close paraphrase' are paraphrases. Re-verify exact wording against the live pages before copying any of it into the book.
- platform.claude.com pages returned raw text.
- Vendor terminal pages (S&P, LSEG) are marketing and are used only for functional scope.
- The researcher's web-search budget ran out partway through. The IBKR AI scope and Mistral tier limits could not be researched further.
- OpenAI, Anthropic, xAI and Mistral master API terms were not fetched. Data-policy facts come from their documentation pages.
- Prices in these records are observations dated 2026-10-22 and must not be copied into code as constants.

multiasset.notes:
Scope: 14 records for book chapter 21 (options, fixed income, futures, FX, crypto), each research-only with trading disabled in the initial eligibility profile. The P0 record is the eligibility gate that enforces this. All analytics records are P1-P3 because they are not needed for the stocks paper desk.

Evidence method: the verifier re-fetched every cited URL on 2026-10-22. www.interactivebrokers.com, LSEG, Bloomberg cirrus-mirror, S&P press, Treasury, ECB, Fed, NY Fed, Kite, OPRA, CCIL (PDF), TreasuryDirect, FINRA developer, OCC, Eurex, Coinbase docs, Kraken and arXiv pages were fetched with curl (HTTP 200). The three www.finra.org pages returned 403 to curl and were fetched with WebFetch. Bloomberg function scope (OVME, OVDV, OMON/OMST/OVI/OPX, OVML, YAS, FIW/PORT) comes only from marketing or webinar pages on Bloomberg's own mirror and is not documentation of how those functions work. S&P Capital IQ Pro scope comes only from two S&P press releases.

Added during verification (fetched 2026-10-22): IBKR TWS API delayed-data page (market data types 1-4; 15-minute delayed US data), IBKR stocks/futures-options/CFD contract pages (secType STK covers stocks and ETFs; FOP; CFD), Kraken Get OHLC Data page (720 entries; uncommitted last bar), Cboe SPX delayed quote table (auto-extraction prohibition), NSE website terms (https://www.nseindia.com/static/nse-terms-of-use: automated collection and 'gaming, virtual trading or simulation' use prohibited), FRED legal page via WebFetch (storing/caching prohibited), eCFR 31 CFR Part 356 (Appendix B Treasury auction formulas).

Rights findings that change the design:
(1) The Cboe delayed-quote pages prohibit auto-extraction.
(2) The NSE website prohibits automated collection and any use of its data for 'gaming, virtual trading or simulation activities'. NSE website data therefore cannot feed the paper desk.
(3) CCIL prohibits automated collection and commercial use without written consent.
(4) The FRED terms prohibit storing or caching FRED content. Use the primary sources instead: Treasury, ECB, NY Fed.
(5) The OPRA subscriber agreement limits use to own business or personal use with no retransmission or furnishing to any person. For nonprofessionals it is limited to personal investment activities. Whether storing derived data, automated use, or cloud-model processing is permitted is unresolved.
(6) FINRA TRACE real-time data is free for a Non-Professional's personal, non-commercial use. The FINRA API Fixed Income terms allow non-commercial use and derivative data.
(7) ECB statistics can be reused free with attribution and unmodified, but third-party data needs originator permission, and the ECB yield curves are built from MTS Markets bond prices. ECB FX reference rates are 'for information purposes only'.
(8) Kraken requires prior permission for any non-personal commercial use of its public market data.
(9) IBKR's NSE F&O (L1) package is footnoted 'Services only available for Indian Residents.'
(10) IBKR uses secType STK for both stocks and ETFs, so a broker secType allow-list cannot block leveraged or inverse ETFs. The risk kernel's own classification is the only automated guard for those.

Contradiction to resolve: IBKR's market-data pricing page says it 'no longer offers delayed quotation information on U.S. equities to Interactive Brokers LLC clients', while the TWS API delayed-data page says IBKR 'provides 15-minute delayed market data for US Network exchanges'. Both pages were fetched.

Prices from the IBKR market-data page (retrieved 2026-10-22; owner should recheck before subscribing):
- OPRA L1: USD 1.50/month non-pro, USD 32.75/month pro. Waived at USD 20 commissions per month.
- CME Real-Time L1: USD 1.55/month non-pro, N/A pro.
- TRACE (BTDS): N/A non-pro, USD 65.00/month pro.
- Fee waived: IBKR Currencies; US Bond Real-Time Data (includes US corporate bonds and US Treasuries); Eurex Core L1 (non-pro); NSE F&O L1 (Indian residents only).

news-documents.notes:
Context read: docs/book/01, 11, 17, 19, 23, 33 and docs/requirements/register.md. The relevant IDs are DAT-03 (news/transcripts data), AI-04 (untrusted documents and prompt-injection tests) and PAR-01 (capability register). The 14 records map to those requirements.

Evidence limits:
(1) Every official bloomberg.com page returned 403. Bloomberg scope therefore rests only on third-party trade press (fintechnews.sg, 2024-01-23; thetradenews.com, 2025-01-15), labelled source_type 'other'. No Bloomberg function mnemonics are asserted.
(2) Most interactivebrokers.com documentation and pricing pages returned 403. IBKR claims come from interactivebrokers.github.io/tws-api. BOTH news.html and fundamentals.html say 'This documentation is now deprecated' and point to IBKR Campus. IBKR news fees and the depth or limits of reqHistoricalNews are unverified.
(3) The ESMA/ESAP, EUR-Lex, BSE, Business Wire, GlobeNewswire, Benzinga licensing and Dow Jones pages could not be fetched, so EU disclosure access is marked unavailable/unverified.
(4) NSE pages time out in WebFetch, but curl with a browser User-Agent retrieves them. The NSE terms forbid systematic or automated data collection and storage without prior written permission. That conflicts with the existence of RSS feeds declaring ttl=5. The design ships NSE automation disabled until permission is granted or a licence is held. Feed-sample statistics come from the researcher's single capture of Online_announcements.xml (scratchpad/nse/ann.xml): 1,219 items; 21 mention transcripts; 10 contain the exact phrase 'Transcripts - earnings or quarterly calls'.
(5) Licence findings that matter:
- PR Newswire forbids database storage and AI training.
- The LSEG Workspace news API is for individual users only, with no server-side use.
- FinBERT weights are CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.
- Loughran-McDonald needs a commercial licence outside academic research.
- GLEIF data is CC0, with liquidated damages of CHF 100'000 per case of non-compliance.
- Cloud-LLM processing rights for licensed news and transcripts were found for no vendor, so they default to deny.
(6) Numerical targets marked 'proposed' are owner design targets, not vendor facts.
(7) A data.sec.gov submissions JSON fetched for CIK0001065088 on 2026-10-22 exposes items (e.g. '2.02,2.05') and acceptanceDateTime per filing. Research availability uses first-observed time, not acceptance time.
(8) Several LSEG pages (Intelligent Tagging fact sheet, real-time news page, MarketPsych page, StarMine MMS fact sheet) do not name Workspace. Their product labels now say 'LSEG (...)' rather than asserting a Workspace module. The Kensho page names 'S&P Capital IQ' datasets and the Kensho LLM-ready API, not Capital IQ Pro, and is labelled accordingly.

ops-aws.notes:
Scope: 14 operational capability records (6 P0 for the Mac paper desk, 8 P1 for the AWS path). Reference products are vendor-hosted, so several controls (spend cap, encryption at rest, AWS Backup) have no documented terminal equivalent; those records say so instead of claiming parity.

Key findings:
(1) IBKR documents that a headless TWS/IB Gateway session is not supported. Login is manual, auto-restart (version 974+) covers daily restarts, credentials must be re-entered weekly, and 2FA is mandatory. Unattended weekly login is therefore unavailable and excluded. IBC (GPLv3) fills in credentials but cannot complete card/device logins; its repository was retired on 1 September 2026 and archived. It is not adopted.
(2) IBKR states that a TWS/IBGW session whose username also logs in to Client Portal will not reconnect automatically after the next disconnection. The gateway username must therefore differ from the Client Portal username used for Flex setup.
(3) IBKR paper accounts always connect to a US server. TWS server locations are New York, Chicago, Zurich, Hong Kong and Singapore (from the Host and Ports PDF), plus a Shenzhen gateway for mainland-China users. None is in India.
(4) The IB Gateway Stable download page offers Linux X86_64 and Linux ARM64 installers.
(5) reqExecutions returns only the current day's executions, so restoring an older backup requires Flex reports for earlier days.
(6) AWS Budgets updates up to three times a day and can notify late, so it is not a hard cap. Preventive IaC limits are primary.
(7) CloudWatch's default sliding evaluation window can delay detection of a stopped heartbeat beyond period x evaluation periods. Detection delay is measured.
(8) Apple TN3137: launchd daemons cannot use the data-protection keychain, and that keychain needs provisioning-profile entitlements. From macOS 26.4, file-based keychain files may depend on protected entropy files.
(9) sqlite.org: synchronous=FULL in rollback mode is not necessarily durable across power loss. The WAL-reset bug affects 3.7.0 to 3.51.2, is fixed in 3.51.3 and backported to 3.44.6 and 3.50.7. SQLite is public domain.

Local observations (not URL-cited; re-checked by the verifier on 2026-10-22):
- macOS 26.6.2 (build 25G83).
- /usr/bin/sqlite3 is 3.51.0. Homebrew Python 3.14.7 links SQLite 3.53.4.
- reference/engine.py sets journal_mode=DELETE and synchronous=FULL. ADR-0003 specifies WAL, FULL, foreign_keys, busy_timeout, fullfsync and checkpoint_fullfsync.
- man launchd.plist confirms: SuccessfulExit and Crashed semantics, ThrottleInterval default 10 s, ExitTimeOut system-defined (0 means infinity).
- man launchctl lists bootstrap, kickstart, kill and print.

Verifier method: every cited URL was re-downloaded with curl on 2026-10-22; interactivebrokers.com serves the .md doc pages and PDFs to curl. Pages were converted to text (PDFs with pdftotext), and each supporting quote was checked as a normalised verbatim substring. Two extra pages were fetched to resolve gaps: https://www.sqlite.org/copyright.html and https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/reference/ec2/describe-instance-type-offerings.html.

portfolio-risk.notes:
Scope: 13 capability records. P0 (needed for the stocks paper desk): holdings/cash consolidation, P&L and lots, exposure/concentration, TWR/MWR, and the what-if pre-trade sandbox. P1: risk-adjusted statistics, benchmark rights registry, Brinson attribution, factor risk model, VaR/ES, stress scenarios, optimisation. P2: returns-based factor attribution.

Evidence quality:
- IBKR is the best-documented reference. The white papers on MWR/TWR, performance attribution, and risk measures and exposure give formulas and worked examples; the verifier recomputed every worked example used in an acceptance criterion (Modified Dietz -4.67%, TWR link 0.14%, 10/4 sub-period -4.68% start-of-day vs -4.46% end-of-day, IR 0.433259, Sharpe 1.621, beta 0.9682 population-cov/sample-var vs 1.2909 consistent, BHB allocation 0.00135, selection 0.00275, Frongello -0.245% / -0.775625%). The Risk Navigator user guide and IBKR Campus lessons document VaR (Historical and Monte Carlo; 99/99.5/99.9%; 1-4 days; 100% only in Historical; sub-portfolio aggregation at currency and portfolio levels), ES, custom scenarios and what-if portfolios. The TWS API docs cover positions, P&L and WhatIf.
- Bloomberg PORT evidence is marketing and webinar pages only (professional.bloomberg.com and professional.content.cirrus.bloomberg.com). Named items found on fetched pages: MAC HPA, MAC3 GRM with six horizons, FBS factor-based scenarios, SHOK macro model, four scenario types, integrated optimization, Data Validation Service.
- LSEG Workspace evidence is marketing only (fact sheet and product pages): cross-asset attribution, style analysis, MSCI RiskMetrics VaR (parametric, historical simulation, Monte Carlo), MSCI Barra Optimiser, and a proprietary Global Equity Risk Model.
- S&P Capital IQ evidence comes from the S&P Capital IQ release notes (March 15 and June 15, 2024) and the Capital IQ Pro portfolio analytics landing page. The release-note pages are titled 'S&P Capital IQ Release Notes'; whether the features also apply to Capital IQ Pro is not explicit (unverified).

Findings that affect parity tests:
1. IBKR's TWR white paper says account cash flows are end of day, but its worked example is reproduced only with the flow added to BMV (start-of-day). The convention to match is an open question.
2. IBKR's beta example (published 0.968214) equals population covariance divided by sample variance; a consistent formula on the same four data points gives 1.291.
3. IBKR's Sharpe annualizes daily data with n = 360 and uses the US 3-month T-bill. Its Sortino uses the S&P 500 since-inception return, which is licensed data.
4. IBKR attribution is BHB-style: allocation against the benchmark segment return, selection includes interaction, Frongello linking, purchases at start of day.
5. IBKR's exposure percentages are printed as Total Long Value / (Total Long Value + Total Short Value); whether the short value is signed in the denominator is not stated.

Rights blockers:
- Index constituent and level data (S&P DJI, MSCI, FTSE Russell, STOXX, NSE Indices) needs licences. FRED's S&P 500 copy is copyright-restricted (reproduction prohibited without S&P DJI written permission) and limited to 10 years. NSE Indices requires prior approval and fees where applicable for institutional benchmarking; whether that applies to an individual is unverified. Deutsche Boerse/ISS STOXX restricts certain information to licensed Data Centre accounts.
- The lawful default is an ETF total-return proxy built from IBKR-licensed exchange data, with SEC N-PORT (quarterly data sets, N-PORT filers only) as a lagged source of constituent weights.
- Free lawful inputs verified: FRED DTB3 (Public Domain: Citation Requested; internal commercial use permitted by FRED's summarized terms), US Treasury bill rates (terms not fetched), ECB EUR STR (ECB states it does not charge for or license it) and ECB FX reference rates (information purposes only), Kenneth French factor library (licence terms not stated), IIMA India factors (Oct 1993 to Dec 2025, release 2025-12), Fed 2026 severely adverse and historic CSVs, EBA 2025 market risk shocks (US, EU, and India via a regional aggregate plus EURINR), BIS ES at 97.5% and desk-level VaR backtesting at 97.5% and 99%, GIPS 2020 calculation provisions, and OSQP (Apache 2.0).
- No INR risk-free source could be fetched (RBI DBIE and FBIL are JavaScript applications).

regulatory.notes:
Re-verification of book register S11-S21, S41, S42 as of 2026-10-22, followed by an adversarial verification pass on the same day.

Confirmed:
- S11, FINRA Notice 26-10: published April 20, 2026; effective June 4, 2026; phase-in over 18 months until October 20, 2027. The core provisions are in new paragraph (d)(2) of Rule 4210. The deficit determination excludes good faith and portfolio margin accounts. Real-time monitoring is not required. The 90-day restriction applies when a customer makes a practice of failing to satisfy deficits as promptly as possible AND fails to satisfy a deficit by close of business on the fifth business day; it lasts 90 calendar days or until the deficit is satisfied. Deficits up to the lesser of 5 percent of margin-account equity or $1,000 do not count toward that practice. A deficit remains outstanding until satisfied or until the close of business on the 15th business day.
- S12, Rule 15c3-5 compliance guide: still served, 'Modified: 01/06/2011'. Current rule text checked on eCFR (Title 17 up to date as of 10/20/2026, last amended 10/19/2026).
- S15, SEBI Feb 4, 2025: original effective date August 01, 2025.
- S16, NSE/INVG/67858: TOPS 10 OPS per exchange, static IP, daily logout, 5-year broker audit trail.
- S18, RBI Forex FAQ: updated as on August 28, 2024. Q6 bars LRS remittance of margin for online forex trading. Its disclaimer says FEMA and rules prevail over FAQs.
- S21, IRS Topic 429: last reviewed 24-Sep-2026.
- S42, Reg SHO key points: 'Modified: 5/31/2022'.

Corrections and additions for the book register:
(1) S13 was revised: 'Updated August 7, 2026'; its freeriding example now uses one-business-day settlement. The book's caveat about older examples can be narrowed.
(2) S15 needs a companion: SEBI/HO/MIRSD/MIRSD-PoD/P/CIR/2025/132 (Sep 30, 2025). It records the earlier extension to October 01, 2025 (circular dated July 29, 2025, not fetched) and sets a glide path: milestones 31 October 2025, 30 November 2025 and January 03, 2026, with an onboarding bar from January 05, 2026 for non-compliant brokers. The framework applies to all stock brokers w.e.f. April 01, 2026.
(3) S17: NSE/INVG/73992 (April 30, 2026, Circular Ref 31/2026) was read from the NSE zip attachment. It is the Consolidated Circular for the Non-NEAT Frontend facility and replaces NSE/MSD/67753. s.8.4.8.16 says retail algorithms 'should be hosted on brokers’ cloud servers/environment', which conflicts with the book's AWS/Mac hosting for India unless the broker confirms otherwise. s.8.4.1 exempts only 'Tech Savvy retail investor (within OPS threshold)' from per-algo registration; s.8.4.7 requires Algo ID '99999' for non-registered client algos within 10 OPS. s.8.4.8.2 requires the broker's routing server to be in India. s.8.1.12 bars algo market orders and the s.8.6 table repeats this as the Market Price Protection check, with further mandatory controls (runaway stop, no unlimited values). A note restricts the static IP requirement to tech-savvy retail investors. The NSE overview page shows 'Updated on: 27/05/2026'.
(4) S19 and S20: the ESMA URLs return 403, and EUR-Lex returns HTTP 202 with an empty or bot-verification body. The register should add the EU Publications Office Cellar OJ texts (original 2014 versions) and mark the consolidated text as unverified. MiFID II Art. 93 sets application from 3 January 2017; MAR Art. 39(2) from 3 July 2016 with listed exceptions; later amendments not verified.
(5) S41 is still dated June 10, 2021, but now includes a section on the June 4, 2026 / October 20, 2027 intraday-margin transition.
(6) Add the RBI LRS FAQ (Id=115, updated as on April 06, 2023; USD 2,50,000 per April-March financial year; margin remittances and forex trading abroad are prohibited items) and eCFR 12 CFR 220.8 (Reg T cash account, 90-day withdrawal of delayed payment).
(7) IBKR: Form 3071 (06/29/2023), still served, describes the legacy PDT block; IBKR's regime under Notice 26-10 is unverified. Form 3203 (10 January 2025) sections 3B, 4, 5B, 16, 30C, 34, 38 and 39 and the IBKR API market-data compliance pages (PRO account, USD 500 minimum, API Acknowledgement, Professional by default, API data is off-platform, one paper account may share a live user's data, no dissemination via TWS API, API User Activity Certification for US futures users) were fetched. Section 5B covers IBKR's own algorithmic order types, not client-built automation. No IBKR statement on non-display fees, long-term storage or cloud-model processing of API data was found.

Applicability summary for a single retail owner using a broker API:
- 15c3-5 binds broker-dealers with market access. It serves only as a design benchmark here.
- FINRA 26-10 governs broker treatment of margin accounts and matters to a cash-only account only through broker policy.
- Reg T cash-account freeriding rules apply through the broker.
- The SEBI/NSE retail algo framework applies to API users. There is no single-user exemption; registration is required above 10 OPS per exchange.
- The RBI LRS/FEMA limits apply once the owner is a person resident in India under FEMA (an adviser must determine this).
- The MiFID II own-account exemption likely covers retail broker API trading unless the setup involves DEA, venue membership, market making, an HFT technique or dealing on own account when executing client orders (broker confirmation needed).
- MAR prohibitions apply to everyone, including actions in third countries concerning in-scope instruments.
- IRS Topic 429 trader status is fact-dependent.

- IBKR: official docs fetched as markdown from www.interactivebrokers.com/docs/tws-api/doc/*.md. Key findings: no historical data for securities that are no longer trading (survivorship bias); historical data may differ by request time (snapshotting required); small-bar pacing rules; request rate = market data lines / 2 per second; the paper simulator fills from top of book; WhatIf returns commission and fees. capabilities.title: Security search and instrument discovery
capabilities.user_workflow: 1) The owner types a partial name, ticker, ISIN or FIGI into the terminal command bar. 2) The system returns a ranked list grouped by instrument. Each instrument expands to its listings, showing venue MIC, currency, ticker, status (active, suspended or delisted) and identifiers. 3) The owner narrows the list with filters (asset class, country, venue, status, include inactive). 4) The owner explicitly selects one listing. The system never auto-selects a tradeable contract from a natural-language name (ch. 3). 5) A resolution card shows identifiers, source lineage and as-of time, with actions to add to a watchlist, open a chart or open the corporate-action history.

reference_scope.module_or_feature: Command-line keyword security lookup refined with yellow market-sector keys
reference_scope.supporting_quote: If you don't know the ticker, in the command line, start typing a keyword or the company name. A list of matches appears. You can refine this list by pressing a yellow market key.

reference_scope.module_or_feature: rd.discovery.search with views (e.g. Views.EQUITY_QUOTES), filter, select, order_by, top
reference_scope.supporting_quote: The search() function identifies a matching set of documents which satisfy the caller's criteria, sorts it, and selects a subset of the matches to return as the result.

reference_scope.product: S&P Capital IQ (guide titled 'S&P Capital IQ Platform User Guide'; not stated to be Capital IQ Pro)
reference_scope.supporting_quote: To search for public, private companies, indices, people, type the name in the search box
Up to 16 matching results are returned. There must be an interval of at least 1 second between successive calls to reqMatchingSymbols.
Rate-limit table for /v3/search and /v3/filter: 5 per minute without an API key, 20 per minute with one; Max Results Per Page 100; Max Number of Pages 150; Max Terms In Query 12.

capabilities.inputs: Free-text query (name fragment, ticker, ISIN, CUSIP only if licensed, FIGI, IBKR conid, NSE symbol); optional filters: asset class, country, MIC, currency, status, as-of date.
capabilities.outputs: Ranked candidate list. Each candidate has: internal instrument_id, listing_id, display ticker, MIC, currency, ISIN, FIGI fields (figi, compositeFIGI, shareClassFIGI as returned by OpenFIGI), status, listing date, delisting date if any, source name, retrieved_at, and a match-reason label (exact id, exact ticker, name token, fuzzy).
capabilities.behavior: The search runs on a local index built from the point-in-time instrument master (record point-in-time-instrument-master). An exact-identifier fast path validates ISIN, SEDOL and CUSIP check digits and the FIGI format before lookup. Ranking order: (a) exact identifier match; (b) exact ticker on the primary listing in the user's preferred market; (c) exact ticker on other listings; (d) name token prefix; (e) fuzzy match. Delisted or inactive listings are hidden unless the include-inactive filter is set, and are badged when shown. When the local index has no hit, the system optionally falls back to OpenFIGI /v3/search and IBKR reqMatchingSymbols through a token-bucket limiter that follows the published limits. External hits are shown as 'unmapped external candidates' until they pass mapping and verification. No candidate becomes tradeable without explicit owner selection and broker contract verification (record broker-contract-resolution).

analytics_definitions: Recall@k = |{q in Q : correct listing in top k results}| / |Q| (unitless, over the labelled query set Q)
MRR = (1/|Q|) * sum over q of 1/rank_q, with 1/rank_q = 0 when the correct listing is absent (unitless)
Search latency = time from keystroke debounce end to rendered result list, reported as p50/p95 in milliseconds

ISIN check (standard algorithm stated without a fetched source; verify against ISO 6166 before release): 12 characters = 2-letter country code + 9-character NSIN + 1 check digit. Letters are expanded to digits (A=10..Z=35), then a Luhn mod-10 check is applied. All 2,611 ISINs in NSE EQUITY_L.csv on 2026-10-22 pass this check.

dependencies.backend: Search service over the instrument master. Rate-limited OpenFIGI client. IBKR adapter symbol search.
dependencies.frontend: Command bar with typeahead, filter chips, inactive badge, resolution card with lineage.
dependencies.storage: Local full-text index (e.g. SQLite FTS) rebuilt from master versions. Index manifest with source hashes.
dependencies.integration: OpenFIGI API key (optional), SEC EDGAR fair-access client, IBKR TWS/Gateway session, licensed NSE/BSE master feed when contracted.

capabilities.degraded_behavior: If external sources are unreachable, search uses the last good local index and shows its as-of time. If OpenFIGI returns 429, the client waits for the retry-after header value (OpenFIGI documents this header as sent only with 429) and labels results 'external lookup deferred'. If the IBKR session is down, broker search is hidden. An empty result never falls back to guessing from the name.
acceptance_criteria: On a labelled fixture of at least 200 queries (US, IN, EU; including 20 delisted and 20 cross-listed instruments), exact ISIN queries reach Recall@1 = 100%.
An exact primary-listing ticker query with a country filter (e.g. AAPL, country US) returns the primary listing at rank 1 in at least 99% of the fixture cases.

A query matching several listings with the same short symbol returns all of them, and selection requires an explicit click. No automatic resolution occurs (UI test asserts no listing is selected after the query).
Delisted listings appear only when include-inactive is set, and they carry delisting date and status.
Local search p95 latency is at most 50 ms on an index of 100,000 listings on the reference Mac (proposed project budget).
In a 10-minute fallback soak test, the OpenFIGI client sends at most 5 search/filter requests per minute without a key (20 with a key), and reqMatchingSymbols calls are at least 1 second apart.
Every result row shows its source and retrieved_at. Rows whose source has no recorded rights are excluded (scanner count = 0).
capabilities.verification_procedure: 1) Build a fixture query set with hand-verified answers: names, tickers, ISINs and FIGIs, including delisted and cross-listed cases. 2) Run the search offline with external sources disabled and compute Recall@1, Recall@5 and MRR. 3) Re-run with OpenFIGI mocked to return 429 with a retry-after header and check the wait and the labels. 4) Replay at 10x keystroke rate and measure p95 latency. 5) Scan the index for rows lacking a rights record.

parity_dimensions.latency: Local index target p95 of 50 ms or less (project budget). External fallback is bounded by OpenFIGI and IBKR pacing.
parity_dimensions.usability: Single command bar, keyboard-first, with lineage visible on every result.
parity_dimensions.operational_reliability: Works offline from the last snapshot. Each source degrades independently.

capabilities.title: Identifier cross-reference and FIGI mapping
capabilities.user_workflow: 1) The owner imports or selects instruments by any supported identifier. 2) The system maps each one to FIGI fields and to its internal instrument and listing IDs. 3) The owner reviews a mapping report that flags unmapped, ambiguous and conflicting rows. 4) The owner approves or rejects proposed mappings for conflicts. 5) Approved mappings become versioned child records of the instrument. Research, UI, risk and execution all read the same map (ch. 3).

reference_scope.supporting_quote: A list of contract identifiers that the customer is allowed to view. CUSIP/ISIN/etc.

capabilities.inputs: Identifier type plus value (ISIN, FIGI, TICKER with exchCode or MIC, ID_BB_GLOBAL, broker conid, NSE symbol with series, CUSIP or SEDOL only under licence). Optional currency and MIC hints.
capabilities.outputs: Mapping records: (internal_instrument_id, internal_listing_id, provider, external_id_type, external_id, mapping_version, valid_from, valid_to, source, retrieved_at, evidence_hash, status in {verified, proposed, ambiguous, conflict, unmapped}). Summary report with coverage and conflict counts.
capabilities.behavior: Identifiers are layered: issuer, then security (ISIN; OpenFIGI shareClassFIGI), then listing (ticker plus MIC; OpenFIGI figi and compositeFIGI), then broker contract (record broker-contract-resolution). The layer assignment of OpenFIGI fields is a working assumption: the API page defines only figi, and describes COMPOSITE_ID_BB_GLOBAL as linking FIGIs at trading-venue level within one country and ID_BB_GLOBAL_SHARE_CLASS_LEVEL as assigned to an instrument traded in more than one country. Mapping calls batch jobs to the OpenFIGI limits (10 jobs per request without a key, 100 with one). Every job outcome is stored, including 'No identifier found' results (the page shows this string under 'error' in a sample, while its table describes a 'warning' when no FIGI is found; handle both). A mapping is 'verified' only when at least two independent sources agree, for example OpenFIGI ISIN-to-ticker/exchCode and the IBKR SecIdList ISIN for the chosen conid. A disagreement sets 'conflict' and blocks order routing for that listing until the owner resolves it (ch. 3). Mapping updates create new versions and never rewrite historical executions. Check digits are validated before any external call. RIC values are stored only if an LSEG licence is recorded; the system never generates RICs by string rule.

ISIN: redistribution terms of national numbering agencies unverified. CUSIP and SEDOL: licensed (record identifier-licensing-guard). RIC: LSEG proprietary symbology; rights outside an LSEG licence unverified.

rights.retention: Mapping versions kept indefinitely for replay. Licensed identifiers follow licence retention.
rights.model_processing: FIGI, ticker and ISIN values may be sent to models. CUSIP, SEDOL and RIC values are withheld unless a licence permits it.

analytics_definitions: Mapping coverage = |inputs with exactly one verified listing mapping| / |inputs| (unitless)
Ambiguity rate = |inputs with more than one candidate listing after hints| / |inputs|
Cross-source agreement rate = |listings where OpenFIGI-derived ISIN equals broker SecIdList ISIN| / |listings with both values|

CUSIP check digit (standard algorithm stated without a fetched source; verify against CGS documentation): weighted mod-10 over 8 characters (digits as-is, letters A=10..Z=35, *@# = 36..38), doubling every second position and summing the digits of each product; check = (10 - (sum mod 10)) mod 10

SEDOL check digit (standard algorithm stated without a fetched source; verify against LSEG SEDOL documentation): weights 1,3,1,7,3,9 over 6 characters (letters = 9 + alphabet position); check = (10 - (weighted sum mod 10)) mod 10

capabilities.behavior: The internal immutable instrument_id is never reassigned (ch. 3). Each attribute change (ticker, name, MIC, status, lot, tick schedule) closes the previous version and opens a new one. Valid intervals for the same key may not overlap. Ticker resolution is always (ticker, MIC or country, date) and never ticker alone. Ticker reuse by a different issuer after a delisting resolves to different instrument_ids on either side of the boundary. Free sources are mostly current-only: SEC tickers and the Nasdaq directory carry no history, while SEC formerNames gives name history. So the system takes daily snapshots from go-live and derives changes by diffing. Pre-go-live ticker history requires a licensed source (e.g. Nasdaq Daily List for Nasdaq securities) or owner-entered evidence with citation. The knowledge-time axis ensures a backtest at t uses only reference data recorded before t, plus a configurable publication lag.

capabilities.behavior: Calendars are stored as data (not code), with version, source URL, retrieved_at and approval. Session times are local wall-clock times with a time zone. Instants convert to UTC through IANA tz, and DST gaps and overlaps are handled explicitly. Holidays falling on weekends (NSE lists 15-Feb, 21-Mar, 15-Aug and 08-Nov-2026 on weekends) are recorded but must not alter weekday logic. Per-venue exceptions within an operator follow the operator page (Euronext 2026: Oslo closed Maundy Thursday, Ascension Day and Whit Monday and half day on 1 Apr; Milan and Oslo closed 24 and 31 Dec; Dublin closed on the Irish May bank holiday and on 28 Dec). The FWB calendar (Xetra and Börse Frankfurt) lists 24 and 31 Dec 2026 as non-trading days with settlement open, and Ascension Day, Whit Monday and Corpus Christi 2026 as trading days. The page states that shares and ETPs on Frankfurt and Xetra end at 20:00 CET on such public holidays, while also giving Xetra hours as 9:00 to 17:30 CET; the Xetra close time on those days stays unverified until resolved (open question). A daily cross-check compares the next two days of IBKR TradingHours per instrument with the calendar and raises a discrepancy alert. A discrepancy blocks automatic session start for that venue until the owner resolves it. Calendar horizon is tracked per venue: NYSE through 2028, FWB through 2032 per page, Euronext 2026, NSE current year only. Instants beyond the horizon return 'unknown', never 'open'. NSE Muhurat session timings are not given in the holiday master (session fields are null); they are captured from the exchange circular and are unverified here.

capabilities.behavior: Event lifecycle: announced, then confirmed, then effective; a cancelled event is kept as a cancelled version. Each event carries its knowledge time so backtests do not see announcements before they were public. Adjustment applies to observations strictly before the ex-date. Factor products are computed in exact rational arithmetic and rounded only for display. Free-text exchange subjects (e.g. NSE 'Bonus 1:1', 'Face Value Split (Sub-Division) - From Rs 10/- Per Share To Rs 2/- Per Share') are parsed by typed parsers. The ratio convention for NSE 'Bonus a:b' (assumed a new shares for every b held) is not defined on any fetched page and must be confirmed from an NSE or SEBI source before the parser is enabled. analytics_definitions: Split ratio r = new_shares / old_shares (e.g. 2-for-1: r = 2; 1-for-10 reverse: r = 0.1)
Bonus a:b (assumed a new shares for every b held; convention unverified): r = (a + b) / b; 'Bonus 1:1' gives r = 2
Face-value split FV_old to FV_new: r = FV_old / FV_new
Price adjustment factor for an event with ex-date x: f = 1/r applied to prices at t < x; volume factor = r
Cumulative price factor F(t) = product over events e with ex_e > t of f_e (exact rational); adjusted price P_adj(t) = P_raw(t) × F(t); adjusted volume V_adj(t) = V_raw(t) / F(t)
Expected post-event quantity q' = q × r. Fractional remainder q × r - floor(q × r) is settled per broker (cash in lieu).

capabilities.behavior: Status state machine per listing: active, then flagged (deficient, delinquent or bankrupt), then delisting pending (Form 25 filed), then delisted (filing date + 10 days), then deregistered (+90 days or a shorter period the SEC determines). Terminal pricing after delisting (OTC trading, liquidation value) is not inferred. The post-delisting return is 'missing with reason', never zero (ch. 11 missing-value rule). Held positions in a delisting instrument trigger an owner alert and block new buys.

capabilities.behavior: Status is taken from what the provider reports, never from what was requested: IBKR TWS API EWrapper.marketDataType (1 live, 2 frozen, 3 delayed, 4 delayed frozen) and IBKR Web API field 6509 (first character R, D, Z, Y, N; O = Market Data API Acknowledgement incomplete; second character P = snapshot, p = consolidated). Delayed values carry delay_minutes (IBKR documents 15-20 min) and are never merged into a real-time series or used for signals flagged real-time. sampling_mode records that IBKR Level 1 is aggregated snapshots, not every quote: TWS API documents 250 ms for US stocks; the Web API update interval is unverified and must be recorded as 'unknown' until measured. One-shot snapshots (reqMktData snapshot=true returns data from the past 11 s; a regulatory snapshot costs USD 0.01 per request and is available for common US stocks only) are stored as snapshot records. Web API snapshots require a pre-flight request before data arrives; the first empty response is not a quote. Age = now - event_ts (fallback receipt_ts, flagged). Quotes are classified normal/locked/crossed/one-sided/zero-size and retained, not deleted (book Ch.11 quality gates). IBKR documents that a tickPrice of -1 or 0 followed by a tickSize of 0 means no data is currently available for that field; such fields become null with reason 'no data currently available'. All prices are decimal with explicit scale and currency. The order-ticket path re-validates status = real-time and age <= pre-trade budget on the server, independent of the UI. US, India and Europe listings share the same schema; currency and session calendar come from the listing record.

age_ms = now_utc_ms - event_ts_ms (fallback receipt_ts_ms, flagged 'receipt-time age') [milliseconds]
stale_t = (age_ms > budget_ms[use]) for use in {display, signal, pre_trade} [boolean]
quote_state = crossed if bid > ask; locked if bid = ask; one_sided if exactly one side null; empty if both null

Web API code O: global banner that the API acknowledgement is incomplete.
acceptance_criteria: Every IBKR status code (TWS 1-4; Web API R, D, Z, Y, N, O and flags P, p) maps to exactly one stored status and UI badge; fixture coverage is 100% of these codes.
A quote with status other than real-time cannot enable order submission; a server-side test asserts rejection reason 'quote not real-time'.
With a fake clock, the displayed age refreshes at least once per second and the stale flag flips within 1 s of crossing each configured budget.
A fixture with tickPrice -1 and tickPrice 0, each followed by tickSize 0, is stored as null with reason 'no data currently available', never as a price of -1 or 0.
Crossed and locked quotes are retained, labelled and counted per session; a fixture with 10 such quotes yields 10 stored, labelled rows.

A regulatory snapshot request requires a confirmation that shows USD 0.01 cost and the remaining local allocation; the local cap is enforced before the request is sent (test: request N+1 is refused locally when the cap is N).
An entitlement change from delayed to live (marketDataType 3 then 1) updates the stored status on the next callback without restart and writes one audit-log entry.
capabilities.verification_procedure: 1) Build a deterministic fixture of IBKR callbacks: marketDataType 3 then 1, tickPrice -1/0 with tickSize 0, a crossed quote, a 30 s gap. Replay through adapter, normalizer and UI store with a fake clock; assert statuses, ages, badges and order-ticket gating. 2) In IBKR paper with IB Gateway, request an unsubscribed US symbol after reqMarketDataType(3) and confirm callback type 3 and the DELAYED badge; repeat for a subscribed symbol and confirm type 1. 3) For 20 symbols compare displayed bid/ask/last against the TWS watchlist at the same instant; differences must be within one sampling interval (250 ms for US stocks). 4) Cut the gateway network and confirm the disconnected state within the configured timeout. 5) Measure the Web API snapshot update interval empirically and record it in the source registry.

capabilities.behavior: Live prints come from IBKR reqTickByTickData ('Last' or 'AllLast'; AllLast includes combos, derivatives and average-price trades not in Last) or the Alpaca trades channel (subscription to trade corrections and cancel/errors is automatic). IBKR limits: tick-by-tick subscriptions <= 5% of market data lines (5 at the default 100 lines); no more than one request for the same instrument within 15 s; not available for options or combos; indices only for CME indexes. Historical prints use reqHistoricalTicks (Trades, Bid_Ask, Midpoint; max 1000 per request; last 3 years; data not returned from multiple trading sessions in one request), paged with a pacing-aware scheduler. IBKR halted ticks (zero price, zero size, pastLimit set) map to HALT; a following zero-price, zero-size tick immediately after a halted tick maps to RESUME. Where the source marks aggregation (the TWS window shows '+'), aggregated=true is preserved; the platform does not claim every print where the source aggregates. Corrections and cancels never overwrite: they create a new version with a link to the original (book Ch.11). Condition codes are kept as raw source strings plus a mapped internal category; unmapped codes are flagged, not dropped. VWAP and volume calculations declare which conditions they include.

capabilities.inputs: Instrument ID; interval delta; range or duration; session filter (RTH/all); price basis (trades, midpoint, bid, ask); adjustment mode (raw/split/split+dividend); live flag.
capabilities.outputs: Bar records {instrument_id, interval, start_ts, end_ts, open, high, low, close, volume, vwap, trade_count, basis, session, adjustment_mode, complete, source, construction_version, revision}; live bar updates with complete=false.
capabilities.behavior: Bars are half-open [start, start+delta) aligned to the listing's session calendar and time zone. Two construction paths coexist and are labelled: vendor bars (IBKR reqHistoricalData bar sizes from 1 s to 1 month; keepUpToDate for live, updated approximately every 4-6 s; reqRealTimeBars 5 s only; Kite candles minute, 3/5/10/15/30/60 minute and day; Alpaca bars) and platform bars built from stored eligible trades. A bar is complete only when its interval has ended and the source confirms (vendor) or the trade stream has passed end_ts plus a settle delay (platform). Strategies receive only complete bars (book Ch.05: final high/close cannot be used before completion). Intervals with no eligible trades produce a bar marked no_trades with null OHLC rather than zero values. IBKR states historical data is filtered for trade types that occur away from the NBBO (combo legs, block trades, derivative trades), so IBKR historical volume is generally lower than real-time volume; the platform stores the source and does not reconcile them by force. IBKR bars of 30 s or less older than six months are unavailable; a request outside limits returns a coverage gap, not an empty success. A request scheduler enforces IBKR's small-bar pacing rules: no identical request within 15 s, fewer than six requests for the same contract/exchange/tick type within 2 s, at most 60 requests in any 10 minutes, BID_ASK counted twice; Web API history endpoint 10 requests/s and 50/min.

capabilities.inputs: Instrument ID; date range; frequency (day/week/month); adjustment mode; corporate-action event table (splits, cash and stock dividends, symbol changes); dataset version.

capabilities.behavior: The platform stores unadjusted (raw) daily OHLCV and computes adjustments itself from a versioned corporate-action table, because vendor series mix conventions (IBKR TRADES is split-adjusted only; ADJUSTED_LAST is split+dividend adjusted; the streaming previous close for US equities is corporate-action adjusted). Vendor-adjusted series may be stored for comparison but are labelled with their vendor convention. Accounting and order reconstruction use raw prices; research uses the mode its question requires (book Ch.02, Ch.05). Each adjustment factor is traceable to an event record with source and announcement/ex dates. A new corporate-action correction creates a new factor version; prior dataset versions remain reproducible. Securities that stop trading are kept with their final history where obtained; IBKR does not provide data for securities no longer trading, so the platform reports a survivorship coverage gap rather than silently excluding them. Symbol changes map to the same internal instrument ID.

analytics_definitions: Split factor for event with ratio a:b (a new shares per b old) effective at ex-date e: prices before e multiplied by b/a; volumes multiplied by a/b

Cash dividend factor at ex-date e: F_e = 1 - D_e / C_{e-1}, where D_e is dividend per share and C_{e-1} the raw close on the prior trading day [dimensionless]; prices before e multiplied by the product of later F
Cumulative adjustment A_t = product of all factors for events with ex-date > t; adjusted_price_t = raw_price_t x A_t
Total return index TR_t = TR_{t-1} x (C_t + D_t) / C_{t-1} using raw closes and dividends with ex-date t
Simple return r_t = P_t / P_{t-1} - 1; log return g_t = log(P_t / P_{t-1}) (book Ch.05)

capabilities.behavior: IBKR depth updates arrive as position-indexed insert (0), update (1), delete (2) operations per side; the book model applies them in order and must empty the book on error 317 'Market depth data has been RESET'. Smart depth (isSmartDepth=True, only when the contract exchange is 'SMART') returns aggregated data with the exchange holding the order in marketMaker; direct depth returns the market maker MPID. reqMktDepthExchanges lists venues for which depth is available via API. Depth is not supported for calendar spreads or combos. Kite 'full' mode provides 5 levels for NSE/BSE. BSE India Spot Market Max20 (licensed internationally via Deutsche Börse) provides netted pre-trade information up to depth 20 at specified time intervals, so it must be labelled interval-sampled. Depth is labelled by source semantics (by price, by order, market maker, sampled). Odd lots are excluded by IBKR; this is shown. The book is checked for crossed state after each update; a crossed book is flagged (may be valid transiently per Ch.11) and triggers a resubscribe if persistent. Depth data is not used for strategy decisions in the initial cash-equity policy unless a strategy release explicitly approves it.

analytics_definitions: Top-N imbalance I_N = (sum_{k<=N} B_k - sum_{k<=N} A_k) / (sum_{k<=N} B_k + sum_{k<=N} A_k), undefined when denominator is 0 [dimensionless, -1..1]
Cumulative depth D_side(p) = sum of sizes at levels at or better than price p [shares]
Size-weighted quote proxy w_t = (a_t B_t + b_t A_t) / (A_t + B_t) (book eq. 2.2) [quote currency]
Depth-to-trade ratio = top-N displayed size / median trade size over window [dimensionless]

capabilities.behavior: All studies are computed by the platform (IBKR does not provide studies via API) with deterministic, versioned implementations validated against TA-Lib as a reference oracle. Each study declares input basis (close, typical price, etc.), adjustment mode, warm-up length and missing-data policy; values during warm-up are null and visibly marked. The chart header always shows source, status (real-time/delayed), session filter, adjustment mode and time zone. The live last bar is drawn as incomplete. Comparison series are rebased at the first common timestamp. Rendering may use an open-source library (e.g., Lightweight Charts under Apache-2.0, which requires the NOTICE attribution and a link to tradingview.com on the user-facing page) and must aggregate for display without altering stored data (book Ch.22). Proprietary chart engines and their visual assets (Bloomberg, ChartIQ) are not copied. Drawings are stored as user data with instrument and price/time anchors.

analytics_definitions: SMA_n(t) = (1/n) x sum_{i=0}^{n-1} x_{t-i}; null for t < n-1
EMA_n(t) = alpha x_t + (1-alpha) EMA_n(t-1), alpha = 2/(n+1); seeded with SMA_n at t = n-1 (seed convention declared)
RSI_n (Wilder) = 100 - 100/(1 + RS), RS = smoothed average gain / smoothed average loss over n with Wilder smoothing alpha = 1/n
Bollinger(n,k): middle = SMA_n; upper/lower = SMA_n +/- k x sigma_n, sigma_n the population standard deviation over n bars (convention declared)
MACD(12,26,9) = EMA_12 - EMA_26; signal = EMA_9(MACD); histogram = MACD - signal
ATR_n = Wilder-smoothed true range, TR_t = max(H_t - L_t, |H_t - C_{t-1}|, |L_t - C_{t-1}|) [quote currency]
Rebased comparison R_j(t) = 100 x P_j(t) / P_j(t0) for common start t0 [index points]

capabilities.inputs: List of internal instrument IDs (ordered, with optional separators/groups); column definitions; line budget from entitlement registry; refresh policy per row (stream, poll snapshot, delayed).

capabilities.behavior: A watchlist is owner data stored by internal instrument ID, independent of any broker. Quote columns come from the quote-status record and keep status and age per cell; fundamental columns show value plus as-of (period end and filing date) and never mix periods silently. A line allocator tracks concurrent streaming subscriptions against the IBKR allocation (minimum 100 lines, shared by the TWS watchlist and every API connection); rows beyond the budget are served by snapshot polling at a declared interval or by delayed data, labelled accordingly. Web API calls respect IBKR's 10 requests/s global limit; the TWS API message-rate limit is not documented on the fetched pages and is a configurable parameter until verified. Optional sync writes the list to IBKR (watchlist id must be a number; rows reference conids; blank rows allowed); the platform list remains authoritative. Exports include status and timestamp columns. Column formulas (e.g., % change basis = previous close) are visible.

Receives a triggered alert that records the data value, source, status and timestamp that caused it. 4. Reviews alert history and acknowledges or snoozes.

reference_scope.supporting_quote: Designate what condition type to use. ... Available condition types: * `1` - Price * `3` - Time * `4` - Margin * `5` - Trade * `6` - Volume
Alerts allow users to set up notifications to pop-up in their Trader Workstation, Interactive Brokers app, or via email in the event of a particular event
Bloomberg Launchpad delivers dynamic multi-asset class security monitors, powerful alerting tools, sophisticated charting and news that moves markets.

Real-Time updates: Receive instant notification of new content. ... Portfolios: Receive alerts on news, events, new financial data, research reports and filings and other documents related to companies in your portfolio(s).

capabilities.inputs: Alert definition {instrument or list, condition type, operator, threshold, combination logic (AND/OR), repeatable flag, outside-RTH flag, time in force and expiry, channels}; quote/trade/bar streams; licensed news headline stream; SEC submissions feed.
capabilities.outputs: Alert trigger records {alert_id, condition, observed value, threshold, data source, data status, event_ts, evaluation_ts, delivery results}; alert history; optional mirror alert at IBKR.
capabilities.behavior: The platform runs its own alert engine on the data it is entitled to, mirroring IBKR's alert model (condition types price, time, margin, trade, volume; logicBind AND/OR; alertRepeatable; outsideRth; tif GTC/GTD with expireTime) and extending it to study values, relative volume, news and filings. Each trigger stores the observed value and the quote status; alerts evaluated on delayed data are labelled 'triggered on delayed data' and can be disallowed per alert. Crossing alerts use previous and current values to avoid repeat triggers while the value stays beyond the level; hysteresis is configurable. News alerts use only licensed API news (IBKR enables BRFG, BRFUPDN and DJNL by default; BRF, BZ and FLY require API-specific subscriptions); headlines are untrusted text (book Ch.11) and an alert never executes an order. Filing alerts use the SEC EDGAR submissions API, which SEC states is updated with a typical processing delay of less than a second. Optionally the engine mirrors simple price alerts to IBKR so they fire when the platform is offline, recorded as a separate alert with broker evaluation semantics. Alerts persist across restarts; missed evaluation windows (platform down) are reported, not back-filled as triggers.

capabilities.title: Equity screening with point-in-time criteria, reproducible as-of runs and real-time scans
capabilities.user_workflow: 1. Owner builds a screen: universe (exchange/country/listing type), criteria on price, liquidity, fundamentals and ratios, and sort. 2. Runs it 'as of now' or 'as of' a past date; the as-of run uses only data available at that date. 3. Inspects each result's inputs (values, units, period, filing date, source). 4. Saves the screen, sends results to a watchlist, or schedules it; runs a historical sequence of as-of screens for a simple backtest. 5. Separately runs intraday scans (top % gainers, volume spikes) on entitled real-time data.

reference_scope.supporting_quote: Bloomberg has developed a backtesting tool that can analyze the performance of a portfolio produced by an EQS screen. The test updates the portfolio at user-defined historical intervals.
The override field PiTDate is equivalent to the flag AsOf in the Bloomberg Excel Add-In.

reference_scope.module_or_feature: Screener object (LSEG Data Library for Python)
reference_scope.supporting_quote: Use the Screener object in the LSEG Data Library for Python to programmatically filter large universes of instruments (e.g., equities) by criteria such as fundamentals, prices, and classifications
we integrated AI-Assisted Screener capabilities into the Companies dataset. This enhancement allows users to screen for companies more efficiently by using natural language
Scans are limited to a maximum result of 50 results per scan code, and only 10 API scans can be active at a time.

capabilities.inputs: Universe definition with as-of date tau; criteria expressions over typed fields (price, volume, market cap, ratios, growth); availability lags; data versions; optional natural-language request translated to criteria (shown for confirmation).
capabilities.outputs: Result set with per-row values, units, currency, period end, filing date, source and missing-data reasons; screen definition and run manifest (tau, dataset versions, formula versions); optional backtest series of as-of results.
capabilities.behavior: Every field used by a screen has an availability time. For US fundamentals the platform reconstructs point-in-time values from SEC XBRL companyfacts/companyconcept, where each fact carries end date, fiscal year/period, form, accession number and filed date; a fact is usable at tau only if filed + availability lag <= tau. SEC states the frames API aggregates one fact for each reporting entity that is last filed and most closely fits the requested calendar period; it is therefore not point-in-time and must not be used for historical as-of screens. Restated values supersede earlier ones only from their own filing date. Price and market-cap criteria use the raw close at or before tau and shares outstanding available at tau. The universe at tau includes securities that later delisted when data exists; otherwise the run reports a survivorship coverage gap with counts. Ratios with negative or zero denominators are flagged 'NM' and excluded from ranking unless the owner opts in (book Ch.11). Missing values remain missing with a reason (book Ch.11 feature contract). Natural-language screening (as in S&P AI-Assisted Screener, which converts natural language into screening criteria) may be offered by translating text into explicit criteria that the owner sees and confirms; the model never runs a screen on hidden criteria. Real-time scans (top movers, volume spikes) are a separate mode computed from entitled quotes; IBKR's API scanner may be used as a source (50 results per scan code, 10 active API scans, periodic updates while subscribed, results contain no market data fields, filters generally require market data subscriptions). India and Europe fundamentals require a separate licensed source.
