analytics_definitions: Availability rule: fact f usable at tau iff filed_date(f) + lag_days <= date(tau); lag_days >= 1 by default because 'filed' is date-only [days]
TTM_x(tau) = sum of the latest four discrete quarterly values of x available at tau; if Q4 is not reported discretely, Q4 = FY - (Q1+Q2+Q3) using values available at tau (derivation flagged)
Market cap(tau) = raw close(tau) x shares outstanding(latest value available at tau) [currency]
P/E(tau) = market cap(tau) / TTM net income(tau); 'NM' if TTM net income <= 0
EV(tau) = market cap + total debt + preferred + minority interest - cash and equivalents, each as available at tau (documented treatment, book Ch.11) [currency]
Survivorship coverage = securities with data at tau / securities listed at tau in the universe definition [percent]

capabilities.title: Market-data entitlement, professional status, display vs non-display use and fee registry
capabilities.user_workflow: 1. Owner records, per data source and exchange, the subscription, professional/non-professional status, permitted uses (display, non-display/automated, derived data, storage, model processing), monthly cost and evidence links. 2. Before a feature consumes a source, the platform checks the registry and blocks unlicensed uses. 3. Owner reviews a monthly cost and usage report and upcoming policy changes (e.g., US CT Plan from 2027-04-01).

reference_scope.supporting_quote: By default, all users are classified as Professional Market Data users. Individuals who believe they should be classified as Non-Professional market data users should update their market data subscriber status within the client portal.
IBKR allows for free on-platform data; however, data on the API is considered off-platform. Exchanges maintain different licensing requirements and agreements for off-platform market data viewing.
The Market Data API Acknowledgement is required for all users who intend to request market data through any API platform.

reference_scope.module_or_feature: Entitlements Management and Reporting System (EMRS); non-display applications
reference_scope.supporting_quote: EMRS makes it convenient to report data usage to exchanges, as well as allocate costs to actual users.

capabilities.inputs: Source registry entries (book Ch.11): provider, dataset, exchange/tape, subscription ID, subscriber status, permitted uses, retention, redistribution, model-processing permission, cost, evidence URL and verification date; consumer declarations (each feature/strategy declares its use type).
capabilities.outputs: Entitlement decisions (allow/deny with reason) per consumer and source; monthly cost/usage report; policy-change calendar; audit log.
capabilities.behavior: Each consumer declares a use class: display (terminal), non-display (automated strategy, alerts, screening, feature computation), derived-data publication, storage for replay, or model processing. The registry maps sources to permitted classes and the platform enforces at subscription time. Defaults are deny. Facts recorded from fetched sources: IBKR classifies users as Professional by default; API data is off-platform and some free bundles provide data only in TWS; API market data requires an opened account (demo accounts cannot subscribe), an IBKR PRO account, USD 500 in the account in addition to the cost of all subscriptions, subscriptions made in Client Portal and the Market Data API Acknowledgement. US legacy CTA schedule: professional display Network A USD 45/27/23/19 per device per month by tier, Network B USD 23; non-professional USD 1.00 per network per month; non-display use fees Network A USD 2,000 (last sale) and USD 2,000 (quotes), Network B USD 1,000 each. CTA defines non-display use as accessing, processing or consuming data for a purpose other than display or further redistribution, and states it does not apply to the creation and use of derived data. US CT Plan from the Operative Date (planned 2027-04-01): professional Tape A flat USD 26, Tape B USD 23, Tape C USD 24 per month; non-professional sliding scale from USD 0.90 to USD 0.25 per individual by band; usage-based classification; uniform 15-minute delayed data license. NSE's non-display policy covers automated trading decision-making and derived data for internal analysis, and requires an agreement/undertaking with NSE Data & Analytics and payment of fees; its definition of Subscriber includes clients who receive market data from NSE data vendors. Whether these direct-licensee fees apply to an individual receiving data through IBKR or another broker is unresolved.

capabilities.behavior: The India adapter maps Kite binary packets (ltp 8 bytes, quote 44 bytes, full 184 bytes including market depth) into the same normalized quote and depth schema as US sources, tagging venue NSE or BSE. Subscriptions are capped at 3000 instruments per connection and 3 connections per API key. REST quote snapshots are limited to 500 instruments (/quote) and 1000 (/quote/ohlc, /quote/ltp) per call. The instrument master dump is generated once every day and its last_price is not real time; storage keys use exchange + tradingsymbol, never the numeric token, because tokens may be reused. Historical candles (minute, 3/5/10/15/30/60 minute, day; continuous and OI options) feed the bar store with source labels. NSE and BSE are kept as distinct listings; no consolidated quote is implied. NSE's non-display policy explicitly covers automated trading decision-making and derived data for internal analysis, so strategy and screening consumers of NSE data are blocked in the registry until coverage is confirmed. capabilities.behavior: European data is handled per venue with the venue's currency and calendar. A pan-European licensed feed (e.g., Cboe Europe: one license covering more than 6,200 securities from the major European markets; no end user fees for retail/non-professionals as stated) can supply real-time quotes for many listings; national exchange data (e.g., Euronext) is subject to that exchange's data agreements and prices. Delayed-data delays differ by exchange and are recorded per venue rather than assumed to be 15 minutes. Trade flags (MiFID II) are kept raw plus mapped. The EU consolidated tape for shares and ETFs (EuroCTP) is treated as a separate source: trade press reports ESMA authorisation with EuroCTP given until 30 September 2026 to complete operational arrangements and free access for retail investors; a distributor announced a go-live date of 14 September 2026; one regional news article dated 2026-09-29 reports it went live on 14 September; TheTRADE reports the tape computes an EBBO from venue and APA data. Operating status has not been confirmed from ESMA or EuroCTP, so the platform must not display a tape-labelled price until a licensed feed is connected and its status is confirmed in the registry. Until then the venue panel and a labelled partial derived best are the only cross-venue views.

capabilities.behavior: Maintain bitemporal identifier_map rows (issuer_id, id_type, id_value, valid_from, valid_to, source, retrieved_at). Seed US issuers from the SEC submissions API / nightly submissions.zip (fields include tickers, exchanges, lei, sic, fiscalYearEnd and formerNames; formerNames carry from/to dates, tickers and exchanges do not on the fetched sample). capabilities.user_workflow: 1. Owner adds issuers to a research watchlist. 2. The system backfills each issuer's filing index and downloads primary documents, exhibits and XBRL for selected forms (10-K, 10-Q, 8-K, 20-F, 40-F, 6-K, DEF 14A, Forms 3/4/5, 13F-HR, Schedules 13D/13G). 3. During EDGAR hours, new filings appear on the instrument's Filings tab with acceptance time, form and 8-K item numbers; Item 2.02 (results) and Item 4.02 (non-reliance on prior statements) raise alerts. 4. Owner runs phrase, boolean and proximity searches over stored filings with form and date filters and opens the document at the hit. 5. For corpus-wide search of all EDGAR filings since 2001 the system opens SEC full-text search with the query pre-filled.

capabilities.behavior: Poll the submissions JSON for watched CIKs on a budgeted schedule (hard cap below the SEC limit of 10 requests/second; default 5 requests/second shared by all SEC jobs) and reconcile nightly against EDGAR daily/full index files (company, form, master, XBRL). Store raw documents unchanged with hashes; parse 8-K item numbers; link amendments (/A) to originals by file number and report period; deduplicate by accession number. Acceptance times are normalised to true UTC from the EDGAR 'Accepted' Eastern time (see the point-in-time record: the submissions JSON 'Z' value did not equal true UTC on three fetched samples). Build a local full-text index over stored documents supporting the SEC FTS query grammar subset (phrases, OR, NOT/-, NEAR(n) with default 10 words, trailing *). Corpus-wide search uses a deep link to SEC full-text search because the fetched FAQ documents no API. Submissions that begin after 5:30 p.m. ET (10:00 p.m. for Forms 3, 4, 5) may be disseminated the next business day; the UI shows acceptance time and dissemination date separately. Filing text is untrusted data: embedded instructions never change tool permissions.

Request budget: sum over SEC jobs of requests per second <= configured cap < 10.
Proximity match NEAR(n): terms within n words (SEC default 10).

Amended filings link to their originals for 20 test pairs.

analytics_definitions: Duration class: ANNUAL if 335 <= days(end - start) <= 395; QUARTER if 61 <= days <= 121 (SEC frames tolerance).

Cash-flow tie-out residual = (CFO + CFI + CFF + FX effect) - change in cash (and restricted cash where tagged).

capabilities.behavior: Implement our own documented, versioned mapping from us-gaap and ifrs-full concepts to a canonical item set (vendor standardization rules are proprietary and are not copied). A canonical value always lists contributing facts and the rule; if a rule cannot apply, the value is null with reason UNMAPPED, never zero. TTM uses only discrete quarters available at the as-of time. Calendarization is optional and labelled as an approximation. Currency conversion uses period-end rates for balance-sheet items and period-average rates for flow items by default (policy configurable and displayed), with the FX source and date stored. Fiscal-year changes produce a flagged transition period excluded from TTM and growth unless the owner overrides. Units (USD, shares, USD-per-shares, pure) follow XBRL units; per-share values are never summed.

analytics_definitions: TTM_t(item) = sum of the 4 most recent discrete quarterly values with knowledge_time <= t; null if any quarter missing.
Alternative TTM = FY_last + YTD_current - YTD_prior_same_length (used only when discrete quarters unavailable; flagged).
Calendarized flow value for calendar year Y = sum over fiscal periods p of value_p x overlap_days(p, Y) / days(p) (linear-accrual approximation; flagged).
FX conversion: value_target = value_local x rate(local->target, date), date = period end for instants, average over the period for durations.
YoY growth = value_t / value_{t-4 quarters} - 1; undefined (NM) if prior <= 0.

capabilities.behavior: Store every fact occurrence per filing append-only (no overwrite). Knowledge time of a fact = acceptance time of the filing that carried it, converted to true UTC from the EDGAR 'Accepted' Eastern timestamp with America/New_York rules (companyfacts 'filed' is a date without time). The submissions JSON acceptanceDateTime carries a 'Z' suffix but did not equal true UTC on three fetched samples: Apple 10-K 0001193125-09-214859 shows 'Accepted 2009-10-27 16:18:29' on the EDGAR index vs JSON 2009-10-28T00:18:29.000Z; Apple 10-Q 0001193125-10-012085 shows 'Accepted 2010-01-25 16:23:57' vs JSON 2010-01-26T02:23:57.000Z; Form 4 0001140361-26-040127 shows 'Accepted 2026-10-19 18:32:55' vs JSON 2026-10-20T02:32:55.000Z. On these samples the JSON value lags true UTC by the Eastern UTC offset (4 h in EDT, 5 h in EST), so it is stored only as a raw field and is not used as knowledge time until the rule is validated on a larger sample. A later filing reporting the same (concept, period, unit, dimensions) with a different value creates a new version flagged RESTATED; same value creates a RE-REPORTED link. 8-K Item 4.02 filings flag affected periods as NON_RELIANCE until a restated filing arrives. The SEC frames API is not used for backtests because it selects the last filed fact. Survivorship: deregistered and acquired filers remain queryable. Backtest jobs pass decision timestamps; any feature with knowledge_time > decision_time aborts the run.

analytics_definitions: MarketCap = sum over share classes (price_class x shares_outstanding_class), currency of listing.
EV_standard = MarketCap + total debt + preferred equity + noncontrolling interest - cash and equivalents - short-term investments (policy-documented).
EV_ex_leases = EV_standard - operating lease liabilities (if leases included in debt).
EV_pension_ex_equity_method = EV_standard + net unfunded pension liability - equity-method investments.
P/E = price / diluted EPS (TTM); NM if EPS <= 0.
EV/EBITDA = EV / EBITDA (TTM); NM if EBITDA <= 0. EBITDA = operating income + D&A (documented).
FCF = cash from operations - capital expenditures; FCF yield = FCF(TTM) / MarketCap.
ROIC = EBIT x (1 - tax rate) / average(invested capital), invested capital = total debt + equity - cash (documented variant).
Net debt / EBITDA = (total debt - cash) / EBITDA(TTM).

analytics_definitions: Consensus mean_t = (1/n) x sum of active estimates e_i at time t (if computed from broker-level data); else vendor-provided consensus at t.
Dispersion_t = standard deviation of active estimates / |mean_t|; undefined if mean_t = 0.
Revision breadth over window w = (count up - count down) / count of estimates revised in w.
Consensus change over w = mean_t / mean_{t-w} - 1.

Surprise = (actual - consensus_pre) / scale, scale = predeclared positive denominator (e.g., std. dev. of past surprises); consensus_pre = last snapshot with time < announcement time (book chapter 17).

capabilities.title: DCF and WACC valuation with sensitivity surface and valuation range summary
capabilities.user_workflow: 1. Owner opens Valuation for a non-financial issuer. 2. The DCF template pre-fills historical FCFF components from standardized fundamentals and lets the owner enter forecast assumptions (growth, margins, capex, working capital, tax). 3. WACC inputs are pre-filled with sourced values: risk-free rate from the official curve for the currency, beta (computed or entered), equity risk premium (owner-chosen source), cost of debt and weights; every input shows its source and date. 4. Owner views EV, equity bridge, per-share value and a WACC x terminal-growth sensitivity grid. 5. A range summary (football field) shows DCF range, trading-comps range and 52-week price range side by side. 6. Owner saves the model version and exports it with formulas.

reference_scope.supporting_quote: The Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) methodology is available only for non-banking companies; it is not supported for Banking, Insurance, or REIT sectors.

Calculate the Discounted Cash Flows (DCF) of a company, including WACC and exit multiple sensitivity outputs. It also includes customizable selections for the risk-free rate of return & sensitivity analysis.
Delivered a new football field valuation framework directly in Capital IQ Pro based on trading comps and precedent transactions to streamline valuation analysis workflows.
BETA - beta ... WACC - weighted average cost of capital

capabilities.inputs: Standardized historical financials; owner forecast assumptions; risk-free curve (US Treasury par curve, ECB euro area curve, India source TBD); beta from price history (market-data area) or owner input; ERP and country risk premium (owner-selected source, e.g., Damodaran); cost of debt; tax rate; diluted share count; EV-to-equity bridge items; comps ranges.
capabilities.outputs: Versioned model {assumptions with sources, FCFF projections, TV, EV, equity bridge, per-share value}, sensitivity grid, scenario table, football-field chart data, XLSX export with live formulas.
capabilities.behavior: Implements equation 17.1 of the book. Validation rejects WACC <= g and currency-inconsistent inputs (e.g., USD risk-free with INR cash flows) unless the owner records an explicit override. Banks, insurers and REITs are blocked from the FCFF template by default with a reason (financials need different structures). All inputs carry source, date and unit; the risk-free rate is read from the official curve at the chosen tenor and date. FRED is not used as a stored input source because its terms prohibit storing, caching or archiving FRED content and its use in developing or training machine learning or AI systems. Sensitivity grids and scenarios are computed deterministically. AI agents may propose assumptions only with attached evidence; numbers in the model come from typed inputs, not prose.

analytics_definitions: EV = sum_{t=1..T} FCFF_t / (1 + WACC)^t + TV_T / (1 + WACC)^T; TV_T = FCFF_{T+1} / (WACC - g), requires WACC > g (book eq. 17.1).
Exit-multiple TV alternative: TV_T = multiple x EBITDA_T.
WACC = w_e x k_e + w_d x k_d x (1 - tau); w_e, w_d market-value weights.
k_e = r_f + beta x ERP (+ CRP if used); CAPM is a modeling convention.
FCFF = EBIT x (1 - tau) + D&A - capex - change in net working capital.
Equity value = EV - net debt - preferred - noncontrolling interest + non-operating assets (documented bridge); per-share = equity value / diluted shares.
Sensitivity grid: value(WACC_i, g_j) for WACC_i = WACC0 + {-2,-1,0,+1,+2} x step_w and g_j = g0 + {-2,-1,0,+1,+2} x step_g, cells with WACC_i <= g_j marked invalid.

capabilities.title: Rights registry and cloud-model processing gate for news, transcripts and documents
capabilities.user_workflow: 1) Owner opens Sources > Rights and creates one entry per provider/dataset (SEC EDGAR, each IBKR API news provider, PR Newswire RSS, NSE feeds, FCA NSM, transcript vendor). Each entry records the terms URL, contract reference and retrieval date. 2) Owner sets tri-state flags (allow/deny/unknown): display, store_raw, retention_days, derive_facts, derive_embeddings, export, redistribute, local_model, cloud_model, allowed_cloud_providers. 3) Ingestion refuses any source whose entry is missing or unresolved. 4) When an extraction or summary job requests a cloud model call, the gate checks the rights tags of every input artifact against the job's provider and records allow or deny with a reason. 5) Owner reviews the denial log and the rights badge on each document. Flag changes are signed policy changes and apply only to future jobs.

capabilities.inputs: Terms evidence entered by the owner for each source; IBKR entitlement list (reqNewsProviders); model-provider registry entries (training, retention, region); job descriptors with input artifact hashes and target provider.
capabilities.outputs: Versioned rights entries; per-artifact rights tags carried through lineage; an allow/deny record for every cloud call and export; retention-deletion manifests.
capabilities.behavior: The gate denies by default: an unknown flag evaluates to deny. Every raw artifact (headline, article body, filing document, transcript, audio, announcement PDF) carries source_id, rights_version and acquisition timestamp. A derived artifact (fact, summary, embedding, sentiment score, search-index posting) inherits the most restrictive tags of all its inputs and records lineage edges. A cloud submission is allowed only when all four conditions hold. (1) Every input source permits cloud_model for that operation. (2) The model-provider entry records terms the owner accepted. Examples: OpenAI states API data is not used for training by default and abuse-monitoring logs are kept up to 30 days; Anthropic's Commercial Terms say Anthropic may not train models on Customer Content and the customer represents and warrants that it has all rights and permissions required to submit Inputs. (3) The job role is on the allow-list. (4) Redaction and size checks pass. At expiry, the retention scheduler deletes raw text from the DB, object store, search index and embedding store, and keeps hashes and manifests where permitted. Exports (CSV, clipboard, reports) check export/redistribute. SEC.gov content is tagged public because the SEC states that site information is public information and may be copied or further distributed, and asks for citation. Rights versions are immutable, so past decisions remain auditable.

capabilities.inputs: EDGAR Latest Filings Atom feed (type filter); data.sec.gov submissions JSON per CIK; filing index pages and documents; EDGAR daily index and nightly bulk ZIP for reconciliation and backfill; instrument master for CIK mapping.
capabilities.outputs: Filing records {accession, CIK, form, items[], acceptanceDateTime, first_observed_utc, availability_time, documents[] with SHA-256}, amendment links, gap reports, typed event candidates.
capabilities.behavior:
The service polls the Atom feed with a declared User-Agent. One global token bucket covers all EDGAR consumers and is capped at <= 10 requests/second (configurable lower). For each new accession:
- Fetch the CIK submissions JSON and confirm form, items (e.g. '2.02,2.05' in a fetched sample) and acceptanceDateTime.
- Fetch the index, primary document and exhibits.
- Store raw bytes, URL, HTTP date, receipt timestamp and hash.
Items are mapped to the Form 8-K taxonomy (Sections 1-9). An 8-K/A is linked to its original where that can be determined; otherwise it is flagged 'unlinked amendment'. For research, availability time is the first observed public time, not acceptanceDateTime. The SEC states that some submissions begun after 5:30 p.m. ET (10:00 p.m. for Forms 3, 4, 5) are disseminated the next business day. At end of day the stream is reconciled against the daily index and gaps are re-fetched. The nightly bulk ZIP, republished at approximately 3:00 a.m. ET, is used for backfill. When the submissions 'recent' array is truncated, older filings are read from the additional JSON files listed in 'files'. HTML is rendered sanitized, without scripts.

capabilities.behavior: Each market adapter writes the same schema. In the NSE Online announcements capture (researcher's fetch, 2026-10-22), item pubDate values carry no timezone offset, e.g. '22-Oct-2026 17:42:46'. The channel lastBuildDate uses +0530, so the adapter treats pubDate as IST and converts it to UTC; this is an inference, checked by a fixture test. The same capture declares ttl 5 and carries subjects such as 'Outcome of Board Meeting' and 'Analysts/Institutional Investor Meet/Con. Call Updates', plus items describing 'Transcripts - earnings or quarterly calls'. NSE terms of use prohibit 'systematic or automated data collection activities (including scraping, data mining, data extraction and data harvesting)'. They also prohibit copying or storing content without prior written permission. Automated polling therefore ships disabled. Until the owner obtains written permission or a licensed product, the adapter supports manual import only. The FCA NSM is free to view, download and export to CSV but states it is not a real-time provision of information, so it is used for completeness and backfill, not latency. EU single access (ESAP) and national storage mechanisms were not verified, so the EU adapter shows 'unavailable'. BSE pages could not be fetched, so the BSE adapter is 'unverified'.

capabilities.inputs: An IBKR TWS/Gateway session with API news entitlements (reqNewsProviders), BroadTape NEWS contracts, per-contract generic tick 292, reqHistoricalNews and reqNewsArticle; a direct vendor REST API (e.g. Benzinga News API with token and updatedSince delta); public RSS (SEC press releases; PR Newswire headlines, summaries and links) under their terms.

capabilities.behavior: The adapter discovers entitlements with reqNewsProviders. It subscribes to BroadTape contracts (e.g. symbol 'BZ:BZ_ALL', secType 'NEWS', exchange 'BZ') and to per-instrument news through generic tick 292 (e.g. 'mdoff,292:BZ'). A missing API news subscription returns an 'invalid tick type' error, which the adapter surfaces as an entitlement state. Bodies are fetched with reqNewsArticle by articleId only when rights allow storage. History is backfilled with reqHistoricalNews, with provider codes joined by '+' (e.g. 'BZ+FLY'). Direct vendor adapters use delta polling; Benzinga docs recommend the updatedSince parameter for the News API to ensure minimal latency. Revisions create new versions linked by provider_story_id. Receipt timestamps come from an NTP-disciplined clock, and provider timestamps are never presented as receipt times. Gap detection compares live capture with a historical re-query for each provider-day. Pacing follows IBKR limits (Ch 12).

capabilities.title: Syndication deduplication, story clustering and revision tracking
capabilities.user_workflow: Owner sees one cluster per underlying story, with the earliest licensed timestamp, copy count and providers. Expanding a cluster shows each copy and the revision diffs. Duplicates do not fire duplicate alerts and are not double-counted in sentiment or event features.

reference_scope.supporting_quote: This covers almost 10,000+ news sources in-product and available via API.

reference_scope.product: S&P Capital IQ (Key Developments dataset; Capital IQ Pro not named on page)
reference_scope.module_or_feature: Key Developments: news sources consolidated into structured events
reference_scope.supporting_quote: Key Developments delivers over 2,000 structured events daily from more than 20,000 news sources.

capabilities.inputs: Normalized news, press-release RSS items, SEC 8-K exhibits (EX-99.1) and exchange announcements, each with timestamps and rights tags.
capabilities.outputs: Cluster records {cluster_id, member ids, earliest_licensed_timestamp, canonical member, providers[], revision chain, correction flag}; merge log.
capabilities.behavior: Text is normalized: Unicode NFKC, whitespace, and removal of boilerplate such as contact blocks and safe-harbor paragraphs through configurable patterns. Exact duplicates are found by SHA-256 of the normalized text. Near-duplicates are found by MinHash/LSH over word shingles, with a Jaccard threshold validated on labeled data. Canonical-link evidence (the same press-release URL, or the same SEC accession referenced) forces a merge. Revisions with the same provider_story_id form a version chain with diffs. earliest_timestamp = min over members of the earliest licensed timestamp. Cluster ids are stable once assigned: merges are recorded, not renumbered. Hash and shingle artifacts inherit rights tags and are deleted with the raw text when required.

analytics_definitions: jaccard(A,B) = |S(A) INTERSECT S(B)| / |S(A) UNION S(B)| over k-word shingle sets [ratio]; near-duplicate if >= tau, tau chosen on validation data
pair_precision = true duplicate pairs predicted / pairs predicted; pair_recall = true duplicate pairs predicted / true duplicate pairs
cluster_purity = sum over clusters of max label share / total items [ratio]
earliest_timestamp_error_s = t_cluster_earliest - t_true_first [seconds]

dependencies.storage: Cluster tables; shingle/LSH index with rights tags
dependencies.integration: News ingestion, filings stream, alerts (one per cluster), sentiment and event features (counted once)

acceptance_criteria: Exact copies are merged in 100% of fixture cases.
Proposed target: pair F1 >= 0.95 on the labeled set.
In replay tests, alerts fire exactly once per cluster.
Daily sentiment aggregation counts each cluster once (unit test with 3-copy fixture).
Replaying the same input sequence twice yields identical cluster ids.
earliest_timestamp_error_s = 0 on the fixture where the true first copy is known.
Proposed target: p95 incremental clustering time <= 50 ms per item at 1,000,000 indexed items.
capabilities.verification_procedure: Build a fixture with an earnings press release in three copies (SEC 8-K EX-99.1, PR Newswire RSS, an IBKR news provider), a revised headline, and an unrelated story with similar wording. Assert one cluster for the three copies, a version chain for the revision, a separate cluster for the unrelated story, and the correct earliest timestamp. Then compute pair metrics on the labeled set.

capabilities.user_workflow: On every filing, announcement, news item and transcript, the owner sees the tagged issuers and instruments, each with confidence, relevance (primary subject or passing mention) and the evidence span. The owner can correct a wrong tag; the correction is stored as an evaluation label. All document views can be filtered by instrument or watchlist.

reference_scope.module_or_feature: Labs: Kensho NERD named entity recognition (University of Pennsylvania Lippincott Library guide, 2026-03-20)

capabilities.inputs: Document text with structural ids (CIK in EDGAR headers, NSE symbol in exchange feeds, IBKR conId on contract news, ISIN/LEI strings); instrument master; SEC company_tickers.json and submissions metadata; OpenFIGI mappings; GLEIF LEI records and mapped ISINs.
capabilities.outputs: Mention records {doc_id, version_hash, start, end, surface, candidates[], resolved instrument_id or 'unresolved', confidence, relevance_role}; document-level issuer list.
capabilities.behavior:
Stage 1, candidate generation: structured identifiers first, then an alias dictionary from the instrument master (current and former names, tickers with exchange context), then NER. Stage 2: resolution to an internal instrument_id with point-in-time validity (ticker and name changes are dated). Mapping sources:
- SEC company_tickers.json (cik_str, ticker, title). It is a current-only file, so it is snapshotted daily.
- EDGAR submissions, for exchanges and former names.
- OpenFIGI, for ISIN/CUSIP/SEDOL/ticker to FIGI. Without a key: 25 requests/min and 10 jobs/request. With a key: 250/min and 100 jobs. Results are cached, and retry-after is honored on 429.
- GLEIF, for LEI and mapped ISIN/BIC.
Short tickers and tickers that are common words need exchange or company-name corroboration; otherwise the mention stays 'unresolved'. A relevance classifier labels each mention as primary subject or passing mention. Owner corrections become labels and never silently override history.

capabilities.user_workflow: The owner enters either a boolean, phrase, proximity or prefix query or a natural-language question, and can filter by issuer, market, form/category, date range and source type. Results are ranked with highlighted snippets. The owner can open a document at the matched span, save the search as an alert, and export result lists.

capabilities.inputs: All documents admitted by the rights gate (filings, exhibits, exchange announcements, transcripts, news bodies), with entity tags and metadata; query strings; a relevance set labelled by the owner.
capabilities.outputs: Ranked hits {doc_id, version_hash, score, snippet, highlight offsets}; saved searches; CSV export of result metadata where rights allow.
capabilities.behavior:
The first version uses a local inverted index (SQLite FTS5), following Ch 11's rule to add a separate engine only when justified.
- Indexed fields: title, body sections, speaker.
- Tokenizers: unicode61 with the porter wrapper for English, and the trigram tokenizer for substring search over codes and identifiers. Per FTS5 docs, trigram substrings shorter than 3 characters match nothing.
- Ranking: bm25() with per-column weights.
- Spans: snippet() and highlight() supply them, and exact character offsets are computed separately for citations.
- Query syntax: phrases, NEAR(... , N) with N defaulting to 10, prefix '*', AND (implicit), OR, NOT and parentheses.
An optional semantic layer (embeddings) is fused with BM25 by reciprocal rank fusion, only for sources whose rights allow embeddings. Index updates are incremental, and expired or deleted documents are removed in the next index cycle. For US filings, EDGAR full-text search (filings since 2001) serves as a manual cross-check and discovery source, used within fair-access limits.

datasets.name: EDGAR full-text search
datasets.coverage: full text of all EDGAR filings submitted electronically since 2001, including attachments such as exhibits

datasets.name: Local document index (internal)
datasets.coverage: only documents we lawfully hold

rights.licensing: Index entries inherit source rights; EDGAR public.
rights.entitlement: Search results show only documents the owner is entitled to view.
rights.retention: Index postings deleted when source retention expires.
rights.model_processing: Embeddings are built only for sources with derive_embeddings=allow. Cloud embedding calls go through the gate.

analytics_definitions: BM25(D,Q) = sum over q in Q of IDF(q) * f(q,D) * (k1 + 1) / (f(q,D) + k1 * (1 - b + b * |D| / avgdl)). FTS5 hard-codes k1 = 1.2 and b = 0.75 and multiplies the result by -1, so better matches score numerically lower.
RRF(d) = sum over rankers r of 1 / (k + rank_r(d)), k a tuned constant
recall@k = relevant docs in top k / relevant docs; nDCG@10 standard definition over owner-graded relevance
index_lag_s = t_indexed - t_ingested [seconds]

dependencies.backend: Indexer, query parser/validator, ranker, optional embedding service, snippet/offset service
dependencies.frontend: Search bar with syntax help, facet filters, result list with highlighted snippets, open-at-span viewer, saved searches
dependencies.storage: FTS5 tables (initial), embedding store (optional), saved-search table
dependencies.integration: Rights gate, entity tags for filters, alerts (saved searches), grounded Q&A retrieval

capabilities.degraded_behavior: While the index rebuilds, search serves the previous consistent snapshot and shows its timestamp. If the semantic layer is unavailable, search falls back to BM25 only and labels results 'keyword only'.
acceptance_criteria: Syntax tests on a fixture corpus: phrase, NEAR/N, prefix*, OR, NOT and grouping return the hit sets that the FTS5 documentation semantics predict (100% of test cases).
Proposed target: recall@20 >= 0.90 on 100 owner-labeled queries.
Proposed target: p95 query latency <= 300 ms on 1,000,000 documents on the production host.
Proposed target: p95 index_lag_s <= 60.
Expired documents return 0 hits after the next index cycle.
For 30 filing-only queries, top-20 overlap with EDGAR full-text search is reported; it is not required to match.
capabilities.verification_procedure: Build the labeled query set across filings, transcripts and news, and run the evaluation nightly. Benchmark latency on a synthetic 1M-document corpus. Run expiry tests. Compare 30 filing queries with EDGAR FTS manually, within fair-access limits.

capabilities.behavior:
Taxonomy v1 is anchored on primary-source structure.
- Form 8-K items (all items in the Form 8-K General Instructions): 1.01 material definitive agreement, 1.02 termination of a material definitive agreement, 1.03 bankruptcy or receivership, 1.04 mine safety, 1.05 material cybersecurity incidents, 2.01 completed acquisition or disposition, 2.02 results of operations, 2.03 creation of a direct financial obligation, 2.04 triggering events that accelerate or increase an obligation, 2.05 exit or disposal costs, 2.06 material impairments, 3.01 delisting notice or transfer of listing, 3.02 unregistered sales of equity, 3.03 material modification to holders' rights, 4.01 change in certifying accountant, 4.02 non-reliance on previously issued financial statements, 5.01-5.08 governance and management changes, 6.01-6.06 asset-backed securities items, 7.01 Regulation FD disclosure, 8.01 other events, 9.01 financial statements and exhibits.
- NSE subject strings, preserved verbatim and mapped. Examples observed in the captured feed: 'Outcome of Board Meeting', 'Change in Directors/KMP/SMP/Auditor/RTA', 'Bagging/Receiving of orders/contracts', 'Price movement'.
- FCA NSM categories.
Subtypes and quantities are extracted by typed parsers that handle parenthesized negatives, the scale words million/billion and lakh/crore, and currencies. LLM extraction is allowed only under the rights gate, and every extracted value must match a source span. Events merge across 8-K, press release and news through the dedup clusters. Backtests use availability_time only.

capabilities.user_workflow: Owner sees per-document and per-instrument daily sentiment, with a method label (dictionary, local model, cloud model), confidence and contributing sentences. Management prepared remarks are scored separately from Q&A. Comparisons against subsequent returns are for research only.

capabilities.inputs: Deduplicated documents with availability times and entity tags; a sentiment lexicon (licensed or built by the owner); local classifier weights; sentences labelled by the owner; prices for evaluation.
capabilities.outputs: Sentence scores with spans; document scores; daily instrument scores with method/version; evaluation reports (calibration, IC).
capabilities.behavior:
Three versioned scorers:
(a) Dictionary tone, using a finance word list (Loughran-McDonald, which is free for academic research and needs a commercial license otherwise) or a list built by the owner.
(b) A local classifier. FinBERT weights are CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, a non-commercial licence, so they are used only if the owner's use qualifies; otherwise an own model is trained.
(c) Cloud LLM classification with structured output, only where rights allow.
A document with no sentiment words gets a missing state, not zero. Daily instrument scores aggregate the deduplicated clusters available before the cutoff, weighted by confidence. Transcripts are scored by section. Scores are research features and cannot create orders (Ch 19).

analytics_definitions: net_tone = (P - N) / (P + N) with P, N counts of positive/negative lexicon words [-1, 1]; missing when P + N = 0

BLS: the schedule web pages refused automated fetch in the research session. Owner inputs: an importance map and a mapping from events to instruments, currencies and countries. The pinned IANA tzdata version and market holiday calendars come from Ch 3.
capabilities.outputs: calendar_event rows {event_key, agency, release_code, release_name, country/region, reference_period, scheduled_local, source_tz, tz_basis (explicit_offset | source_stated | assumed), scheduled_utc, time_status (exact | date_only | unconfirmed), status (scheduled | released | delayed | rescheduled | cancelled), importance_owner, linked_series_ids, linked_instrument_ids, source_url, retrieved_at, snapshot_version}. Also: an append-only calendar snapshot log, a change log, CSV/ICS exports with attribution, an event stream to the actuals-capture and consensus records, and a risk-window feed.
capabilities.behavior: Each source has an adapter that fetches on a schedule (daily for full calendars, hourly within 48 h of an event), keeps the raw payload with its hash, and normalizes it into calendar_event. event_key = hash(agency, release_code, reference_period), so it stays the same when an event is rescheduled. A changed time or date creates a new snapshot version and a change-log row. Older versions are never overwritten. Time zones: FRED's calendar states 'All times are US Central Time' (tz_basis=source_stated); Eurostat states Europe/Luxembourg (source_stated); the BEA JSON carries explicit UTC offsets (explicit_offset) and is preferred over the BEA HTML page, which shows times without a zone; the Census list view shows times without a zone, so Census times are stored with tz_basis=assumed (America/New_York) and flagged until an official statement is found. The BEA JSON is keyed by release family (e.g. 'Gross Domestic Product'), so it does not distinguish advance from second estimates; release names are joined from the HTML page by date. The BEA JSON also contains repeated timestamps within one release key and a top-level 'file_last_updated' string; the adapter dedupes on (release key, timestamp) and records file_last_updated as the source version. The MOSPI calendar gives dates only, states '*In case of holidays, reports release on next working day' and 'Dates indicated may change in case of exigencies'. Those events are stored date-only with time_status=unconfirmed and never get an invented time. FRED dates are labelled 'source-published date, not FRED availability', following FRED's own caveat that release dates 'do not necessarily represent when data will be available'. The calendar is display and research metadata. Its risk-window tags may only reduce exposure or abstain. The UI always shows source and retrieval age, and shows a source as stale when it has not refreshed within its freshness budget.

capabilities.title: Release-time capture of actuals, revisions to prior and first prints
capabilities.user_workflow: 1. At the scheduled time, the owner sees the event change from 'scheduled' to 'released', with actual value, unit, reference period, the prior value as first shown and the prior value as now revised. 2. Opens the detail: source document link, payload hash, source publication time, first-observed time, latency against schedule and parser version. 3. If consensus is licensed, compares against it (consensus record). 4. The released value is published to the research and strategy layer as a typed, versioned event feature whose availability time is the first-observed time.

reference_scope.module_or_feature: Economic release data: prior, revision to prior, consensus, actual

reference_scope.supporting_quote: "Headlines are updated two to three minutes after their release time for time series data."

capabilities.inputs: Calendar events from the release-calendar record. The BLS Public Data API v2 (JSON; the newest observation carries "latest": "true"). The ECB Data API updatedAfter parameter (returns observations 'added', 'revised' and 'deleted' since a supplied timestamp). The Eurostat API ('updated twice a day, at 11:00 and at 23:00 CET'; only the latest version is kept). MOSPI press releases linked from the ARC (PIB pages). FRED/ALFRED output_type=4 ('Observations, Initial Release Only'), used for after-the-fact reconciliation of US first prints. The BEA data API was not researched in this pass.
capabilities.outputs: release_event {event_key, series_id, reference_period, actual, unit, scale, seasonal_adjustment, prior_period, prior_as_first_shown, prior_now, revision_to_prior, source_published_at, first_observed_at, ingest_seq, source_url, payload_hash, parser_version, status (released | corrected | quarantined)}, plus an append-only correction chain and per-source latency statistics.
capabilities.behavior: From T-2 minutes the poller tightens for the event's source, within each source's fair-access limits, with jittered backoff and a hard cap. When a payload's newest observation for the expected reference period appears, the parser extracts typed numbers and validates unit, scale, period and sign against series metadata, then writes release_event idempotently on (event_key, payload_hash). Values that fail validation are quarantined, never zero-filled (Ch 11: a missing value is not zero). The prior value as now revised is captured in the same transaction so revision_to_prior is exact. If the agency corrects a value later, a new version is linked to the original and nothing is overwritten. Live availability time is first_observed_at. Values reconstructed from history use a conservative availability (see definitions). Typed facts are produced by parsers, not language models. A model can summarize, but a model summary never triggers an order (Ch 17).

analytics_definitions: revision_to_prior = prior_now - prior_as_first_shown (series units).
release_latency_s = first_observed_at_utc - scheduled_utc (seconds; per source distribution tracked as p50/p95/max).

availability_time (live) = first_observed_at_utc. availability_time (reconstructed history) = scheduled_utc + p95(release_latency_s for that source), or 23:59:59 local on the release date if no scheduled time is known.
derived month-over-month change (when computed locally) pch = 100 * (x_t / x_{t-1} - 1), with x_t and x_{t-1} taken from the same vintage.

dependencies.backend: Event-driven poller and per-source parsers, a validation layer (unit/scale/period), an idempotent writer and a correction linker.
dependencies.frontend: Calendar row state transitions, a release detail drawer and a latency panel.
dependencies.storage: release_event table, raw payload store with hashes, and per-source latency metrics.
dependencies.integration: Release-calendar record (triggers), vintages record (each release creates a vintage), consensus record (surprise), Ch 17 event pipeline, Ch 26 observability.

capabilities.degraded_behavior: If the source is unreachable at release time, the status becomes 'delayed (source unreachable)' and nothing is published. Release failures and recoveries feed the per-source observed release latency. If the parse fails or validation is ambiguous, the value is quarantined, flagged for the owner and no feature is emitted. If the reference period is unexpected (for example, a skipped month), it is flagged. Duplicate payloads are no-ops.
acceptance_criteria: In a replayed BLS CPI fixture with injected timing, the 2026 M09 observation is recorded with first_observed_at >= scheduled_utc, and no feature for it is emitted before first_observed_at.
When prior_now differs from prior_as_first_shown, revision_to_prior = prior_now - prior_as_first_shown is stored and both values are displayed.
Replaying the same payload twice yields exactly one release_event.
A payload whose scale differs from series metadata (for example thousands vs units) is quarantined and emits no feature.

For a sample of 20 US series-releases, every captured first print equals the ALFRED output_type=4 value after applying the series' unit and scale. Any mismatch fails the check and is listed with series, reference period and both values.
capabilities.verification_procedure: Use a recorded-HTTP replay harness with injected timing (early, on-time, late, 5xx, malformed). Assert the state machine transitions and that no early emission occurs. Reconcile with ALFRED initial releases each night. Fault injection (Ch 28): drop the network at T-0, restore at T+3 min, and assert the status sequence and recorded latency.

capabilities.title: Consensus forecasts, point-in-time consensus snapshots and surprise metrics
capabilities.user_workflow: 1. Before a release, the owner sees the consensus statistic (median or mean as the licence provides), contributor count and range if licensed, the source name and the snapshot time. 2. After release, sees raw surprise (actual minus consensus) and standardized surprise. 3. Opens a per-indicator surprise history chart and an owner-defined composite surprise index per region. 4. Research event studies (Ch 17) pull the last consensus snapshot strictly before release time. 5. Where no licence exists, sees public survey forecasts (Philadelphia Fed SPF, ECB SPF) labelled 'quarterly survey forecast', never 'consensus'.

reference_scope.module_or_feature: Economic forecasts function: consensus and individual contributor forecasts
reference_scope.supporting_quote: "The economic forecasts function provides consensus as well as individual contributor forecasts for more than two dozen specific indicators across countries and regions."
"Bloomberg's consensus forecasts with historical timestamps and revisions" ... "capturing forecast updates, consensus evolution, and full revision histories"; observations "extending back to 1997".
"Consensus forecasts covering 900+ economic indicators and market variables"; "Historical polling data and forecast revisions tracked continuously since 1999".
Data Frequency "Real-Time"; delivery: "Excel, Deployed/Onsite Servers, API, Web Service, SFTP, Cloud, Desktop, FTP, Bulk, Website, Digital Files"; history "From 1999".
"Consensus is proprietary and actively managed to ensure optimum results from the forecasts submitted by economists around the world who participate in Econoday's survey."

reference_scope.product: S&P Capital IQ Pro (2023 press release)
reference_scope.module_or_feature: Macroeconomic historical and forecast datasets (S&P's own forecasts; the release does not describe them as consensus)
reference_scope.supporting_quote: "Enhanced historical and forecast datasets" "on more than 40 global macroeconomic indicators for more than 200 countries and territories".

capabilities.inputs: One licensed consensus source chosen by the owner. Candidates whose documentation was fetched: the Trading Economics calendar API, whose Forecast field is documented as 'Consensus forecast from a representative group of economists', and LSEG Reuters Polls. Bloomberg is available only under a Terminal or data licence. Public survey alternatives: Philadelphia Fed SPF (quarterly since 1968; mean and median forecasts, cross-sectional dispersion, and individual forecasts identified only by ID numbers) and ECB SPF (four times a year since 1999; point forecasts and probability distributions; aggregates and microdata). Actuals come from the actuals-capture record, release times from the calendar record, and an indicator definition registry (SA/NSA, MoM/YoY, units).
capabilities.outputs: consensus_snapshot {event_key, source, license_id, statistic (median | mean | vendor-defined), value, unit, n_contributors?, high?, low?, snapshot_time, retrieved_at}, plus surprise {event_key, consensus_snapshot_id, raw, standardized, scale_definition, N_history}, a composite_surprise_index time series per region, and survey_forecast rows for SPF data clearly typed as surveys.
capabilities.behavior: Consensus is snapshotted at T-24h, T-1h and as the last pre-release poll, and every snapshot is kept. Surprise uses the latest snapshot with snapshot_time strictly before scheduled_utc. A definition check must pass before surprise is computed: the indicator measure, seasonal adjustment, transformation and unit of the consensus must equal the actual's (Ch 17). Vendor-own projections (e.g., Trading Economics TEForecast, documented as 'Trading Economics' own projection') are stored as forecasts, never as consensus. Trading Economics field semantics are mapped as documented: Previous = 'Value from the previous release, after revision if applicable'; Revised = 'Value reported in the previous release, before revision'; Date = 'Release date and time of the data in UTC'. A 'consensus' is never derived from news text, scraped pages or incomplete data (Ch 1). Each row carries license_id, and storage, display and model processing are gated by that licence's flags. Without a licence the consensus column shows 'not licensed' and surprise is not computed, while SPF survey forecasts are available as a separate, lower-frequency research input.

rights.licensing: Consensus is licensed content. Storage, redistribution and derived-data rights are contract-specific and were not fetched for any vendor (unverified). IBKR states its Econoday consensus is proprietary. Philadelphia Fed SPF page shows only 'Copyright 2026. All rights reserved.' (reuse terms unverified). ECB SPF falls under the ECB reuse policy: source quoted, unmodified.
rights.entitlement: A paid or contracted vendor subscription for consensus (vendor pricing unverified). The IBKR display of Econoday is listed as free, but the fetched page shows no API or extraction right.
rights.retention: Per vendor contract (unverified). Snapshots must be deletable by license_id if a licence ends, while allowed hashes and manifests are kept (Ch 11).
rights.model_processing: Default deny for licensed consensus until the contract explicitly permits external-model processing. Public SPF data is allowed subject to its terms (unverified for Philadelphia Fed).

analytics_definitions: raw_surprise = actual - consensus (indicator units; for rates of change, percentage points).

standardized_surprise = raw_surprise / s, where s = sample standard deviation of raw_surprise over the previous N releases of the same indicator and same consensus source, using only releases before the current one. Undefined if N < 12 (owner-configurable minimum).
dispersion_scaled_surprise = raw_surprise / sd(contributor forecasts), only when contributor-level data is licensed.

composite_surprise_index(region, t) = sum over indicators i of w_i * sum over releases k with t_k <= t of z_{i,k} * exp(-ln(2) * (t - t_k) / H), where H = half-life in days (owner-set). This is a project-defined index, not a vendor index.
snapshot_valid(snapshot, event) = snapshot.snapshot_time < event.scheduled_utc (strict inequality).

dependencies.backend: Vendor adapter(s), snapshot scheduler, definition-match validator and surprise calculator.
dependencies.frontend: Consensus and surprise columns in the calendar, a surprise history chart and a composite index chart, all with source and license badges.
dependencies.storage: consensus_snapshot, surprise and survey_forecast tables, with license_id on every row.
dependencies.integration: Calendar and actuals records, the Ch 17 event study pipeline, the Ch 11 source registry (rights flags) and the Ch 19 model router (deny licensed rows).

capabilities.degraded_behavior: With no licence or a vendor outage, consensus shows 'unavailable' and surprise is not computed. Snapshots older than the configured maximum before release are flagged stale. A licence expiry purges or hides rows as the contract requires. Surprise history never mixes consensus sources without a visible break marker.
acceptance_criteria: Given snapshots at T-2d, T-1h and T+5m, surprise uses the T-1h snapshot. The T+5m snapshot is never used.
An indicator whose consensus is YoY while the actual is MoM is rejected with a definition-mismatch error and no surprise row is written.
Standardized surprise is null until 12 prior same-source releases exist.
Rows with license model_processing=false never appear in any cloud-model request log (audit query returns zero rows).
SPF values are displayed with the label 'quarterly survey forecast' and their survey date, and never fill the consensus column.
A Trading Economics TEForecast value is stored with statistic='vendor projection' and never populates consensus_snapshot.
capabilities.verification_procedure: Replay fixtures with timed snapshots and actuals, recompute surprises with an independent script and compare exactly. Run a rights audit by scanning model-router request logs for license_ids flagged deny. Do a source-switch test: change vendor mid-history and assert a break marker and no mixed standardization window.

capabilities.title: Macro series vintages and point-in-time (as-of) queries
capabilities.user_workflow: 1. The owner picks a series (e.g., US payrolls, euro area GDP growth, India IIP) and an as-of date, then sees the value as known at that date next to the latest value. 2. Opens the revision triangle (reference period by vintage) and the revision statistics. 3. A backtest requests macro features as of each decision time and runs a leak check that fails if any feature's availability time is after the decision time. 4. Where no historical vintages exist (Eurostat, MOSPI, RBI before our first snapshot), the owner sees 'vintage unknown before <date>' instead of the latest value.

reference_scope.product: LSEG/Refinitiv Datastream (2022 fact sheet hosted by the University of Zurich)
reference_scope.supporting_quote: "Economics point in time data covers 111+ countries/ markets and over 10,000 economic series." It lets you "view economic data as it was originally reported upon release, then view how it changed over time."
"Combine forecasts, Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI), surveys and point-in-time history in one source." The Features & Benefits section gives 10,000 for "Economic PIT series".
"historical, time-stamped observations extending back to 1997" ... "capturing forecast updates, consensus evolution, and full revision histories"

capabilities.inputs: ALFRED/FRED API: series/observations with realtime_start, realtime_end, vintage_dates and output_type (1 = Observations by Real-Time Period, 2 = Observations by Vintage Date, All Observations, 3 = Observations by Vintage Date, New and Revised Observations Only, 4 = Observations, Initial Release Only), and series/vintagedates (dates only, YYYY-MM-DD). Philadelphia Fed Real-Time Data Set for Macroeconomists. ECB Data API includeHistory=true (the help page: 'the version currently in production and all previous versions will be returned'; the CSV output carries ACTION, VALID_FROM and VALID_TO columns, observed in a probe). Our own snapshots of latest-only sources: Eurostat, BLS, MOSPI, RBI DBIE. Release times come from the calendar and actuals records.
capabilities.outputs: A bitemporal observation store {series_id, reference_period, value, unit, valid_from (knowledge time), valid_to, availability_time, source, source_vintage_id, retrieved_at, payload_hash}. Plus an as_of(series, t) API, a revision triangle matrix, revision statistics, and a leak-check report per backtest.
capabilities.behavior: Vintages from ALFRED and RTDSM are loaded as source vintages. Vintages from latest-only sources are built by daily (or release-triggered) snapshots that write a new version only when a value changes. ALFRED vintage dates carry no time of day, so availability_time is set conservatively from the calendar release time when known, otherwise end of day in the source timezone (Ch 3: a September backtest must not use a December revision). ECB includeHistory rows are loaded with their VALID_FROM timestamps. A probe on 2026-10-22 of euro area GDP growth (MNA/Q.Y.I9.W2.S1.S1.B.B1GQ._Z._Z._Z.EUR.LR.GY from 2024-Q1, includeHistory=true) returned 9 observations (2024-Q1 to 2026-Q1), one version each, all VALID_FROM 2026-07-15T11:14:38+02:00, so ECB history depth is not assumed and earlier as-of queries return 'vintage unknown'. Corrections create new versions and never mutate old rows (Ch 11). Each as-of result carries provenance so the terminal can show inputs and dates.

analytics_definitions: Bitemporal value: each stored value v(s, p) has a knowledge interval [valid_from, valid_to). as_of(s, p, t) = the v with valid_from <= t < valid_to and availability_time <= t; otherwise 'unknown'.
availability_time for an ALFRED vintage date d = d + release_time_of_day(source calendar) in the source timezone if known, else d 23:59:59 in the source timezone.
first_release(s, p) = the value in the earliest vintage containing p (equivalent to ALFRED output_type=4).
total_revision(s, p) = v_latest(s, p) - first_release(s, p); mean_abs_revision(s) = mean over p of |total_revision|; revision_bias(s) = mean over p of total_revision.
Leak check: for every (feature, decision_time tau) pair used in a backtest, require availability_time <= tau; report count and list of violations.

dependencies.storage: Columnar bitemporal tables partitioned by source/series (Ch 11), with a metadata DB for vintage manifests.

A deliberately leaked feature (availability_time > decision_time) makes the backtest leak check fail with the violating row listed.
The revision triangle for a sample series reproduces ALFRED output_type=2 data cell-for-cell.

Assert values and 'unknown' states. Run the snapshotter on a synthetic latest-only source with scripted changes and assert version counts. Inject a late-arriving vintage and assert the leak check catches its use.

analytics_definitions: Let k = observations per year (12 monthly, 4 quarterly, 52 weekly, 1 annual).
chg_t = x_t - x_{t-1}; ch1_t = x_t - x_{t-k}.

pca_t = 100 * ((x_t / x_{t-1})^k - 1); cch_t = 100 * ln(x_t / x_{t-1}); cca_t = 100 * k * ln(x_t / x_{t-1}); log_t = ln(x_t). (FRED documents these unit keys by name only; the formulas are standard definitions to be checked against FRED output.)

Aggregation to a lower frequency: avg = mean of observations in the period; sum = sum; eop = last observation in the period. Error if the target frequency is higher than native (FRED: 'an error will be returned if a frequency is specified that is higher than the native frequency of the series').
rebase_t = 100 * x_t / x_base.

Range policies (Fed) are stored as lower and upper bounds, never as one number. Minutes due dates are computed from published rules and shown as 'computed', with the official date replacing them when published. analytics_definitions: change_bp = 100 * (r_new - r_old), with rates in percent.
For target ranges [L, U]: midpoint = (L + U) / 2; change_bp uses the change in U (equal to the change in L for parallel moves); a non-parallel change is flagged.

FOMC minutes_due = decision_date + 21 calendar days ('The minutes of regularly scheduled meetings are released three weeks after the date of the policy decision'); e.g., decision 2026-10-28 gives minutes due 2026-11-18.

RBI minutes_due = last meeting day + 14 calendar days (Section 45ZL of the RBI Act, 1934: 'the Reserve Bank shall publish, on the fourteenth day after every meeting of the Monetary Policy Committee, the minutes'); e.g., meeting October 5 to 7, 2026 gives 2026-10-21, matching the press release dated Oct 21, 2026.

capabilities.behavior: The Treasury XML is ingested from 18:00 ET with retries until 21:00 ET. Tenor fields observed in the October 2026 feed (BC_1MONTH, BC_1_5MONTH, BC_2MONTH, BC_3MONTH, BC_4MONTH, BC_6MONTH, BC_1YEAR, BC_2YEAR, BC_3YEAR, BC_5YEAR, BC_7YEAR, BC_10YEAR, BC_20YEAR, BC_30YEAR) map to canonical tenors. The feed also carries BC_30YEARDISPLAY (equal to BC_30YEAR on 2026-10-21); it is kept as a raw field, not stored as a separate tenor. A missing tenor stays missing and is never interpolated into storage. The curve methodology metadata records that Treasury's par curve uses 'a monotone convex method' (replacing the quasi-cubic hermite spline 'as of December 6, 2021') on 'indicative, bid-side market price quotations (not actual transactions)' obtained 'at or near 3:30 PM each trading day', and that 'Treasury reserves the option to make changes to the yield curve as appropriate and in its sole discretion'. Any change seen on re-fetch is stored as a new version. H.15 is ingested after 16:15 ET via FRED and reconciled against Treasury for constant-maturity nominal tenors (H.15 notes 'Source: U.S. Treasury'). GSW is loaded weekly (generally Tuesday, data through prior Friday). SOFR is ingested after about 08:00 ET with the NY Fed notice attached in the UI. The compounding convention of Treasury par yields is not stated on the fetched pages (the methodology page says only that bill inputs are 'bid discount rates corresponding to their bond equivalent yields') and is stored as 'unverified'. Bootstrapping is blocked until it is confirmed.

Continuous to annual-compounded conversion: y_annual = 100 * (exp(z/100) - 1).

capabilities.title: Yield-curve analytics: interpolation, bootstrapping, forwards, spreads, curve history and factor decomposition
capabilities.user_workflow: 1. The owner selects one or more curves (UST par, GSW zero, ECB AAA/all, BoE nominal/OIS, INR when available) and dates. 2. Views interpolated values at arbitrary maturities, implied forward rates (e.g., 1y1y, 5y5y), and standard spreads (2s10s, 3m10y, 5s30s) in bp, with history charts. 3. Compares two curves (e.g., UST 10Y vs euro AAA 10Y) only after converting both to a common compounding convention, which the UI shows. 4. Runs a level/slope/curvature (PCA) decomposition of daily curve changes over a chosen window. 5. Exports the analytics with formulas and inputs (Ch 11 formula visibility).

capabilities.behavior: Interpolation is display-only unless the curve's convention is verified. Available methods are linear on zero rates and natural cubic on zero rates; Treasury's own monotone convex method is noted as the official method but not reproduced unless a verified specification is implemented. Bootstrapping from par yields is enabled only for curves whose coupon frequency and compounding are verified (the UST par convention is currently unverified, so it is blocked). Fitted curves (GSW, ECB) are evaluated from published parameters. Spreads between curves with different conventions are refused unless both are converted to one convention, and the conversion is shown. PCA runs on daily changes in bp over a common tenor grid with missing values excluded pairwise and listed. Each output records the input curve versions so a historical analysis can be replayed exactly (Ch 11).

analytics_definitions: Linear interpolation on zero rates: z(m) = z_i + (z_{i+1} - z_i) * (m - m_i) / (m_{i+1} - m_i), for m_i <= m <= m_{i+1}. No extrapolation beyond the end points (returns null).

Par-to-zero bootstrap for a semiannual par curve (enabled only when the convention is verified): with coupon c_n = y_n/100 and D the discount factor, 1 = (c_n/2) * sum_{i=1..2n} D(t_i) + D(t_{2n}), solved sequentially: D(t_{2n}) = (1 - (c_n/2) * sum_{i<2n} D(t_i)) / (1 + c_n/2). Intermediate semiannual par yields are interpolated and flagged.
Continuous zero from a discount factor: z(t) = -100 * ln(D(t)) / t (percent).
Forward rate between t1 < t2 (continuous): f(t1, t2) = (z2 * t2 - z1 * t1) / (t2 - t1). For example, 5y5y = f(5, 10).
Spread_bp(a, b) = 100 * (y_a - y_b), with both in the same convention. Semiannual-to-continuous: z = 200 * ln(1 + y_sa/200).
PCA: X = T x K matrix of daily changes in bp; covariance C = X_c' X_c / (T - 1); eigen-decomposition C = V L V'; explained variance share_k = L_k / sum(L).

capabilities.title: Market-implied policy-rate path and meeting probabilities, with published-proxy fallback
capabilities.user_workflow: 1. The owner opens Policy Expectations for the Fed (later ECB and RBI). 2. Sees, for each upcoming meeting, the market-implied expected rate after the meeting, the cumulative change in bp from the current rate, and a simplified probability of a 25bp move, with the instrument prices and timestamps used. 3. Compares with published central-bank-research proxies (FRBSF interest rate probability distributions, Atlanta Fed Market Probability Tracker). 4. Tracks the implied path over time. 5. Views outputs as research context only. They cannot raise risk limits (Ch 17).

capabilities.inputs: Futures prices for the policy-rate underlyings, which require licensed exchange data: 30-day fed funds futures and three-month SOFR futures and options (CME), and €STR futures (exchange not researched). For IBKR delivery, the entitlement requirement and fees are unverified (pricing pages returned 403). Also the meeting calendar (central-bank record), the current effective rate (NY Fed EFFR), and published proxies: FRBSF distributions ('calculated from prices of fixed-income derivatives'; SOFR caps and floors from the beginning of 2022, LIBOR-based before) and the Atlanta Fed MPT (transforms 'options on SOFR futures prices' into a distribution for the three-month compounded average SOFR; 'draws from Chicago Mercantile Exchange (CME) data').
capabilities.outputs: implied_path {bank, as_of, meeting_id, implied_rate_after, cum_change_bp, p_move_25bp (simplified), inputs[contract, price, ts]}, proxy_series {source, as_of, horizon, quantiles/probabilities}, and a path history.
capabilities.behavior: The extractor uses the meeting-month averaging method on monthly fed funds futures (definitions below), applied sequentially across meetings. It is labelled 'project method (simplified, risk-neutral, no term premium adjustment)'. It is never labelled as Bloomberg's or CME's method, because neither methodology page was fetched. Probabilities assume two outcomes (no change or ±25bp) and are clipped to [0, 1] with a flag when clipped. If licensed futures data is not available, the panel shows only published proxies with their own labels and update dates (FRBSF shows an 'Updated' date; the Atlanta Fed page states no update interval). ECB and RBI paths are disabled until instruments and data rights are verified.

analytics_definitions: Fed funds futures implied average rate for contract month: r_avg = 100 - P (percent).

Meeting-month decomposition: with N days in the month and the decision effective after day d, r_avg = (d/N) * r_pre + ((N - d)/N) * r_post, so r_post = (N * r_avg - d * r_pre) / (N - d). When N - d is small (meeting late in the month), use the next month's contract as r_post (r_post = 100 - P_next) and flag it.
Cumulative change: cum_change_bp(meeting j) = 100 * (r_post_j - r_current).
Simplified move probability: p_move = (r_post - r_pre) / 0.25 for a 25bp step, clipped to [0, 1], sign gives direction. Labelled 'two-outcome approximation'.
Expected rate from a published distribution: E[r] = sum_k p_k * r_k over the published buckets.

capabilities.title: Official FX reference rates (ECB, Fed H.10, FBIL/RBI) for valuation and reporting
capabilities.user_workflow: 1. The owner sets the base reporting currency (e.g., USD or INR). 2. The portfolio view values each currency balance and foreign holding with an official reference rate, showing provider, fixing time, publication time and age. 3. The owner opens the FX reference table to compare ECB, H.10 and FBIL rates for the same pair and date. 4. End-of-day statements use a declared reference source per currency pair. 5. A reporting conversion never creates spendable cash in another currency (Ch 3).

reference_scope.supporting_quote: "Exchange rate coverage includes more than 11,000 daily rates for 179 currencies – all against USD and many against GBP, EUR and other major currencies. Data is sourced from central and other national banks."
Key Stats list "340+" under "Currency factors".

capabilities.inputs: ECB euro foreign exchange reference rates: usually updated 'around 16:00 CET' on TARGET working days, after a concertation procedure 'around 14:10 CET'; the API series title is 'ECB reference exchange rate, US dollar/Euro, 2.15 pm (C.E.T.)'; formats CSV (.zip), XML and XML (SDMX-ML). Fed H.10: 'noon buying rates in New York for cable transfers payable in the listed currencies', 'certified by the Federal Reserve Bank of New York for customs purposes', 'updated weekly on Mondays at 4:15 p.m.'; the current release quotes currency units per USD except the asterisked AUD, EUR, NZD and GBP ('* U.S. dollars per currency unit'); 'past releases are not revised'. FBIL USD/INR reference rate: published at 1:00 pm Mumbai time from 6 January 2025, previously 1:30 pm (HKEX circular). The RBI homepage lists INR reference rates for USD, GBP, EUR, JPY (per 100), AED and IDR (per 10000) labelled '(Source : FBIL)'. Holiday calendars come from Ch 3.
capabilities.outputs: fx_fixing {provider, base_ccy, quote_ccy, rate (exact decimal), orientation ('quote units per 1 base'), unit_multiplier, fixing_time_local, fixing_tz, published_at, first_seen_at, obs_date, source_url, payload_hash}, plus normalized internal rates x_{c->B} with lineage and an fx_staleness status per pair.
capabilities.behavior: Each provider's quote orientation is normalized to one internal convention (Ch 3: x_{c->B} = units of base B per unit of c). ECB rates are quote currency per 1 EUR. H.10 rates are units per USD except the asterisked currencies. FBIL USD/INR is INR per USD; RBI's display quotes JPY per 100 and IDR per 10000, so the unit multiplier is stored. Rates are stored as exact decimals as published, never as rounded binary floats (DOM-02). Availability time is the publication or first-seen time, not the fixing time. An ECB 14:15 CET fixing is not used before it is first seen (publication around 16:00 CET). H.10 daily values are available only after the following Monday's 4:15 p.m. release, so for live valuation H.10 is a weekly backfill source. The pair-level source priority is declared in configuration (e.g., USD/INR: FBIL; EUR crosses: ECB; others: H.10), and any fallback is visible. The ECB says its rates are published 'for information purposes only' and 'Using the rates for transaction purposes is strongly discouraged', so they are used for valuation and reporting, never for order pricing or funding checks. Funding uses the adverse broker-side rate (Ch 3).

analytics_definitions: Orientation normalization: ECB quote 'Q per 1 EUR' = R gives x_{EUR->Q} = R and x_{Q->EUR} = 1/R. H.10 non-asterisk 'C per 1 USD' = R gives x_{C->USD} = 1/R. H.10 asterisk 'USD per 1 C' = R gives x_{C->USD} = R. RBI 'INR / 100 JPY' = R gives x_{JPY->INR} = R/100.
Cross via a pivot P: x_{A->B} = x_{A->P} * x_{P->B}, computed in exact decimal with declared rounding only at presentation.
Base equity (Ch 3, eq. 3.2): E_B = sum over c of x_{c->B} * E_c.
Staleness_s = now_utc - published_at_utc. A pair is stale if staleness_s exceeds a configured budget (e.g., 2 business days for reporting).

capabilities.behavior: Quotes are labelled tradable (broker quote, live), delayed, or reference (official fixing, not tradable), and the matrix never mixes these without a per-cell badge (Ch 1). Crosses are computed from direct pair quotes when available. Otherwise they are triangulated through USD or EUR with bid and ask legs chosen conservatively (definitions below) and labelled 'synthetic cross'. Inversion swaps bid and ask. Quote orientation follows market convention for display and the Ch 3 internal convention for computation. Attribution uses reference fixings at period ends by default, so it is reproducible. Live P&L uses broker quotes. CIP forwards use the Ch 21 simple relation and are research only (actual forwards include basis and market conventions).

analytics_definitions: Inverse quote: bid(B/A) = 1 / ask(A/B); ask(B/A) = 1 / bid(A/B).
Synthetic cross via pivot P (both legs quoted as P per unit): for A/C with A/P and C/P quotes, bid(A/C) = bid(A/P) / ask(C/P), ask(A/C) = ask(A/P) / bid(C/P) (conservative, widest spread).
mid = (bid + ask) / 2; spread_bp = 10000 * (ask - bid) / mid.
Currency attribution in base B for asset priced in L: R_base = (1 + R_local) * (1 + R_fx) - 1, where R_fx = x_{L->B,t1} / x_{L->B,t0} - 1; interaction = R_local * R_fx.
Covered-interest-parity forward (Ch 21, simple compounding): F = S * (1 + r_d * T) / (1 + r_f * T), with S in domestic per foreign unit and T in years. Research only.

capabilities.title: Cross-asset and cross-market correlation, rolling and shrinkage estimates, and macro-factor betas
capabilities.user_workflow: 1. The owner selects a set of instruments and series: US/EU/India stocks or ETFs, index proxies, yield changes (e.g., UST 10Y, ECB AAA 10Y), FX returns (EUR/USD, USD/INR) and macro surprise series. 2. Chooses frequency (daily or weekly), window (e.g., 60, 120 or 252 observations), method (sample, EWMA, shrinkage) and return definitions. 3. Views a correlation heatmap with confidence intervals and a rolling correlation chart for any pair. 4. Runs a regression of portfolio or stock returns on macro factors (rates, FX, surprise) to get betas with standard errors. 5. Exports results with inputs and parameters. The tool warns when non-synchronous closes (US, Europe, India sessions) bias daily correlations.

capabilities.behavior: Returns are computed per asset class: log returns for prices, changes in bp for yields (never percentage returns of yields), log returns for FX in a declared orientation, and standardized surprises as event-aligned series. Alignment uses the UTC close timestamps of each market. Daily cross-region pairs get an asynchrony warning, and the tool offers weekly returns or lead-lag summed correlations. Pairwise-complete data is used, with n per cell shown. Cells with n below the minimum are blank. Shrinkage toward a constant-correlation target keeps the matrix positive semi-definite when the target is positive definite and delta > 0. EWMA uses an owner-set lambda. All estimates are conditional on the sample (Ch 17) and are shown with confidence intervals. No estimate feeds risk limits automatically.

analytics_definitions: Price log return r_t = ln(P_t / P_{t-1}). Yield change dy_t = 100 * (y_t - y_{t-1}) in bp. FX log return in declared orientation.
Sample correlation rho_ij = cov(r_i, r_j) / (sd(r_i) * sd(r_j)) over the pairwise-complete window of n observations.
EWMA covariance: S_t = lambda * S_{t-1} + (1 - lambda) * r_t r_t' (demeaned or zero-mean, as declared); correlation from S_t.

Shrinkage: S* = delta * F + (1 - delta) * S, where F = constant-correlation target (average off-diagonal correlation with sample variances) and delta in [0, 1] estimated or owner-set. Report delta. The intensity estimator is unverified until a primary source is fetched.
Fisher confidence interval: z = atanh(rho), se = 1 / sqrt(n - 3), CI = tanh(z ± 1.96 * se).
Non-synchronous adjustment (summary): rho_adj = rho_0 + rho_{+1} + rho_{-1} (lead-lag sum) or use weekly returns. Labelled as diagnostic.
Factor regression: r_t = a + sum_k b_k f_{k,t} + e_t by OLS. Standard errors are heteroskedasticity-robust (HC1); R2 and residual volatility are reported.

capabilities.inputs: Broker position snapshots and streams (IBKR TWS API reqPositions/reqAccountUpdates; Zerodha Kite /portfolio/holdings and /portfolio/positions); executions and commissions; the ledger journal (ch09); corporate actions; marks from licensed market data (IBKR subscriptions) with timestamps; FX rates (broker FX or ECB reference rates, labelled); manual CSV of holdings, transactions or returns for accounts without an API.
capabilities.outputs: A holdings table with provenance per value. A cash ladder per currency and account. NAV per account, per session and consolidated in base currency. A reconciliation report with typed differences. A versioned snapshot export (CSV/JSON) carrying source identifiers, as-of times and the denominator used for weights.
capabilities.behavior: The ledger journal is authoritative for policy buckets. Broker snapshots are evidence and are reconciled; they never silently overwrite the ledger (ch09). Every number carries currency, scale, source and as-of time. A position with no fresh mark is shown as stale/unpriced with its last mark and age; it is never valued at zero, and it is excluded from any 'fresh NAV' figure. Base-currency conversion uses an explicitly chosen FX source per account. ECB reference rates are labelled informational and are not used to size transactions. Settled and unsettled quantities are separated (Kite holdings expose t1_quantity, 'Quantity on T+1 day after order execution'; IBKR settlement follows the ch09 calendar). Session allocations, protected proceeds and reservations are claims on assets, not additional assets, so they are never added to NAV. Weights always name their denominator: account NAV, authorized capital or session seed. Manual/CSV accounts are read-only, carry an import hash and are excluded from automated risk limits unless the owner opts in. Unknown external trades go to an external-owner bucket and still reduce available capital.

analytics_definitions: NAV_base = sum_i q_i * p_i * X(c_i->base) + sum_c cash_c * X(c->base) - liabilities_base   [base-currency units]
Weight w_i = MV_i / D, where D is one of {account NAV, authorized capital, session seed} and is shown with the number   [dimensionless, displayed as %]
