capabilities.degraded_behavior: Broker disconnected: show the last snapshot with its age, set the account badge to UNRECONCILED, block new entries and allow controlled risk reduction (ch09). Mark stale or missing: flag the row, show the last mark and its age, and leave it out of fresh NAV. FX missing: show local-currency values only, and show the consolidated base NAV as 'incomplete' with a list of the missing currencies. Snapshot pagination incomplete: do not advance the watermark. Manual CSV account: always 'as of import time'.
acceptance_criteria: After startup reconciliation on the replay fixture, ledger quantity equals broker quantity for every instrument (zero tolerance); any injected difference is classified with a reason code and sets that account to 'entries blocked' until resolved.
An automated UI test enumerates every rendered holdings cell that shows a monetary value and fails if any lacks currency, as-of timestamp or source id.
A position whose last mark is older than its freshness budget is rendered with a stale flag, its last mark and its age; its value is never 0 and is excluded from the 'fresh NAV' total (fixture test).
With IBKR and Kite fixtures both loaded, disconnecting one broker sets only that account to UNRECONCILED; the other account's values and badge are byte-identical before and after the disconnect.
Allocating, protecting or reserving cash leaves NAV unchanged, and C + U + I = D + P holds after each of: buy, partial fill, sell, settlement, protection and restart in replay.
Switching the weight denominator changes only the weight column; quantities, market values and NAV are byte-identical before and after.
CSV import rejects every row that cannot be mapped to an instrument, lists the rejected rows by row number, and stores the file's SHA-256 with the import record.
capabilities.verification_procedure: 1) Build a deterministic replay fixture: an IBKR paper account (US stock, EU stock, USD and EUR cash) and recorded Kite holdings/positions JSON (two NSE stocks, one non-zero t1_quantity). 2) Run startup reconciliation; assert zero breaks. 3) Inject an external manual IBKR trade and a delayed commission; assert an external-owner bucket entry, an available-cash reduction and a blocked-entries state until reconciled. 4) Stop the price feed for one instrument; assert the stale flag and its exclusion from fresh NAV. 5) Remove the EUR FX rate; assert the base NAV is marked incomplete and lists EUR. 6) Run the ch09 acceptance tests and the conservation-invariant check after each step. 7) Archive the reconciliation reports with the artifact hash.

acceptance_criteria: In a single-currency deterministic replay (buys, partial fills, sells, fees, a 2:1 split, a cash dividend), realized P&L + change in unrealized P&L + income - fees equals NAV change minus external flows exactly, in integer minor units, after every event.
In a multi-currency replay, the price and FX-translation components sum to base-currency P&L within 1 minor unit per currency conversion.
FIFO and specific-ID lot methods each reproduce hand-computed realized P&L on a 5-lot fixture, and the difference between methods is reported.
A delayed commission adjusts realized P&L on the posting date, links to the original fill's execution id, and leaves every earlier daily P&L snapshot byte-identical.
On an IBKR paper account, after fees are final, |ledger realized - broker realized| <= 0.01 units of the instrument's currency per instrument, or the line carries a reason code from the defined set.
For each venue (NYSE/Nasdaq, Xetra/Euronext, NSE) the daily P&L boundary is displayed, and a fixture spanning the US and EU daylight-saving changes places each boundary at the venue's local close.

analytics_definitions: Long exposure L = sum over q_i>0 of MV_i; short S = sum over q_i<0 of MV_i (S <= 0)   [currency]
Gross G = L + |S|; Net N = L + S   [currency]; NAV-denominated: G/NAV, N/NAV   [%]

IBKR white-paper percentage form, as printed: Long% = Total Long Value / (Total Long Value + Total Short Value); Short% = Abs(Total Short Value / (Total Long Value + Total Short Value)); Gross% = Long% + Short%; Net% = Long% - Short%   [%]. Whether Total Short Value is signed in the denominator is not stated in the paper (see open_questions)
Bucket weight w_g = sum_{i in g} MV_i / D   [%]
Herfindahl HHI = sum_i w_i^2   [dimensionless]; effective N = 1/HHI   [count]; top-k share = sum of k largest w_i   [%]
Look-through exposure to security j: E_j = MV_j(direct) + sum_f MV_f * h_{f,j}, with h_{f,j} the fund weight as of date d_f   [currency]
Beta_i = Cov(r_i, r_m)/Var(r_m) on daily simple returns over window W (preset W = 2 years), with the same n-1 normalisation in numerator and denominator   [dimensionless]
Beta-weighted exposure BWE = sum_i beta_i * MV_i   [currency]; portfolio beta = sum_i w_i * beta_i   [dimensionless]
Currency exposure per currency c = sum of MV of assets and cash denominated in c   [base currency]

capabilities.title: Time-weighted and money-weighted return measurement with GIPS-consistent cash-flow handling
capabilities.user_workflow: 1) Owner opens Performance. 2) Picks scope (account, consolidated, session, strategy, sector or asset-class component) and a period (7D, MTD, 1M, YTD, 1Y, since inception, custom) with daily/monthly/quarterly frequency. 3) Toggles TWR and MWR. 4) Reads gross and net-of-fee returns; periods under one year are not annualized. 5) Opens the cash-flow list behind the number (deposits, withdrawals, transfers, session allocations) and the valuation dates used. 6) Compares with the broker-reported return; differences are labelled by convention.

reference_scope.supporting_quote: The MWR and TWR buttons allow investors to quickly toggle between Time-Weighted Return or Money-Weighted Return as their Performance Measure.

reference_scope.module_or_feature: MWR (Modified Dietz) and TWR method white paper
reference_scope.supporting_quote: Modified Dietz provides a computational advantage over Internal Rate of Return (IRR). Unlike IRR, it does not require iterative trial and error to solve for the return.

reference_scope.module_or_feature: TWR sub-period linking and component aggregation
reference_scope.supporting_quote: Add market values and cash flows across all components for each day, calculate a daily combined return, and then geometrically link the daily returns to get the combined return

reference_scope.module_or_feature: Independent examination of GIPS calculation requirements (Alpha Performance Verification Services; periods Dec 31, 2008 - Dec 31, 2024)
reference_scope.supporting_quote: PortfolioAnalyst software calculated both Time-Weighted Return and Money-Weighted Return net account performance in accordance with the Global Investment Performance Standards calculation requirements.
2.A.12 Returns for periods of less than one year must not be annualized.
When calculating money-weighted returns, the firm must: a. Calculate annualized since-inception money-weighted returns. b. Calculate money-weighted returns using daily external cash flows.

capabilities.inputs: Daily valuations (NAV per scope at a defined cut-off), external cash flows with timestamps and flow type, fees (for net returns), component-level market values for sector/asset-class returns, valuation-policy settings (flow timing convention, large-flow threshold if daily valuation is unavailable).
capabilities.outputs: TWR and MWR series per scope and period. Gross and net. Annualized only when the period is at least one year. A linked unit-value (VAMI/unitized NAV) series. A methods manifest (flow convention, valuation frequency, fee basis). A broker comparison.
capabilities.behavior: The default is daily valuation with daily-linked TWR, so no large-flow approximation is needed. The flow-timing convention is a setting with two values: start-of-day (flow added to BMV; this is the only convention that reproduces IBKR's worked TWR example) and end-of-day. Each return stores which one it used. MWR is given two ways: Modified Dietz for a bounded period and an IRR on daily external cash flows since inception; GIPS 2.A.29 requires annualized since-inception money-weighted returns using daily external cash flows when a firm calculates MWR, and does not name IRR. Component returns aggregate market values and flows per day before linking, so component returns do not sum to the total (as IBKR's paper notes). At session level, owner allocations and protected-proceeds transfers count as external flows; at account level they are internal policy moves and are not flows. Deposits must not reset the high-water mark in a way that hides losses (ch06). Returns are net of all realized fees by default; gross is shown alongside.

analytics_definitions: Daily sub-period return, start-of-day flow convention: r_t = EMV_t / (BMV_t + CF_t) - 1, CF signed (withdrawal negative)   [decimal]
Daily sub-period return, end-of-day flow convention: r_t = (EMV_t - CF_t) / BMV_t - 1   [decimal]
TWR over [0,T]: TWR = prod_t (1 + r_t) - 1   [decimal, displayed %]
Modified Dietz: R_MD = (EMV - BMV - sum CF_i) / (BMV + sum W_i*CF_i), W_i = (CD - D_i)/CD, CD = calendar days in period, D_i = day of flow   [decimal]
IRR (since-inception MWR): solve -BMV*(1+r)^{T/365} - sum CF_i*(1+r)^{(T-t_i)/365} + EMV = 0 for r   [annualized decimal]
Annualized return for period of Y >= 1 years: (1+R)^{1/Y} - 1; no annualization if Y < 1 (GIPS 2.A.12)
Unit value (VAMI-style): U_t = U_{t-1}*(1 + r_t), U_0 = 1000   [index points]

capabilities.inputs: TWR return series (record return-measurement-twr-mwr), benchmark return series (record benchmark-index-data-rights), risk-free rate series by currency (US: FRED DTB3 or US Treasury daily bill rates; EUR: ECB EUR STR; INR: unverified source), the purchases/sales journal for turnover.
capabilities.outputs: A statistics table per scope/period/frequency with sample size n, annualization factor, risk-free source and vintage. A drawdown table (peak, valley, recovery or 'ongoing'). A return distribution histogram. A benchmark-comparison table for up to 3 benchmarks.
capabilities.behavior: Statistics are computed only on TWR series (as IBKR states). Annualization factors are explicit: the default is 252 trading days, 12 months or 4 quarters; an IBKR-compatible preset uses n = 360 for daily data. Standard deviations use n-1. The Sortino minimum acceptable return is configurable (default: risk-free). In IBKR-compatible mode the screen notes that IBKR uses 'the historical annual return including dividends since inception of the S&P 500' for downside deviation and Sortino; that series is not reproduced unless licensed. Beta uses consistent covariance/variance normalisation. Any stat with too few observations returns 'insufficient data' (e.g., 3-year std needs 36 monthly returns). Max drawdown is computed on the unit-value (VAMI) series so deposits do not mask losses. The risk-free rate is aligned to period frequency and converted from discount to an investment-yield basis, with the conversion documented.

analytics_definitions: Annualized return (arithmetic, IBKR form): R_ann = mean(r) * n; annualized std: sigma_ann = std(r) * sqrt(n)   [decimal]; n = periods per year (252/12/4 default; 360 daily in IBKR mode)
Sharpe = (R_ann - Rf_ann) / sigma_ann   [dimensionless]
Sortino = (R_ann - MAR_ann) / DD_ann, DD = std of returns below MAR (IBKR: standard deviation of all negative returns) annualized by sqrt(n)   [dimensionless]
Beta = Cov(r_p, r_b)/Var(r_b) with identical normalisation (n-1 both)   [dimensionless]
Alpha (IBKR form) = (R_p,ann - Rf) - Beta*(R_b,ann - Rf)   [decimal per year]
Tracking error TE = std(r_p - r_b) * sqrt(n); Information ratio IR = mean(r_p - r_b)*n / TE   [decimal; dimensionless] (IBKR's example uses unannualized annual differences)
Correlation rho = Cov(r_p, r_b) / (sigma_p * sigma_b)   [dimensionless]
Max drawdown MDD = max_t (1 - U_t / max_{s<=t} U_s) on unit-value series   [decimal, shown positive]
Calmar = average CAGR / MDD   [dimensionless]
Turnover = min(purchases, sales) / average monthly market value over period   [decimal]
Recovery = time from valley to the first t with U_t >= prior peak, else 'ongoing'   [days]

Unhedged base-currency return: R_base = (1 + R_local)(1 + R_fx) - 1   [decimal]
Tracking difference of proxy vs licensed index (when both available): TD = R_proxy - R_index   [decimal per period]

capabilities.behavior: Single-period effects are computed daily (default) or per chosen frequency and linked with Frongello, so the linked effects sum to the geometric active return. The IBKR-compatible variant uses portfolio weight = beginning weight plus purchases, allocation measured against the benchmark segment return (no total-benchmark subtraction) and selection including the interaction term, as printed in IBKR's white paper. The Brinson-Fachler variant (allocation vs total benchmark return) is offered as an alternative and labelled; its primary source was not fetched in this pass. Segments present in only one of portfolio or benchmark are handled explicitly (zero weight; where the segment return is undefined, allocation uses the benchmark return and selection is 0). Attribution is refused, with an explanation, when benchmark segment weights are unlicensed and no proxy is selected. analytics_definitions: Portfolio segment weight (IBKR form): w_p,i = beginning weight + purchases weight; benchmark w_b,i = beginning weight   [decimal]
BHB allocation A_i = (w_p,i - w_b,i) * R_b,i   [decimal return contribution]
BHB selection S_i = w_b,i * (R_p,i - R_b,i); interaction I_i = (w_p,i - w_b,i)*(R_p,i - R_b,i)   [decimal]
IBKR selection (interaction folded in) S'_i = w_b,i*(R_p,i - R_b,i) + (w_p,i - w_b,i)*(R_p,i - R_b,i)   [decimal]
Brinson-Fachler allocation A^BF_i = (w_p,i - w_b,i)*(R_b,i - R_b)   [decimal]
Contribution to return C_i = w_p,i * R_p,i   [decimal]
Frongello linking for period t: adj_effect_t = effect_t * prod_{s<t}(1+R_p,s) + R_b,t * sum_{s<t} adj_effect_s   [decimal]
Residual check: |sum_t sum_i adj effects - (prod(1+R_p) - prod(1+R_b))| <= 1e-10

capabilities.behavior: The model is versioned and point-in-time: exposures use only data available at the estimation date (ch11). The covariance must be symmetric PSD. The condition number is logged and an unstable sample covariance is shrunk toward a factor or diagonal target with disclosed intensity (ch06). Specific risk has a floor. Euler decomposition is used; a negative contribution is labelled 'hedge', not 'no risk'. Horizons: daily and monthly at minimum, with scaling assumptions disclosed. Coverage by market (US, Europe, India) is reported, and positions outside coverage get a proxy treatment (fallback to a market-beta-only model) with a warning. Bias statistics are computed on rolling out-of-sample windows and shown next to forecasts. A licensed vendor model, if the owner subscribes, plugs into the same interface; its outputs keep vendor labels and rights flags.

analytics_definitions: Factor model: r = X f + e, with Cov(f) = F, Cov(e) = D (diagonal)   [returns per horizon]
Asset covariance: Sigma = X F X^T + D   [return^2 per horizon]
Ex-ante volatility sigma_p = sqrt(w^T Sigma w); active risk TE = sqrt((w - w_b)^T Sigma (w - w_b))   [decimal per horizon, annualized with stated factor]
Marginal contribution MCTR_i = (Sigma w)_i / sigma_p; component CTR_i = w_i * MCTR_i; sum_i CTR_i = sigma_p   [decimal]
Factor vs specific variance split: sigma_p^2 = w^T X F X^T w + w^T D w   [return^2]
Factor contribution for factor k: x_pk * (F x_p)_k / sigma_p, x_p = X^T w   [decimal]
Bias statistic over T windows: b = std_t( r_{p,t+h} / sigma_hat_{p,t} )   [dimensionless; ideal 1]
Condition number kappa = lambda_max / lambda_min of Sigma   [dimensionless]

capabilities.user_workflow: 1) Owner opens Risk > VaR. 2) Chooses a method (Historical, Parametric, Monte Carlo), a confidence level (95/97.5/99/99.5/99.9%; 100% for Historical only) and a horizon in days. 3) Reads portfolio VaR and ES, VaR as % of NAV, per-currency sub-portfolio VaR, component VaR, and per-position scenario price/value columns at the tail scenario. 4) Includes or excludes positions to see the effect. 5) Opens the backtest panel: daily VaR exceptions over the last 250 trading days at 97.5% and 99%. 6) Runs the same on a what-if portfolio.

choose a confidence level assumption of between 99%, 99.5%, or 99.9%. ... Continuing right is the Horizon drop-down. Set the period to 1,2,3 or 4 days.
Expected Shortfall (ES) Expected Shortfall (average value at risk) is the expected return of the portfolio in the worst case; the average of all losses which are greater or equal than VaR.
MSCI's RiskMetrics provides risk analytics including parametric, historical simulation and Monte Carlo Value-at-Risk methodologies, as well as market exposure and sensitivity analysis

capabilities.inputs: Current or what-if holdings with marks and FX. Historical daily returns of instruments and FX (window, e.g., 250-1,000 days). Factor model or covariance (record factor-risk-model-ex-ante) for parametric and Monte Carlo. Method/confidence/horizon settings. Realized daily P&L for backtesting.
capabilities.outputs: VaR and ES (currency and % NAV) per method/confidence/horizon. Per-currency sub-portfolio and aggregate figures. Component VaR. Tail-scenario table with scenario price/value per position. Backtest exception counts and test statistics.
capabilities.behavior: Loss is L = -dV in base currency. Historical simulation fully revalues each position under each historical scenario (equity and FX returns applied jointly); for multi-day horizons it uses overlapping h-day returns, not sqrt-time scaling, unless the user picks scaling, which is labelled. Parametric is delta-normal using the model covariance. Monte Carlo draws factor and specific shocks (normal or Student-t, stated) with a fixed seed recorded for reproducibility. ES is offered in two labelled forms: IBKR's 'average of all losses which are greater or equal than VaR' and the quantile-integral form (book eq. 6.3); they differ when the empirical distribution has atoms, and only the quantile-integral form is used for subadditivity checks. VaR is computed per currency sub-portfolio and aggregated, as IBKR describes. The screen states that VaR does not represent the potential worst-case loss (as IBKR states). Backtesting compares 1-day VaR at 97.5% and 99% with realized P&L over the last 250 trading days, mirroring the BIS desk-level design (one-day VaR at both percentiles, at least one year of observations) as a diagnostic, not a regulatory claim.

analytics_definitions: Loss L = -(V_scenario - V_0)   [base currency]
VaR_alpha = inf{ l : P(L <= l) >= alpha }; empirical with N scenarios: VaR = L_(ceil(alpha*N)) of ascending-sorted losses   [currency]
ES_alpha (IBKR form) = mean{ L_s : L_s >= VaR_alpha }; quantile-integral form ES_alpha = (1/(1-alpha)) * integral_alpha^1 VaR_u du (book eq. 6.3)   [currency]
Parametric VaR = z_alpha * sqrt(h) * sigma_p,1d * V_0 - h*mu_p,1d*V_0   [currency]; ES_normal (zero mean) = V_0*sqrt(h)*sigma*phi(z_alpha)/(1-alpha)
Component VaR (parametric, zero mean) CVaR_i = w_i * (Sigma w)_i / sigma_p * z_alpha * V_0; sum_i CVaR_i = VaR   [currency]
VaR % NAV = VaR / NAV   [%]
Backtest exception: I_t = 1 if L_t,realized > VaR_t-1; Kupiec POF LR = -2 ln[(1-p)^{T-x} p^x] + 2 ln[(1-x/T)^{T-x} (x/T)^x], p = 1-alpha   [chi-square 1 df]

capabilities.behavior: Scenarios are versioned data, not code. Linear equity/ETF positions are revalued by shocked price; instruments without a direct shock are mapped to a shocked index/factor via beta or factor exposure, and the mapping (proxy, beta, window) is shown. Regulator scenarios are imported with source URL and file hash. The Fed severely adverse domestic CSV gives quarterly levels from 2026 Q1 for variables including 'Dow Jones Total Stock Market Index (Level)' and 'Market Volatility Index (Level)'; the jump-off level comes from 2026_Final_Historic_Domestic.csv (2025 Q4), and the peak-to-trough equity decline is derived from the path. The EBA 2025 market risk scenario (provided by the ECB) gives relative equity shocks (%) by country index (e.g., US Standard and Poors 500 Index -61, Germany DAX 40 Performance Index -44, France CAC 40 Index -49, Southern and South-eastern Asia aggregate -43) and FX relative shocks (e.g., EURINR 14.6). Operational scenarios (gap through stop, stale quotes, halt, failed cancel, fee revision, currency move) are evaluated against order/limit logic, not just prices. Results never feed automatic trading; they inform limits and owner review.

capabilities.behavior: A what-if is a copy-on-write sandbox over a snapshot version and never mutates the ledger or reservations. Cash impact uses the reservation rules (limit price x quantity + fee envelope; ch09). Only price-bounded entries are allowed in the first release. Sells are checked against owned, unreserved quantity. Limits are evaluated at order, instrument, strategy, session, broker and consolidated levels with the same code the live risk gate uses. Broker what-if preview is optional, rate-limited and labelled 'broker estimate'; IBKR documents that it returns initial and maintenance margin impact and commission and fees in the OrderState object; for a cash, long-only account its margin fields are informational. When the underlying snapshot changes, the what-if is marked stale and must be recomputed before conversion to orders. Conversion creates order intents that still pass the independent risk supervisor (book R08); the what-if result cannot authorise an order.

capabilities.title: Constrained portfolio optimisation, target allocations and rebalancing trade lists
capabilities.user_workflow: 1) Owner opens Portfolio > Construct. 2) Picks an objective: equal weight (baseline), capped-volatility, minimum variance, mean-variance with turnover penalty (book eq. 6.2), tracking-error minimisation against a benchmark, or match allocation goals. 3) Sets constraints: long-only, cash reserve, position caps, sector/country/currency caps, turnover limit, minimum trade size, lot rounding, fee model, eligible universe. 4) Runs the optimiser and reviews target weights, the trade list after lot rounding and fees, ex-ante risk and drift from targets. 5) Opens the result as a what-if (record what-if-pretrade-portfolio-impact). 6) Converts to order intents or discards. 7) Separately sets allocation goals by asset/sub-asset class and monitors drift.

capabilities.inputs: Current holdings and cash (snapshot), eligible universe, expected returns (optional; from approved research artifacts only), risk model (record factor-risk-model-ex-ante), benchmark weights (if TE objective and licensed), constraints, fee and lot-size model per venue, allocation goals.
capabilities.outputs: Target weights, a rounded trade list (quantities, limit-price bands, estimated fees), ex-ante risk/TE before and after, constraint report (binding constraints, slack), solver status and diagnostics, and a drift report against allocation goals.
capabilities.behavior: Deterministic baselines (equal weight, capped volatility) are always computed alongside any optimiser result; a complex optimiser must beat them in research before promotion (ch06/ch20). Convex problems are solved with a QP solver (OSQP), and solver status, iterations, primal/dual residuals and feasibility are recorded. Infeasible problems return the conflicting constraints, never a relaxed solution without notice. After the continuous solution, weights are converted to whole lots (rounding down for buys), and constraints are re-verified after rounding and fees; if rounding gives zero quantity, no order is created (eq. 6.4 rule). Expected-return inputs must come from approved, versioned research artifacts; an agent cannot inject them directly. Optimisation never adds leverage or shorting while the initial policy excludes them (ch06). Outputs go to a what-if and then to the independent risk gate.

analytics_definitions: Mean-variance with turnover penalty (book eq. 6.2): minimise 0.5 w^T Sigma w - lambda mu^T w + eta ||w - w_old||_1, s.t. w >= 0, 1^T w = 1 - c_reserve, w_i <= u_i, sector caps, ||w - w_old||_1 <= tau   [weights]
Tracking-error minimisation: minimise (w - w_b)^T Sigma (w - w_b) s.t. constraints   [return^2]
Minimum variance: minimise w^T Sigma w s.t. constraints
Equal-weight baseline w_i = (1 - c_reserve)/N; capped-volatility baseline: scale w so sigma_p <= sigma_cap
Lot rounding: q_i = floor(w_i*NAV / (p_i * lot_i)) * lot_i for buys   [shares]
Drift vs allocation goal: d_g = w_g(current) - w_g(target)   [percentage points]
Turnover = 0.5 * sum_i |w_i(new) - w_i(old)|   [decimal]

capabilities.behavior: Default initial profile: cash equities and unleveraged ETFs = paper-eligible; equity/index options, futures, futures options, bonds/bills, speculative FX spot and forwards/NDFs, crypto spot and derivatives, leveraged/inverse ETFs, CFDs, structured products and prediction/event contracts = research_only. FX conversion needed to fund an eligible equity purchase is a ledger capability (book ch.3), not speculative FX, and is governed separately. Enforcement is defense-in-depth: (a) UI omits order affordances; (b) research-proposal schema cannot carry an executable order for a research_only instrument; (c) the independent risk kernel rejects any order intent whose internal asset_class/sub_type is not eligible under the active session's immutable policy snapshot (reason INSTRUMENT_CLASS_NOT_ELIGIBLE); (d) broker adapter refuses IBKR secTypes other than STK (Kite: equity segment only) as a final guard. Limitation of (d): IBKR documents secType STK for both stocks and ETFs ('Specify the symbol for the Stock or ETF'), so the secType allow-list cannot block leveraged or inverse ETFs; for those, the risk-kernel check on the internal leverage/inverse flag (c) is the only automated guard and must not be bypassable by the direct adapter path. Unknown classification = research_only (never permissive). Having a market-data entitlement never implies trade eligibility. Hypothetical positions live in a separate sandbox ledger that cannot be reconciled into or netted against real/paper holdings.

analytics_definitions: mid = (bid + ask) / 2, defined only if bid > 0, ask > 0 and bid <= ask; else null (currency per share/unit of underlying)

moneyness m = K / F and log-moneyness k = ln(K / F), with F the implied forward for that expiry (dimensionless)
time_to_expiry T = (expiry_timestamp - valuation_timestamp) / (365 days) in years (ACT/365F display convention; pricing record defines model convention)
contract_premium_value = premium_per_unit x multiplier x quantity (currency of the option)
put_call_OI_ratio = sum(put OI) / sum(call OI) per expiry or chain (dimensionless; null if call OI = 0)

capabilities.user_workflow: 1) From a chain row or a blank pricer, owner sees model fair value, IV from bid/mid/ask, implied forward and inputs (spot, rate curve point, dividend assumption, time to expiry). 2) Owner overrides any input (vol, rate, dividend, valuation date) and sees the recomputed price. 3) Owner sees solver status per quote (OK, below intrinsic, above upper bound, no bid, not converged) instead of a misleading number. 4) Owner compares our IV with the broker's model IV side by side.

capabilities.inputs: Option contract (right, strike, expiry timestamp, exercise style, settlement, multiplier); underlying price (spot or futures) with timestamp and market_data_type; risk-free curve (US: Treasury CMT/SOFR; EUR: ECB curve; INR: research-only source); dividend assumption (continuous yield, discrete schedule, or implied from put-call parity); option quote (bid/ask/last).
capabilities.outputs: Model price per model; IV (bid, mid, ask) with solver status and iteration count; implied forward and implied dividend/borrow per expiry; input provenance record; broker IV/price (from tickOptionComputation) shown alongside with difference.
capabilities.behavior: Models: Black-Scholes-Merton with continuous dividend yield (book eq. 21.1) for European equity/index options; Black-76 for options on futures; American exercise via a recombining binomial (CRR) or finite-difference engine with discrete cash dividends (escrowed-dividend approach) - selected by contract exercise style, never by default. IV: bracketed root finding (Brent) on sigma in [1e-4, 5.0] after checking no-arbitrage bounds; returns a status, never NaN or an out-of-bounds number. Implied forward per expiry from put-call parity on near-ATM strikes (European) to infer dividends/borrow consistently; American contracts use the forward as input but flag early-exercise premium. Rates interpolated from the selected curve to T (continuously compounded). All inputs and the model choice are stored with each output for audit (book ch.11 'keep formulas visible').

analytics_definitions: BSM call: C = S e^{-qT} N(d1) - K e^{-rT} N(d2); d1 = [ln(S/K) + (r - q + sigma^2/2) T] / (sigma sqrt T); d2 = d1 - sigma sqrt T (S, K in currency; r, q continuously compounded per year; T years; sigma per sqrt(year))
Black-76 call on futures: C = e^{-rT} [F N(d1) - K N(d2)], d1 = [ln(F/K) + sigma^2 T/2] / (sigma sqrt T), d2 = d1 - sigma sqrt T
European no-arbitrage bounds: max(0, S e^{-qT} - K e^{-rT}) <= C <= S e^{-qT}; max(0, K e^{-rT} - S e^{-qT}) <= P <= K e^{-rT}
Implied forward from parity: F = K* + e^{rT} (C(K*) - P(K*)), K* = strike minimising |C - P| among strikes with valid two-sided quotes; implied continuous dividend/borrow q_impl = r - ln(F/S)/T
IV solver: find sigma with |V_model(sigma) - V_quote| <= 1e-8 x max(1, V_quote) within 100 iterations; status in {OK, BELOW_LOWER_BOUND, ABOVE_UPPER_BOUND, NO_TWO_SIDED_QUOTE, NOT_CONVERGED}
Broker comparison: dIV = IV_ours - IV_IBKR in vol points (1 vol point = 0.01 annualised volatility)

analytics_definitions: Delta_call (BSM) = e^{-qT} N(d1); Delta_put = e^{-qT} (N(d1) - 1) (dimensionless per unit)
Gamma = e^{-qT} n(d1) / (S sigma sqrt T) (per currency unit of S)
Vega_per_vol_point = 0.01 x S e^{-qT} n(d1) sqrt T (currency per unit per 0.01 change in sigma)
Theta_per_calendar_day = (dV/dt) / 365 with t in years (currency per unit per day; typically negative for long options)
Rho_per_pct = 0.01 x dV/dr (currency per unit per 1 percentage point)

Position Greek G_pos = G_unit x multiplier x signed_quantity; dollar delta = Delta_unit x S x multiplier x qty (currency); dollar gamma_1pct = 0.5 x Gamma_unit x (0.01 S)^2 x multiplier x qty (currency)
Beta-weighted delta (index-share equivalents) = sum_i Delta_i x S_i x mult_i x q_i x beta_i / S_index
Taylor error = |dV_taylor - dV_full| / max(|dV_full|, epsilon) for a stated scenario (dimensionless)

Persist end-of-day fitted parameters and ATM IVs (our derived data) to build history; history begins on our capture start date unless a licensed archive is added. Peer comparison uses our own computed ATM IVs. Earnings implied move computed from the straddle and from the term-structure 'event variance' method, both labelled approximations.

analytics_definitions: Total implied variance w(k, T) = sigma_imp(k, T)^2 x T (dimensionless), k = ln(K/F_T)
Raw SVI: w(k) = a + b [rho (k - m) + sqrt((k - m)^2 + s^2)], with b >= 0, |rho| < 1, s > 0, a + b s sqrt(1 - rho^2) >= 0
Calendar no-arbitrage: w(k, T2) >= w(k, T1) for T2 > T1 at every k on the grid
Butterfly no-arbitrage: implied risk-neutral density from the fitted smile >= 0 at every grid k (checked numerically)
ATM IV = sigma_imp(k = 0, T) interpolated in total variance across expiries (annualised)
25-delta risk reversal = sigma(call 25 delta) - sigma(put 25 delta); 25-delta butterfly = 0.5 [sigma(call 25 delta) + sigma(put 25 delta)] - sigma(ATM) (vol points)
Realised vol HV_n = sqrt(252 / (n - 1) x sum (r_t - mean r)^2), r_t = ln(P_t / P_{t-1}), n = 21 or 30 trading-day returns (annualised)
IV rank = (IV_today - min IV over 252 stored days) / (max - min); IV percentile = share of stored days with IV below today (requires >= 252 stored days, else null)
Earnings implied move (straddle approx) = (C_ATM + P_ATM) / S for the first expiry after the event (fraction of price)

Event total variance from term structure: v_event = sigma_2^2 T_2 - sigma_1^2 T_1 - sigma_base^2 (T_2 - T_1 - dt_event) (dimensionless approximation, labelled); implied event move approx sqrt(v_event)

analytics_definitions: Expiry payoff Pi(S_T) = sum_legs q_i x mult_i x payoff_i(S_T) - net_premium_paid - fees (currency); call payoff max(S_T - K, 0), put payoff max(K - S_T, 0)
Breakevens = roots of Pi(S_T) = 0 on [0, S_max], found by exact segment intersection on the piecewise-linear payoff

Max profit/loss = max/min of Pi over [0, S_max], plus asymptotic slope test as S_T -> infinity: slope > 0 means unbounded profit, slope < 0 means unbounded loss; payoffs at S_T = 0 are always finite (bounded by strikes and premiums)
Scenario P&L(S, t, dsigma) = sum_i q_i mult_i [V_i(S, t, sigma_i + dsigma) - V_i(now)] (currency, full revaluation)
Probability of profit = integral of 1{Pi(S_T) > 0} under the stated distribution (market-implied from probability-lab record or lognormal at ATM IV), dimensionless
Expected P&L = sum_bins p_j Pi(S_j); ranking score = Expected P&L / stdev(P&L) (dimensionless), the 'expected profit to variability of outcome' ratio described on the IBKR Probability Lab page

capabilities.title: Market-implied probability distribution and user-view trade evaluation (Probability Lab analog)
capabilities.user_workflow: 1) Owner selects underlying and expiry; tool displays the market-implied probability distribution as bars over price intervals, with implied forward. 2) Owner drags bars to express a different view; other bars renormalise; market distribution remains overlaid. 3) Tool searches combinations of 2, 3 or 4 legs and shows the three best by expected-profit-to-variability ratio with expected profit, P(profit), max profit/loss, net debit/credit. 4) Owner resets to market distribution; every trade shows approximately zero expected profit (before costs) under it. 5) Results saved to notebook; no orders.

reference_scope.supporting_quote: given the prices of options, a PD implied by those prices can easily be derived.

We will show you the three best combination trades along with the corresponding expected profit, Sharpe ratio, net debit or credit, percentage likelihood of profit, maximum profit and maximum loss and associated probabilities for each trade

reference_scope.module_or_feature: Zero expected profit under market PD; bar-drag behaviour
reference_scope.supporting_quote: The sum of each possible outcome (profit or loss in each interval) multiplied by its associated probability is the statistically Expected Profit and under the market's PD, it equals zero for any trade.
Set your own probability distribution against the market-implied one and find the structures that fit.

capabilities.inputs: Fitted arbitrage-free smile for the chosen expiry (surface record) or cleaned call/put mid prices; discount factor; implied forward; bin width; user-edited bin probabilities; leg universe and max legs (2-4); fee assumptions.
capabilities.outputs: Market PD (bins, probabilities, CDF), implied forward and moments; user PD; top-3 combinations with expected P&L, ratio, P(profit), max profit/loss with probabilities, net premium; audit record of inputs.
capabilities.behavior: Density from the fitted smile by Breeden-Litzenberger (second strike derivative of call prices) evaluated on a fine grid, then aggregated to display bins; negative densities indicate arbitrage and block publication. Tails beyond listed strikes extrapolated by the surface's wing model and labelled. Normalise to 1. User edits: dragging bar j changes p_j; remaining bars rescale proportionally to keep sum 1. This rule is our own: IBKR describes its behaviour only qualitatively ('all the other bars will simultaneously move, with the more distant bars moving in the opposite direction as all the probabilities must add up to 1.00'), so outputs will differ. Search: enumerate combinations from a strike window around the forward with 2-4 legs, compute expected P&L under user PD using natural prices plus fees, rank by expected/stdev, show top 3. Under the market PD, expected P&L at mid must be approximately zero after discounting; deviations measure fit/discretisation error and are displayed.

analytics_definitions: Risk-neutral density q(K) = e^{rT} d^2C/dK^2 (per currency unit of S_T)
Bin probability P(K_i < S_T <= K_{i+1}) = e^{rT} [dC/dK(K_{i+1}) - dC/dK(K_i)]; tail P(S_T > K) = -e^{rT} dC/dK(K)
Discrete call-spread approximation (our formula; IBKR's page uses an equivalent spread argument without interest): P(S_T > (K_i + K_{i+1})/2) approx = e^{rT} [C(K_i) - C(K_{i+1})] / (K_{i+1} - K_i)
Implied forward check: sum_j p_j x mid_j should equal F_T within tolerance (currency)
Expected P&L_user = sum_j p_user_j x Pi(mid_j) (currency); ratio = Expected P&L / sqrt(sum_j p_user_j (Pi(mid_j) - Expected P&L)^2)
P(profit) = sum_j p_user_j 1{Pi(mid_j) > 0}

analytics_definitions: Par yield y_par(T) solves 1 = (y_par/2) x sum_{k=1}^{2T} DF(k/2) + DF(T) for semiannual coupons (decimal per year)
Zero rate z(T) = -ln DF(T) / T (continuous compounding, decimal per year); instantaneous forward f(T) = -d ln DF(T) / dT
Nelson-Siegel-Svensson: y(tau) = b0 + b1 [(1 - e^{-tau/l1}) / (tau/l1)] + b2 [(1 - e^{-tau/l1}) / (tau/l1) - e^{-tau/l1}] + b3 [(1 - e^{-tau/l2}) / (tau/l2) - e^{-tau/l2}]
Slope 2s10s = (y10 - y2) x 10,000 (basis points); 5s30s analogous; butterfly 2s5s10s = (2 y5 - y2 - y10) x 10,000 (bp)
Reproduction error at input tenor = (y_par_model - y_par_official) x 10,000 (bp)

analytics_definitions: Dirty price = clean price + accrued interest (per 100 face); AI = (C / f) x (days accrued / days in coupon period) under ACT/ACT ICMA
Street-convention price: P_dirty = sum_{k=1}^{n} (C/f) / (1 + y/f)^{k-1+w} + 100 / (1 + y/f)^{n-1+w}, w = fraction of period from settlement to next coupon

Treasury auction convention (31 CFR 356 App. B II.D, reopening in a regular period): (P + A)[1 + (r/s)(i/2)] = C/2 + (C/2) a_n + 100 v^n, A = [(s - r)/s](C/2), v^n = 1/(1 + i/2)^n, a_n = (1 - v^n)/(i/2), P rounded to six places
Macaulay duration D_mac = (1/P_dirty) x sum_k t_k x PV(CF_k) (years); modified duration D_mod = D_mac / (1 + y/f)
Convexity = (1/P_dirty) x d^2 P / dy^2 (years^2); dP/P approx = -D_mod dy + 0.5 Convexity dy^2 (book eq. 21.2)
DV01 = -(dP/dy) x 0.0001 (currency per 100 face per bp)
Effective duration = (P(-dy) - P(+dy)) / (2 x P0 x dy) using deterministic yield shifts (not OAS-based)
YTW = min over workout dates (calls, maturity) of yield to that date
Benchmark spread = (y_bond - y_gov_interpolated(T_bond)) x 10,000 (bp)

capabilities.user_workflow: 1) Owner declares the research decision clock (for example a daily signal at a fixed exchange-local time) and the latency buffer policy. 2) Owner requests a feature panel (entity x field x decision time) such as trailing revenue, net income or a macro series. 3) The as-of layer returns only values whose availability time precedes each decision time, each with source accession/vintage id. 4) Owner inspects lineage for any cell (filing, acceptance timestamp, unit, period) and the restatement history. 5) Owner freezes the panel as a dataset snapshot that the experiment manifest references. 6) Owner compares results computed on as-filed versus latest-restated values to measure look-ahead sensitivity.

capabilities.inputs: Entity identifiers (CIK for SEC filers; vendor permanent ids when licensed; internal instrument id), field identifiers (XBRL taxonomy/tag or licensed vendor field), list of decision timestamps in UTC with the exchange calendar used, latency-buffer policy (seconds or 'next session open'), optional snapshot id to pin a frozen version, macro series ids with requested real-time window.
capabilities.outputs: Long-format panel rows: entity_id, field, period_start, period_end, fiscal_period, value, unit, currency, availability_time (UTC), source_id (SEC accession number or vendor record id), form_type, vintage_id, version_number, missingness_reason (not_reported | not_yet_available | provider_delay | not_entitled | parse_failed), lineage hash. Also a restatement report per entity-field (first-reported versus latest value).
capabilities.behavior: Store facts bitemporally: valid time = fiscal period; knowledge time = availability_time. For SEC filers, availability_time is the submissions API acceptanceDateTime joined on accession number to each companyfacts/companyconcept fact. Each fact carries accn, form, filed and frame fields; this was confirmed on companyconcept JSON for CIK 0000320193 fetched 2026-10-22, and the submissions JSON carries accessionNumber, filingDate, reportDate and acceptanceDateTime. If only a filing date is known, set availability to the next regular session open of the primary listing calendar (conservative project rule, configurable). Never use the Frames API for point-in-time queries because it returns the last-filed fact. Amendments (for example 10-K/A) create a new version; prior versions stay queryable and existing experiment snapshots are unchanged. The as-of query returns, per entity-field-period, the latest version whose availability_time <= decision_time - buffer. Macro series are fetched with ALFRED real-time periods so each observation carries realtime_start/realtime_end; the as-of query selects the vintage valid at the decision time. Missing is never zero: the missingness_reason distinguishes no report, not-yet-available and provider delay. Licensed vendor PIT feeds (Bloomberg, LSEG, Compustat Snapshot) plug in as adapters whose rows must carry the vendor availability timestamp; adapters without one are rejected for research use. India and Europe: no free point-in-time fundamentals API was verified in this pass; the layer exposes them as coverage gaps rather than silently filling from latest-restated sources.

analytics_definitions: AsOf(e, f, p, t) = value of the version v of fact (entity e, field f, period p) with maximum availability_time(v) such that availability_time(v) <= t - buffer; undefined (missing: not_yet_available) if none. Units: those of the fact; t in UTC.
availability_lag_days(v) = (availability_time(v) - period_end(v)) / 86400 s, reported in days.
restatement_drift(e, f, p) = (value_latest - value_first_reported) / |value_first_reported|, dimensionless; undefined if first value is 0.
lookahead_sensitivity(metric) = metric computed on latest-restated panel - metric computed on as-of panel, in metric units (for example annualized return difference in percentage points).
pit_coverage_ratio(dataset, field) = count(cells with explicit availability_time) / count(requested cells), dimensionless in [0,1].
Macro vintage selection: choose the observation row with realtime_start <= t <= realtime_end (FRED/ALFRED real-time period includes both boundary dates, per FRED documentation).

capabilities.degraded_behavior: If SEC APIs are unavailable or rate-limited, ingestion backs off and marks affected entities stale with last-success time; research queries still answer from the last snapshot and label it. If acceptanceDateTime is missing for an accession, the fact is held with the conservative date-only rule and flagged. If a vendor adapter loses entitlement, its fields return missing (not_entitled) and experiments depending on them are marked incomplete, never silently backfilled from another source.
acceptance_criteria: For a 50-issuer US test set and 20 decision dates each, 100% of returned facts satisfy availability_time <= decision_time - buffer (automated assertion over all 1,000 entity-date pairs).
Setting a decision time to 1 second before a filing's acceptanceDateTime (with buffer 0) returns no fact from that accession; setting it to acceptanceDateTime + buffer returns them.
An amended filing creates a new version; a snapshot taken before ingestion of the amendment returns byte-identical results (same content hash) after ingestion.
A point-in-time query routed to the Frames API is rejected with an explicit error code.

For a fixture series with at least one documented revision, an ALFRED as-of query at a date before the revision returns the earlier vintage value (different from the current value), and the row carries realtime_start/realtime_end.
A field with no reported value returns missingness_reason=not_reported and a null value, never 0.
The restatement report lists first-reported and latest values with both accession numbers for every restated cell in the fixture set.
capabilities.verification_procedure: 1) Build golden fixtures from fetched SEC submissions and companyconcept JSON for issuers with known 10-K/A amendments; store raw payload hashes. 2) Compute as-of panels at dates before and after each amendment; assert version selection. 3) Lookahead fuzz: for random facts, set t = acceptanceDateTime - 1 s and assert absence; t = acceptanceDateTime + buffer and assert presence. 4) For ALFRED, fetch a revised series with realtime_start/realtime_end over full history; assert as-of selection equals the vintage valid on the test date. 5) Re-run the full panel from the snapshot id and compare content hashes. 6) Compute lookahead_sensitivity for an earnings-surprise decile or annual-accrual decile sort. This demonstrates the kind of effect Lyle, Siano and Yohn (2024) report, where results 'can differ substantially depending on when the data are accessed'.

parity_dimensions.functional: As-of query semantics (latest known value at a timestamp, version history, restatement visibility) can match vendor PIT products for fields we ingest.

parity_dimensions.latency: SEC XBRL APIs have a typical processing delay of under a minute after dissemination; adequate for daily research, not for event trading within seconds.

A universe built from current constituents is refused for historical backtests unless explicitly labelled as a biased control arm.

analytics_definitions: member(i, t) = 1 if valid_from(i) <= t < valid_to(i) for the universe rule evaluated with data available at t, else 0.
cum_adj_factor(i, t, version) = product over corporate-action events e with ex_date(e) > t and known in version of factor(e); adjusted_price = raw_price x cum_adj_factor (dimensionless factor).
total_return(i, t) = (P_t + D_t) / P_{t-1} - 1 using raw prices and cash distributions D on ex-date; on delisting date use delisting return when licensed, else mark return missing (not zero).
survivorship_bias_estimate = annualized_return(survivor-only universe backtest) - annualized_return(point-in-time universe backtest), in percentage points per year, same strategy and costs.
history_gap_ratio(i) = missing expected sessions / expected sessions between listing and delisting, using the exchange calendar.

capabilities.inputs: Strategy artifact hash, dataset snapshot ids (prices, corporate actions, fundamentals as-of panels), universe membership, exchange calendars, execution model (granularity, latency distribution, fill rule, partial-fill rule, auction handling), cost model id, risk policy snapshot, initial capital and currency, random seed.

capabilities.behavior: Events carry exchange time when available, receipt time, sequence id and a stable replay order; the strategy sees only data whose availability time precedes its decision. A bar's close cannot both generate the signal and fill at that close; the earliest fill is the next eligible event after decision time plus simulated latency. Execution precision matches data granularity: daily bars allow only next-open/next-close or bounded limit fills with pessimistic assumptions; top-of-book data treats a price touch as an opportunity, not a guaranteed full fill; queue position is unobserved and handled with sensitivity ranges. Market-on-close or auction orders require a separate auction model and submission deadline. Cash accounting enforces settlement and no unfunded orders (reusing the ledger rules); partial fills, cancellations and rejections are simulated. A seed controls stochastic latency and fill draws. Every run writes a manifest; replaying the manifest reproduces identical economic events. No-trade decisions are recorded.

Impact uses a configurable square-root scenario model with several Y values and a participation cap based on executable venue volume. Where the broker offers a pre-trade estimate (IBKR WhatIf), paper-stage runs compare modelled commission with the broker estimate. Capacity is estimated by scaling capital and recomputing net utility. Research and cloud-model costs are reported separately and as an all-in figure.

analytics_definitions: IBKR Pro Fixed commission (US stocks, fetched page 2026-10-22): C = min(max(0.005 USD x shares, 1.00 USD), 0.01 x trade_value) per order. Further tiers: 300,001-3,000,000 at 0.0020; 3,000,001-20,000,000 at 0.0015; 20,000,001-100,000,000 at 0.0010; above that 0.0005. Half-spread cost = 0.5 x (ask - bid) / mid x |notional|, in base currency.

Impact scenario (book ch. 7): I = Y x sigma x sqrt(Q / V), as a fraction of price; sigma daily return volatility, Q order shares, V relevant executable volume; evaluated for several Y values (book: 'a scenario model, not a universal law').
Participation rate = Q / V_interval; orders exceeding the cap are split or rejected.
Break-even cost multiple k* = smallest k such that net utility with costs scaled by k equals the predeclared hurdle.
All-in daily P&L = net trading P&L - (infrastructure + data + cloud-model costs) per day, in base currency.

capabilities.title: Walk-forward evaluation with purging, embargo and combinatorial purged cross-validation
capabilities.user_workflow: 1) Owner declares label horizon, training window policy (expanding or rolling), validation and test segment lengths, purge and embargo sizes, and an untouched final holdout. 2) System generates folds and shows a fold diagram with purged and embargoed spans. 3) Parameters are chosen on inner validation only; outer folds produce out-of-sample results. 4) Optionally, CPCV generates multiple backtest paths to obtain a distribution of out-of-sample performance. 5) The final holdout is evaluated once, with access logged.

capabilities.inputs: Sample index with event start time t0 and label end time t1 per observation, label horizon, fold scheme parameters (number of groups N, test groups k for CPCV; window lengths for walk-forward), purge rule, embargo length (sessions or fraction), holdout boundaries, model/parameter grid from the pre-registered search space.
capabilities.outputs: Fold definitions with explicit train/purged/embargoed/test index sets, per-fold fitted parameters and metrics, out-of-sample return paths (one for walk-forward; multiple for CPCV), distribution of OOS metrics, holdout access log.
capabilities.behavior: Walk-forward: train only on data before the validation segment; select parameters on the inner validation segment; evaluate on the next unseen segment; advance. Purging removes any training observation whose label interval [t0, t1] overlaps a test interval. Embargo additionally removes training observations that start within a set span after each test segment. All preprocessing (scaling, imputation, feature selection, universe filters) is fitted within training folds. CPCV splits the sample into N contiguous groups and uses every combination of k test groups, producing multiple OOS paths. The untouched holdout is locked: one evaluation per pre-registered candidate; any further access creates a new registered trial and flags the holdout as consumed. Fold diagrams are rendered for audit. Note: fynance's 'purge' is a fixed number of bars on both sides of each test boundary, not a label-interval purge, so it does not by itself implement the label-interval rule above.

analytics_definitions: Purge set for test interval [a, b]: P = { i in train : [t0_i, t1_i] intersects [a, b] }.
Embargo set: E = { i in train : b < t0_i <= b + h_e }, h_e in sessions (or fraction of T as configured).
Effective training set = train minus (P union E).
CPCV split count = C(N, k) (binomial coefficient); number of complete OOS paths = k x C(N, k) / N.
Walk-forward OOS metric = metric computed on concatenated next-segment returns only.
Holdout consumption counter = number of evaluations on the holdout (must equal 1 per registered candidate).

capabilities.inputs: Trial family from the registry: M trials with synchronized per-period P&L or return series (T x M matrix), selected candidate index, benchmark series, sampling frequency, chosen performance metric, CSCV partition count S, bootstrap settings (block length, replications, seed), significance level and correction method declared in advance.

capabilities.behavior: All inputs come from the registry, so the candidate's author cannot understate the trial count. N-hat is estimated from the average correlation of trial returns; both raw M and N-hat are shown. The DSR paper warns that the average-correlation estimate can be ill-conditioned when T < M(M-1)/2. CSCV requires a true T x N matrix with synchronous rows; asynchronous trials are aggregated to a common index first. Diagnostics are reported with their assumptions; insufficient sample length or too few trials produces 'not computable' instead of a number. These diagnostics supplement, and never replace, the paired-comparison gate and the untouched holdout.

analytics_definitions: Expected maximum Sharpe under the null (Bailey and Lopez de Prado, eq. 1-2, checked against rendered PDF pp. 7-8): SR0 = sqrt(V[{SR_n}]) x ((1 - gamma) x Z^{-1}[1 - 1/N] + gamma x Z^{-1}[1 - (1/N) e^{-1}]). gamma = Euler-Mascheroni constant (approx. 0.5772). Z^{-1} is the inverse standard normal CDF, N the number of independent trials and V the variance of the trials' estimated Sharpe ratios (per-period units).

DSR (eq. 2) = Z[ (SR_hat - SR0) x sqrt(T - 1) / sqrt(1 - g3 x SR_hat + ((g4 - 1)/4) x SR_hat^2) ]. SR_hat is the selected strategy's per-period Sharpe, T the sample length, g3 skewness and g4 kurtosis (non-excess, as implied by the (g4 - 1)/4 term). The result is a dimensionless probability.
PSR(SR*) = same expression with SR0 replaced by a user threshold SR*.
Implied independent trials (Appendix A.3, eq. 9, checked against rendered PDF p. 14): N_hat = rho_hat + (1 - rho_hat) x M, rho_hat = average off-diagonal correlation among M trials (eq. 8).

CSCV/PBO (Bailey et al.): partition the T x N matrix into S equal row blocks. For each of C(S, S/2) combinations, train = joined S/2 blocks and test = complement; n* = best IS strategy; omega_c = OOS rank of n* / (N + 1); lambda_c = ln(omega_c / (1 - omega_c)). PBO = fraction of combinations with lambda_c <= 0. For S = 16, C(16, 8) = 12,870; the paper prints '12, 780', a typo.
Bonferroni p_adj = min(M x p, 1); Holm step-down and Benjamini-Hochberg-Yekutieli step-up adjustments as defined in Harvey and Liu, Backtesting.
Haircut Sharpe = Sharpe implied by the multiple-testing-adjusted p-value (Harvey and Liu); haircut = 1 - SR_adj / SR_hat.

capabilities.inputs: Artifact bundle and hash, evaluation evidence (manifest, diagnostics, paired comparison, stress results, paper reconciliation), immutable promotion policy snapshot (thresholds, confidence level, block method, hurdle, trial correction), authority identity and signature, jurisdiction evidence (for India: exchange algo approval/identifier if required).

capabilities.behavior: Artifact identity is a content hash. Aliases (for example 'active') are pointers, and every move of one is an audited transition, because aliases in common tools such as MLflow are mutable. Transitions are executed only by the promotion service. It verifies that evidence references exist, hashes match and the policy snapshot predates evaluation. The evaluator writes evidence but cannot change thresholds; agents can recommend but not approve their own candidates. Example gates: no causal leakage; costs present; rights resolved; reproducible replay; an untouched-holdout result; and a paired block-bootstrap lower bound of utility improvement above the hurdle. Further gates: effective sample size above minimum; stress outcomes within limits; DSR/PBO computed and within declared bounds as additional diagnostics; clean paper-stage reconciliation. Automatic selection is limited to approved artifacts within an approved parameter domain and instrument set. India live deployment requires recorded broker/exchange algo approval evidence when the SEBI circular applies. Under that circular, self-developed retail algos must be registered through the broker only above an order-per-second threshold. The threshold is set by the Brokers' Industry Standards Forum with the exchanges and SEBI; its value is unverified. The circular states its provisions apply from August 01, 2025; later changes are unverified. Changes take effect for future sessions only, except tightening emergency controls.

capabilities.behavior: Monitoring rules are part of the promotion record and cannot be relaxed by the evaluator or agents. Rules include: realized performance below a predeclared lower band derived from the validation uncertainty; feature drift beyond thresholds; calibration deterioration for probabilistic models; reconciliation errors; repeated operational failures; unexpected model behavior. Quarantine stops new entries immediately, preserves attribution, and avoids duplicate exits. Rollback activates the predecessor only after positions and cash reconcile. Statistical underperformance and software defects are separate incident categories. The red stop is independent and overrides all.

analytics_definitions: Population stability index for feature f: PSI = sum_b (a_b - e_b) x ln(a_b / e_b) over bins b, a_b live share, e_b training share (dimensionless; project design choice, thresholds set in policy).
Performance band breach: realized cumulative net return over window W below lower quantile of the validation-implied distribution for W (block-bootstrap from OOS returns).
Brier score drift = BS_live(window) - BS_validation, with BS as defined in book eq. 4.5, for probabilistic outputs.
operational_failure_rate = failed or rejected-for-defect intents / total intents per day.

Keep a canonical order-type vocabulary limited to types verified in current broker documentation. IBKR basic types include Market, Limit, Stop, Stop Limit, Trailing Stop, Market/Limit on Close, Market/Limit on Open, Pegged to Midpoint and Relative/Pegged to Primary; Kite types are MARKET, LIMIT, SL and SL-M. A capability matrix is keyed by (broker, account mode, product, venue, session, order type, TIF), and unknown cells are disabled (ADR-0012).

Record whether an order type is native at the venue or simulated by the broker. IBKR documents PreSubmitted as accepted by the system (simulated orders) or an exchange (native orders) but not yet elected. Simulated triggers depend on broker infrastructure.

Amendments: for IBKR, only price, quantity and a DAY->IOC TIF change are made in place. Everything else is cancel-then-new with a fresh risk check and reservation, and the UI warns that the old order can fill before the cancel confirms.

Kite MARKET and SL-M orders always carry market_protection; this is a project rule, and the doc defines the parameter for those types. Market orders are not used for new entries, because book Chapter 9 requires price-bounded entries.

Tick and lot validation uses broker market-rule data. If that data is unavailable, the instrument is order-disabled rather than defaulted.

analytics_definitions: Tick validity: price_units mod tick_units = 0, using the tick for the price band. Prices are in instrument-currency minor units, with exact integer arithmetic.
Buy collar: limit <= ref_mid * (1 + c) and limit <= best_ask + k * tick. Sell collar: limit >= ref_mid * (1 - c). c is dimensionless (0.01 = 1%); k is an integer number of ticks.

capabilities.behavior:
Local states follow book Chapter 13 (CREATED, RESERVED, SUBMIT_PENDING, ACKNOWLEDGED, PARTIALLY_FILLED, CANCEL_PENDING, FILLED, CANCELED, REJECTED, EXPIRED, UNKNOWN). They are kept separate from raw broker status.

IBKR status mapping:
- PendingSubmit -> SUBMIT_PENDING.
- PreSubmitted and Submitted -> ACKNOWLEDGED.
- PendingCancel and PreCancelled -> CANCEL_PENDING; IBKR documents that executions may still arrive in both.
- Cancelled -> CANCELED, after checking for a hidden rejection; IBKR notes Cancelled 'could occur unexpectedly when the destination has rejected your order'.
- Filled -> FILLED.
- Inactive -> exception review.
Kite COMPLETE, CANCELLED, REJECTED and UPDATE are mapped the same way.

Quantities and states derive from executions, not from status strings. Duplicate status messages are idempotent.

The parent/child model mirrors the EMSX order/route split: a parent intent can own several child broker orders (schedules, cancel-replace chains).

Durable broker identity is permId for IBKR and exchange_order_id for Kite (null for orders that do not reach the exchange). The system never relies on the API orderId alone across client ids.

Manual TWS orders are read with reqAllOpenOrders, which does not bind, and are assigned to an external-owner bucket. The system does not auto-bind them, because binding cancels/resubmits the order and may affect its queue place.

Preflight records the IBKR 'Maintain and resubmit orders when connection is restored' setting, which is enabled by default. Orders sent during a disconnect stay UNKNOWN and reserved, because TWS may transmit them later.

The red stop cancels system orders individually. reqGlobalCancel is an owner-confirmed emergency action only, because it also cancels orders placed directly from TWS.

Kite: Kite recommends postbacks over WebSocket for individual developers; HTTP postbacks are documented for platforms where one api_key serves many users. HTTP postbacks, if used, are accepted only after SHA-256 checksum validation. Every postback is treated as a hint that triggers an order-history query.

leaves_qty = order_qty - cum_qty for working orders; 0 after a terminal state.
avg_px = sum(q_i * p_i) / sum(q_i) over non-superseded executions, in instrument currency, exact decimal.
Order age = now - acknowledgement time (ns). Cancel latency = cancel confirmation time - cancel request time.

capabilities.degraded_behavior: On disconnect, all working orders keep their last confirmed state, new entries are blocked, and in-flight transmissions become UNKNOWN. After reconnect, open orders, completed orders and executions are re-queried before any state is advanced. Postbacks that fail checksum are dropped and logged. A sequence gap triggers a full order-book query; a gap means EMSX-style sequence numbers where offered, or missing execution ids.
acceptance_criteria: A fill arriving while an order is CANCEL_PENDING is applied: cum_qty increases and the reservation is consumed. The order reaches CANCELED only after a broker cancel confirmation, and a partially filled CANCELED order retains cum_qty > 0. Verified by the fill-during-cancel replay.
Duplicate orderStatus or postback messages produce zero additional events in the projection.
An order transmitted during a disconnect stays UNKNOWN and reserved until a broker query proves its outcome.
Manual TWS orders appear in the external-owner bucket, and the adapter issues zero bind, modify or cancel calls for them unless the owner explicitly acts.
The red stop issues per-order cancels for system orders only. reqGlobalCancel cannot be sent without a separate owner confirmation event.
Every blotter row shows the broker permanent id (IBKR permId, or Kite exchange_order_id when non-null) and the evidence level.
capabilities.verification_procedure: Replay suite with the SimulatedBroker: fill-during-cancel, lost acknowledgement, duplicate status, out-of-order callbacks, amendment rejected after fill, and crash between reservation and transmit. Then in IBKR paper: place, amend and cancel orders and observe the raw callbacks; place a manual TWS order and verify it lands in the external bucket without binding. Compare the end-of-day projection with reqCompletedOrders and with Flex trade confirmations.

capabilities.title: Pre-trade controls: order presets, precautionary limits and rule-based compliance
capabilities.user_workflow: 1) Owner defines signed presets per asset class, optionally per ticker: default order type, TIF, size, price-collar percent and ticks, maximum order value and size. 2) Owner defines compliance rules: restricted list, long-only, no negative cash, concentration caps, trading-hours window, daily gross notional cap, order-rate cap. 3) For each rule, the owner chooses restrict or notify. 4) Every order shows which rules ran, the first decisive failure and the diagnostics. 5) Broker-side precautions (IBKR presets and API precautions, Web API order-reply messages) are reviewed and recorded in preflight. Any bypass is an explicit owner decision.

reference_scope.supporting_quote: This option was created as a safety net to prevent you from transmitting a limit order that has a mistyped limit price. (Percentage field; also Total Value Limit, Size Limit, Number of Ticks, algorithm limits.)
In TWS – 'Global Configuration' – 'API' – 'Precautions', you can enable ... 'Bypass Order Precautions for API orders'.
These precautionary messages may be disabled if the user is comfortable and aware of the behavior they are disabling.
Very often these messages pertain to precautionary settings that are client-configurable for a given username -- effectively 'fat finger' protections that you can adjust or remove if desired

Rules include 'No Negative Cash', 'Concentration of Symbol', 'Custom Trading Hours', 'Orders by Side', 'Gross Exposure Value Limit'; other restrictions can be applied 'to either restrict trading or notify only'.
When entering trading limits in the Org Portal, your entries are effective as of the next business day.
If WhatIf is set to true the order will undergo a credit check for the expected post-trade margin requirement without executing an order.
Pre-trade, post-execution and end-of-day compliance ... Advanced compliance rule building, reporting and complete audit history

capabilities.inputs: Order intent. Signed policy (presets, rule set, thresholds, restricted list). A coherent state snapshot: reconciled positions, settled cash, reservations, open orders, session loss state. A validated reference quote with timestamp. A broker precaution configuration snapshot entered by the owner.
capabilities.outputs: Decision APPROVE / REJECT / NOTIFY, with the first decisive rule, all rule results, the input snapshot hash and the policy version. Preset-filled ticket defaults. Preflight report of broker-side precautions.
capabilities.behavior:
The local risk supervisor is the primary control. It runs every rule against one coherent snapshot (book Chapter 13 pretrade sequence). Rules are typed:
- restricted list
- long-only / orders-by-side
- no negative cash, using settled cash per Chapter 9 equation 9.1
- concentration of symbol/issuer
- trading-hours window
- maximum order value and size
- price collar (percent and ticks)
- daily gross notional
- order rate
- duplicate identity

Each rule is restrict or notify, and agents cannot downgrade restrict rules.

Presets mirror IBKR's structure: instrument-type defaults, with at most one ticker-level preset per symbol. They live in the signed policy, not in TWS.

Broker precautions are a second line. Preflight records the TWS preset precautions and API bypass flags as an owner-entered snapshot. The default deployment does not enable 'Bypass Order Precautions for API orders' unless the owner signs that choice. If precautions would block automated orders, the session cannot start.

Agents never auto-confirm Web API order-reply messages. The adapter may confirm an owner-approved allow-list of messageIds, and each confirmation is logged.

WhatIf previews are used to fetch broker margin estimates and commission/fees where available, never as acceptance evidence.

analytics_definitions: Percent deviation = |limit - ref_mid| / ref_mid (dimensionless); breach if > c_pct.
Tick deviation = |limit - ref_mid| / tick_size (ticks); breach if > k.

Concentration = position_value_after_fill / NAV (dimensionless), using reconciled NAV in base currency. Note: IBKR PTC concentration uses Delta Dollars / account NLV, so values are not directly comparable for derivatives.
Available cash A = max(0, min(C_b, C_l) - H - R - P - B), per currency (book equation 9.1).
Order rate = orders submitted in trailing window W / W (orders per second).

capabilities.inputs: Gateway host/port and client id (configuration outside the repository); credentials entered by the owner in IB Gateway; pinned API library and Gateway versions; market-data-line allowance; deployment record (entity, account type, permissions).
capabilities.outputs: BrokerSessionState (connected, authenticated, auth_required reason, server time, last heartbeat); sync report; pacing telemetry per queue; typed connectivity events (IBKR error/system codes normalized).
capabilities.behavior:
The adapter implements ADR-0012 against the TWS API socket protocol via IB Gateway.

Startup sequence: connect; receive the next valid id; subscribe to account/order state; request open and completed orders, positions, account summary and today's executions; reconcile; then report READY_READONLY. Entries are enabled only by the green-start control.

Pacing: a broker-aware scheduler keeps separate bounded queues for cancels, order entries, queries and subscriptions. It is configured from the account's market-data-line allowance; IBKR documents a default of 100 lines, which gives 50 requests/s. Capacity is reserved for cancels and reconciliation, and local priority cannot exceed the broker limit.

Reauthentication: IB Gateway 'Auto restart' (and 'Never lock' where available) is configured per IBKR guidance. The weekly manual login is expected and surfaces as auth-required. Credential challenges are never automated outside supported mechanisms.

FIX is not used initially. Per IBKR FIX docs, it needs a minimum equity of 10,000 USD to apply and carries a minimum commission of 1,500 USD/month for the first session.

Europe: EU-listed equities are routed through the same IBKR adapter, subject to the owner's entity permissions. MiFIR decision-maker/execution fields are documented for EEA investment firms. They are left unset for a personal account unless the owner's status changes.

Version pinning: the API library and Gateway versions are recorded in every session record.

There are limitations at 400 orders per minute and 10 orders per second. ... a single user/API key will not be able to place more than 5000 orders per day.
Rate limitations also apply for order modification where a maximum of 25 modifications are allowed per order. Post that user has to cancel the order and place it again.
compute this checksum at your end and match it with the checksum in the payload ... Postback API works even when the user is not logged in.

capabilities.inputs: Kite api_key and api_secret (secrets manager); daily request_token from the owner's login; static IP of the execution host; exchange algo identifier if registration applies; instrument tokens; order parameters (variety, product, order_type, validity, market_protection, tag).

capabilities.behavior:
The adapter implements ADR-0012 for Kite.

Session: one login per day. Token expiry at 6 AM the next day surfaces as auth-required. Credential and 2FA steps are never automated.

Orders: cash-equity CNC limit orders first. MARKET and SL-M are sent only with market_protection. The tag (alphanumeric, max 20 chars) carries a hash of the client order id for correlation.

Postbacks: Kite recommends WebSocket postbacks for individual developers. HTTP postbacks, if used, are validated against the SHA-256 checksum. Both are used as triggers to query order history.

Limits: the scheduler enforces 10 orders/s, 400/min, 5,000/day per user/API key and 25 modifications per order (Kite documented values), with lower owner-set caps. The modification count is tracked, and the adapter switches to cancel-and-new before the limit.

Compliance (SEBI circular of 4 Feb 2025): preflight checks the static IP match and the OAuth/2FA mode. It also checks whether the measured order rate could cross the exchange-specified threshold that triggers algo registration; that threshold is to be evolved by the Brokers' Industry Standards Forum. If registration status is unknown, the adapter caps the order rate conservatively and blocks live use.

Holdings: sells check authorised_quantity. Kite's 'T+2' wording on t1_quantity is treated as a documentation lag, to be checked against NSE's published T+1 cycle.

capabilities.behavior:
Dedupe key = (broker, account, execution id).

IBKR corrections: the correction family key is the execId without the digits after the final period. A new suffix supersedes the prior execution through reversal plus replacement events, never by overwriting.

Fees: commission rows link by execId and may arrive after fills. Fees are estimated at fill time and finalized when the report arrives; later fee changes create linked adjustments.

Realized P&L reported by IBKR is stored as broker-reported and compared with the ledger's computation. It is not used as the ledger value.

Capture runs continuously, because IB Gateway serves only executions since midnight (TWS can show up to 7 days via its Trade Log setting). After any outage spanning midnight, the gap is filled from Flex trade confirmations, or from Web API trades (current day plus six previous days) if that API is enabled. The watermark advances only when the backfill is complete.

Unexpected executions (no matching intent, over-reservation, price outside limit) enter the exception journal and freeze new exposure (book Chapter 9).

capabilities.user_workflow: 1) Owner creates Activity and Trade Confirmation Flex Query templates in IBKR Client Portal (fields, XML format) and a Flex Web Service token with IP restriction. 2) Owner registers the query ids and token (secrets manager) in the platform. 3) The scheduler pulls the trade confirmation query intraday and after close, and the activity query after the statement cutoff. 4) The terminal shows each statement's period, generation time, schema version, parse status and differences from the previous pull. 5) Owner downloads the archived raw statement for any day.

reference_scope.supporting_quote: The Flex Web Service is a small, standalone HTTP API for programmatically generating and retrieving pre-configured Flex Queries.
Obtaining Flex Query reports via the Flex Web Service API is a two-step workflow involving requests to both endpoints in sequence. ... Note that all requests must include a User-Agent header.
Rate limit: 1 request per second; maximum 10 requests per minute per token. ... Number of days from the current date to retrieve data for. A maximum of 365 days may be requested.
1005 Settlement data is not ready at this time. Please try again shortly. ... 1019 Statement generation in progress. Please try again shortly.
OrderReference will only be displayed if Audit Trail Fields are set to 'Yes'. ... These features are currently unavailable for Paper Trading Accounts
A token can be specified to remain active anywhere between 6 hours and 1 year. Generating a new token also allows users to restrict which IPs can make flex web service requests.
Format - Choose XML, CSV, Text (Pipe) or Text (Tab). Period - Choose Last Business Day, ... Last 365 Calendar Days, ... or Year to Date; 'a pop-up opens with all possible fields'
the statement cutoff time for securities is generally 8:20 PM EST. ... Daily account statements are available for the four previous calendar years and from the start of the current calendar year.

highly customizable report templates for Activity Statements and Trade Confirmation Reports ... Saved Flex Queries are available for the four previous calendar years and from the start of the current calendar year.
Real-time trade confirmations are generated for all executions. ... Maximum range is 365 days per request.

Account Management: Provides solution for Introducing Brokers and Financial Advisors ... Advisors and brokers can integrate with the Account Management API to manage Client Registration, Client Account Maintenance, User Authentication, Funding, and Reporting.

capabilities.inputs: Flex token (secret); Activity and Trade Confirmation query ids; schedule; date ranges; raw XML/CSV statements; schema field map per query version.
capabilities.outputs: Archived raw statements (hash, period, generation time). Parsed rows by section (trades, cash transactions, positions, corporate actions, fees, as configured). Parse and completeness reports. Inputs to reconciliation and the tax-lot ledger.
capabilities.behavior:
Client: a two-step SendRequest/GetStatement client. Every request carries a User-Agent header, as IBKR requires. It honours 1 request/s and 10/min per token.

Error handling:
- Retryable codes back off. These are the codes whose message says 'try again shortly': 1001, 1004, 1005, 1006-1009, 1018, 1019, 1021.
- Configuration codes fail hard: 1012 token expired, 1013 IP restriction, 1014 query invalid, 1015 token invalid, 1016 account invalid, 1017 reference code invalid.

Parsing: XML is preferred for typed parsing. The parser is keyed by field names, not column position, and stores unknown fields in an extensions map. A Flex query is visible only for the same account selection used when it was created (IBKR token page). Each template is documented in a configuration manifest (fields, sections, format) that the parser validates on each pull.

Schedule:
- Trade confirmation query several times a day for intraday checks. Latency of new executions in trade confirmation queries is not verified.
- Activity query after the securities statement cutoff (IBKR: 'generally 8:20 PM EST') and again the next morning.
- Monthly statements re-pulled after month end.

Versioning: raw statements are immutable; a re-pull that differs creates a new version and a diff.

Paper accounts: audit-trail fields (e.g. OrderReference, Brokerage Order ID) are unavailable, so paper reconciliation keys on execution id instead.

The Account Management API is documented for introducing brokers and financial advisors, so it is not assumed available to a retail account.

capabilities.title: Three-way reconciliation: real-time events, intraday broker snapshot and end-of-day statement vs ledger
capabilities.user_workflow: 1) The platform runs reconciliation per account at startup, periodically and after close. 2) Owner opens the reconciliation screen: positions, settled cash per currency, open orders, executions and fees, each with ledger value, broker value, difference, classification and age. 3) Owner assigns unexplained external trades to the external-owner bucket or attributes them. 4) Breaks block new entries for that account until resolved; risk-reducing actions remain available within constraints. 5) Session close requires a clean end-of-day reconciliation against the broker statement.
