capabilities.inputs: Ledger projections (positions, lots, settled/unsettled cash, reservations, fees). Real-time execution stream. Intraday broker snapshot: IBKR reqPositions, account summary (incl. SettledCash/TotalCashValue), open and completed orders, executions; Kite holdings, positions, orders and trades. End-of-day statements (Flex Activity and Trade Confirmations). Durable watermark.
capabilities.outputs:
Reconciliation report per account and cut time, with:
- matched items
- typed breaks (MISSING_EXECUTION, EXTRA_EXECUTION, QTY_MISMATCH, CASH_MISMATCH, FEE_MISMATCH, OPEN_ORDER_MISMATCH, CORPORATE_ACTION_PENDING, PRICE_MARK_DIFF)
- break ages
- the watermark advance decision
- entry-block flags
capabilities.behavior:
Tier 1 (continuous): every execution and order event is matched to an intent. Unknown external trades go to the external-owner bucket and still reduce available capital.

Tier 2 (intraday, startup and periodic):
- Fetch a complete snapshot with scope and completeness flags.
- Ingest executions since the watermark, with overlap, and deduplicate.
- Compare open orders, positions (by instrument and account), cash per currency and fees. Cash uses the documented field semantics: SettledCash is not BuyingPower.
- Converge with a loop if fills arrive during the snapshot.

Tier 3 (end of day): compare the ledger journal and lots with the Activity statement and Trade Confirmations. This tier closes the session.

Tolerances are typed:
- zero tolerance on quantities and order existence
- currency-minor-unit tolerance on cash, only for documented rounding
- price marks reported separately

The watermark advances only after durable completion.

Breaks block new entries for the account. Risk reduction is limited to confirmed unreserved long inventory.

Kite holdings-vs-positions semantics (overnight positions move to holdings the next day) are normalized before comparison.

capabilities.behavior:
Rule table, keyed by (market, instrument class, segment, trade-date effective range):
- US covered securities: T+1 for trades on or after 2024-05-28.
- India NSE: T+1 for the normal segment, T+0 settlement type for eligible scrips. NSE states that no trading is done in T+0 securities on a settlement/bank holiday.
- EU trading-venue transactions: T+2 until the CSDR amendment applies on 2027-10-11, then T+1. The exact cut-over rule by trade date must be confirmed against the regulation text and the broker.

Business-day arithmetic uses a settlement calendar distinct from the trading calendar. The fetched pages show days where the two diverge:
- NYSE open, Federal Reserve closed: NYSE's 2026 holiday list omits Columbus Day (2026-10-12) and Veterans Day (2026-11-11), which the Fed observes.
- NYSE closed, Federal Reserve Banks open: 2026-07-03, 2027-06-18 and 2027-12-24. NYSE observes those holidays on the Friday; Fed Banks are open while the Board is closed.
So US settlement-date computation must use the calendar the broker/CSD applies, verified against broker-reported settle dates.

NSE excludes bank holidays, NSE holidays and weekends.

Expected dates are hypotheses. Only broker confirmation (settled-cash field movement plus statement settlement data) moves a receivable to settled.

Spendable cash uses min(broker, ledger) minus holds, reservations, protected proceeds and buffer (equation 9.1), per currency, with no cross-currency or cross-broker netting.

Flex code 1005 (settlement data not ready) delays confirmation rather than defaulting.

analytics_definitions:
settle_date(T) = the n-th business day after trade date T in settlement calendar S(market), where:
- n = 1 for US covered securities (trades on/after 2024-05-28) and India NSE normal segment
- n = 0 for the India T+0 settlement type
- n = 2 for EU venues before the CSDR T+1 application date
- n = 1 for EU venues from 2027-10-11 (cut-over rule to be confirmed)
Business day = not Saturday/Sunday and not in S's holiday set.
A = max(0, min(C_b, C_l) - H - R - P - B), per currency and account (book equation 9.1); all terms in currency minor units.
Receivables ladder = sum of unsettled sale proceeds net of fees, grouped by expected settle date per currency.
Settlement exception = broker has not confirmed the expected settlement by end of settle_date + grace (hours, policy).

capabilities.behavior:
Broker-booked entries are authoritative for the account; public announcements produce expected effects only.

Event types are typed, with explicit rules:
- Forward/reverse split: quantity x ratio, basis preserved, fractional cash-in-lieu.
- Cash dividend: receivable on pay date, withholding separate, no quantity change.
- Stock dividend.
- Spin-off: new lot with basis allocation as reported by the broker; the allocation method is broker/jurisdiction-dependent.
- Cash/stock merger.
- Symbol/ISIN/conid change: instrument mapping update, no economic effect.
- Tender/rights: voluntary.

Lots are adjusted through linked journal entries; history is never rewritten. Dependent symbols (A depends on B) are processed in order.

Voluntary elections are owner-only actions performed in the broker portal. Agents may summarize options but cannot submit elections. The platform records:
- the owner's election
- the broker acknowledgement (IBKR processes only electronically acknowledged elections)
- the deadline
It also flags the over-election/pro-rating risk when positions change before the deadline.

Pending corporate actions put affected instruments into a restricted state (no new entries around ex/effective dates, if policy says so). They are classified CORPORATE_ACTION_PENDING until booked, so they do not raise false reconciliation breaks.

analytics_definitions: Split: new_qty = old_qty * (new_shares / old_shares). Total basis per lot is unchanged; per-share basis = basis / new_qty. Cash in lieu = fractional_shares * cash_price.
Cash dividend receivable = qty_on_record_date * dividend_per_share (gross) - withholding, in payment currency.
Spin-off basis allocation: basis_new = basis_parent * w and basis_parent' = basis_parent * (1 - w), with w as reported by the broker (dimensionless).

capabilities.behavior:
A versioned fee-schedule configuration per broker, plan, market and route type stores published parameters, with source URL and retrieval date. Fees are not hard-coded.

The reservation uses a conservative envelope: max(schedule estimate, broker preview where available) plus a policy buffer. Tiered pricing adds exchange, clearing, regulatory and pass-through fees, and routing can choose venues with higher fees.

IBKR: directed API orders are forced to Fixed in the model; SmartRouted API orders follow the owner's plan.

India: the Kite charges endpoint returns brokerage, STT/CTT, exchange and SEBI turnover charges, stamp duty and GST. Kite documents it for an orderbook, with average_price defined as the price 'at which the order was executed' (must be non-zero). Using it pre-trade with an intended price is therefore unverified. Until tested, pre-trade India estimates use the fee schedule and treat charges-API output for executed orders as final-fee cross-checks.

Final fees come from commission reports/statements and are linked to executions. Differences above a threshold are reconciliation breaks.

Fees are recorded per currency. FX conversion for reporting uses a documented rate source, never for funding.

analytics_definitions: IBKR Fixed (US, as published): commission = min(max(0.005 * shares, 1.00), 0.01 * trade_value) USD. The page states that when the calculated maximum is below the minimum, the maximum is assessed. Regulatory fees are added as listed on the pricing page.

IBKR Tiered (US, as published): per-share rate by monthly cumulative volume tier (≤300,000 shares at USD 0.0035, lower rates above), minimum USD 0.35 per order, capped per the published rule. Exchange, clearing, regulatory and pass-through fees are added as listed on the pricing page.
Fee envelope = max(schedule_estimate, broker_preview) * (1 + buffer_pct) + fixed_buffer (currency).
Fee variance (bps of notional) = (final_fee - estimated_fee) / notional * 10^4.

Broker algos: discover availability and parameter schema per contract (Web API algos endpoint, or TWS API documentation) and store it in the capability matrix. Pass parameters as broker-specific extensions.

Record two documented limits: broker algos are opaque (decision logic not visible), and IBKR's legacy docs state that TWAP and best-efforts VWAP are available for all US equities. Availability outside the US is not stated and must come from per-contract discovery.

In-house schedules (book Chapters 13 and 18): TWAP slices and participation caps, with child-size limits, price bounds and a cancel policy.
- The full parent commitment is reserved.
- Amendment loops are bounded (maximum cancel/replace count per interval) to protect queue priority and broker pacing.
- The schedule stops chasing when expected edge no longer covers estimated costs.

India: the India-native slicing options found in Kite docs are the iceberg variety (2-50 legs) and autoslice (for quantities above freeze limits). In-house schedules apply in India subject to the SEBI algo rules.

capabilities.title: Transaction cost analysis (arrival, price improvement, VWAP, markouts, daily range)
capabilities.user_workflow: 1) Owner opens TCA for a date range and filters by strategy, broker, venue, order type, algo, size bucket and side. 2) The summary shows cost in bps of value traded against each benchmark, with the sign convention stated. 3) Owner drills into outliers (top/bottom orders per benchmark) and sees the decision price, arrival quote, fills and post-trade markouts. 4) Owner compares in-house TCA with IBKR's TCA report for the same period as an independent check.

reference_scope.supporting_quote: Performance metrics are expressed as basis points (bps) of value traded. ... Arrival Price: Basis points that your orders were filled better (worse) than the midpoint of the National Best Bid and Offer
is typically available ten minutes after a trade is executed. ... Combinations are not supported.
250+ purpose-built benchmarks and Bloomberg's peer network of 800+ firms
Attribute execution costs across market impact, timing, spread and opportunity cost

capabilities.inputs: Executions with timestamps; decision time and decision price; order submission time; quote snapshots (NBBO or venue BBO) at decision, submission and post-trade horizons; interval and daily VWAP; daily high/low/close; fees.
capabilities.outputs: Per-order and aggregated metrics in bps, with sign convention. Breakdowns by date, side, order type, algo, venue, order size, trade size, order live time and underlying. Outlier lists. Comparison with broker TCA.
capabilities.behavior:
Metrics are computed from the platform's own recorded quotes and fills. The data source and entitlement level are recorded per metric, because real-time and delayed quotes produce different evidence levels.

Sign convention: positive = favourable, as in IBKR's 'better (worse)' definitions. Implementation shortfall is additionally reported as a cost (positive = cost), and both labels are visible.

Benchmarks that need trade-level volume (VWAP) are computed only where entitled trade data exists. Otherwise they are marked unavailable, not approximated from unlabelled bars.

US uses NBBO. India and EU use the venue or broker-provided best quote, labelled as such, because a consolidated quote may not exist.

Execution quality is separated from subsequent market direction, using markouts at several horizons; IBKR uses 1 s, 10 s, 30 s, 1 min, 300 s and 10 min.

Combination/multi-leg orders are excluded initially, as in IBKR's TCA.

analytics_definitions: s = +1 for buy, -1 for sell.
Arrival (bps) = s * (M_submit - P_fill) / M_submit * 10^4, where M_submit is the NBBO (or venue BBO) midpoint at submission; positive = favourable.
Price improvement (bps): buy = (Ask_submit - P_fill) / Ask_submit * 10^4; sell = (P_fill - Bid_submit) / Bid_submit * 10^4.
Markout at horizon h (bps) = s * (M_{t_fill + h} - P_fill) / M_{t_fill + h} * 10^4, for h in {1 s, 10 s, 30 s, 1 min, 300 s, 10 min}.
VWAP (bps) = s * (VWAP_[submit, done] - P_fill) / VWAP * 10^4. Daily VWAP is computed over the full session.
Daily range capture (IBKR definition): buy = (High - P_fill) / (High - Low); sell = (P_fill - Low) / (High - Low) (dimensionless).
Implementation shortfall cost (bps) = s * (P_avg_fill - P_decision) / P_decision * 10^4 + opportunity cost on unfilled quantity; positive = cost.

capabilities.user_workflow: 1) From any workspace the owner presses the global palette shortcut (proposed default Ctrl+K / Cmd+K, rebindable). 2) Types a partial ticker, company or former company name, ISIN, a function keyword (e.g. 'filings', 'blotter', 'stop') or a direct command with parameters. 3) Results appear while typing, grouped by type (instruments, functions/workspaces, saved layouts and bookmarks, filings/documents, help, recent commands); each instrument row shows venue, country, currency and listing status. 4) Down/Up moves through results; Enter runs the selection in the focused panel (or that panel's link channel); Shift+Enter opens it in a new panel or tab; Esc dismisses. 5) On an empty input, Down opens the popup listing recent commands (history), navigable with Down/Up. 6) A free-text question that matches no command goes to help/document search, never to execution. 7) Commands that change funds, orders, policy or start/stop state open their own authenticated control; the palette itself never submits orders.

capabilities.inputs: Keystrokes; internal instrument master (internal id, ticker + MIC/venue, ISIN, FIGI, CIK, LEI, broker contract id where known, current and former names, listing status, currency, country); function/workspace registry (id, title, aliases, parameter schema, required context, permission class); saved layout and bookmark names; help and data-item dictionary corpus; document index (filings titles/metadata); command history; current focus and link channel; owner authentication state.
capabilities.outputs: Ranked, typed result list (ARIA combobox + listbox); on selection, a typed navigation command applied to the target panel, or an instruction to open the dedicated confirmation/authentication screen for mutating commands; command-history entry; local-only query-to-selection statistics for ranking.
capabilities.behavior: Local in-memory index (prefix, token and bounded fuzzy matching) built from the instrument master, function registry, layouts, bookmarks and help titles. Ranking: exact identifier match > ticker prefix > name token > alias > recency/frequency. Instrument rows always show venue, country (US/IN/EU), currency and status so the same ticker on different venues is never conflated; renamed/delisted instruments are found by former names and labelled. Command grammar and vocabulary are our own (no vendor mnemonics copied); owner-editable aliases. Commands are typed objects validated in the client and re-validated by the server (Ch 22: the server repeats all authority and risk checks). The palette is a navigation surface only: any command affecting funds, orders, policy, session or start/stop opens the dedicated authenticated control; the red STOP control is always ranked first for 'stop'/'halt' queries. Free-text questions route to help/document search with source-labelled results; AI-generated suggestions are labelled and cannot execute. The index updates incrementally on instrument-master change events and displays its build time; ambiguous matches are never auto-resolved. Maps to requirement TRM-01 (navigation, keyboard controls).

capabilities.inputs: Panel selection events; channel assignments (panel id -> channel id, role source | destination | both); instrument context object (internal instrument id plus ticker+MIC, ISIN, FIGI, CIK, LEI, broker contract id when known); per-panel capability declarations (accepted context types, asset classes, markets, entitlement requirements).
capabilities.outputs: Context broadcast events with per-channel sequence numbers; destination panel state transitions (loading -> loaded | not-available); channel badges (number + name + colour); polite status announcements; optional FDC3 broadcasts.
capabilities.behavior: Eight user channels by default, each with number, name and colour (ids, names and colour order aligned with the FDC3 recommended set of eight user channels) plus 'unlinked'; colour is never the only indicator. A panel joins at most one channel. Roles: source (send only), destination (receive only), source/destination. On broadcast each destination: (a) checks support for the instrument's market, asset class and entitlement; (b) immediately clears old content and shows a loading state labelled with the new instrument; (c) renders new data or an explicit 'not available for <instrument>: <reason>' state. Responses for a superseded context are discarded by sequence check so stale content never appears under a new header. Context changes are view changes only: an order ticket in a channel is prefilled with the instrument but quantity/side/submission are never driven by linking. Membership is stored in the layout document and survives closing/reopening a panel or the layout (stricter than the behaviour in an archived older IBKR guide, where closing a window erased its group affiliation). Optional bridges: FDC3 Desktop Agent mapping to fdc3.instrument; and, only if the owner separately licenses a Bloomberg Terminal and the interop product, broadcasting to Launchpad groups via Terminal Connect.

capabilities.inputs: Layout document: schema version, name, tabs/pages, grid geometry, panels (type id, parameters, link channel, column/sort/filter state, view mode), lock state, popped-out window hints; owner id; template library; base version for concurrency.
capabilities.outputs: Persisted immutable layout versions; restored workspace; layout export file (JSON); version history list with diff summaries; conflict prompts.
capabilities.behavior: A layout is a preference document validated against a JSON schema; it never contains credentials, account identifiers or licensed data values, only references (instrument ids, query parameters). Explicit save, save-as and autosave draft; each save creates an immutable version (retain last N, proposed 50) with timestamp and diff summary; restoring creates a new version. Optimistic concurrency: a save carries its base version; if another browser session saved meanwhile, the owner chooses keep-mine / keep-theirs / per-panel merge (Ch 22 requires testing two simultaneous browser sessions). Optimistic UI updates are allowed because layouts are harmless preferences (Ch 22 permits optimistic updates only for harmless preferences). Lock mode blocks structural edits (add/remove/resize/move) but not data interaction. Unknown panel types from another build are preserved as 'unsupported panel' placeholders, not dropped. Schema migrations upgrade old versions; on failure the last good version opens. Templates are our own designs following the Ch 22 workspace map. Multi-monitor: tabs may be popped out into separate browser windows; the layout records them and restores them where the browser permits. The red stop and Overview are reachable outside any layout so a broken layout cannot hide them.

Layout load time T_load (ms) = t(all panel frames rendered, excluding data fetch) - t(layout open), p95.
Conflict rate = saves rejected for stale base version / total saves (diagnostic).

Every save appears in version history; restoring version k reproduces it with F = 1.0.
Concurrent edits from two browser sessions produce an explicit conflict prompt; no silent overwrite (the losing save is never persisted without owner choice).
A locked layout rejects add/remove/resize/move via mouse and keyboard while data interaction (selection, sorting, scrolling) still works.
Exported layout JSON validates against the schema; an automated scan finds no credentials, account identifiers or data values.
A layout containing an unknown panel type loads with a placeholder and preserves that panel on save.

capabilities.behavior: Target WCAG 2.2 Level AA on every route. Grids follow the APG grid pattern (single tab stop, arrow/Home/End/PageUp/PageDown/Ctrl+Home navigation, header association). Auto-updating content (quotes, news, blotters) has per-panel and global pause (2.2.2); flashing tick highlights can be disabled. Status messages (fills, rejections, stale data, stop progress) use polite live regions with throttling; safety-critical states (stop activated, live mode) use assertive announcements once. Colour is never the sole carrier: price direction uses sign and arrow glyph; paper/live mode shown in text; link channels show number and name; P&L sign shown explicitly. Text contrast >= 4.5:1, non-text UI components >= 3:1 (1.4.11), focus always visible and not obscured by sticky headers or docked panels (2.4.7, 2.4.11), pointer targets >= 24x24 CSS px or meet a WCAG exception (2.5.8), dragging operations (panel move/resize, column reorder) have single-pointer non-drag alternatives (2.5.7) and keyboard equivalents (2.1.1), all controls expose name/role/value (4.1.2). Reflow (1.4.10) applies to non-grid content; data grids and charts rely on the WCAG exception for 'parts of the content which require two-dimensional layout for usage or meaning'. Publish our own ACR in docs, updated per release.

capabilities.inputs: Grid model (columns with type, unit, currency, scale, source id, rights class), rows (stored decimals, not rendered strings), filter/sort state, rights-registry decisions per source (allowed uses: display, export, storage, redistribution, model processing), owner locale and delimiter settings; for import: CSV file and target list/weights schema.
capabilities.outputs: CSV (RFC 4180 structure, UTF-8 declared via the charset parameter, header present, CRLF) and/or XLSX (ECMA-376 workbook) files; provenance manifest (sources, dataset versions, as-of and availability times, query hash, build id, rights decisions); export audit-log entry; import diff and validation report.
capabilities.behavior: Values come from stored decimals. An XLSX numeric cell is written as a number only when the stored decimal round-trips exactly through an IEEE-754 double at its stored scale; otherwise it is written as text with a note; monetary values always carry currency and scale columns. Date-times exported as ISO 8601 with UTC offset in CSV and as date cells plus a timezone column in XLSX. Missing values export as empty with an adjacent status column (not reported / not yet available / provider delayed / not entitled / not applicable), never as 0 (Ch 11: a missing value is not zero). Text cells beginning with =, +, -, @, tab (0x09), CR (0x0D), LF (0x0A) or full-width variants of formula-initiating characters are neutralized per OWASP guidance; typed numeric cells (e.g., negative numbers) are not altered. Rights gating: each column's source is checked against the source registry; sources without export/storage rights are excluded and listed; real-time exchange data is excluded unless the entitlement explicitly allows export (Ch 23: 'License enforcement must survive exports'). Large exports stream server-side with progress and cancel. Import accepts our CSV schema and IBKR-style ticker lists (DES/SYM/CON lines), resolves identifiers, lists unresolved rows and shows a diff; nothing is applied, and no order is created, without explicit confirmation.

Injection neutralization rate = neutralized dangerous text cells / dangerous text cells (target 1.0).
Rights-gating false-allow count = columns exported whose source policy forbids export (target 0).

Missing values are never exported as 0; the status column is present for every column that can be missing.
A text cell '=HYPERLINK(...)' (and its full-width variant) is exported as inert text; a numeric -5 remains a number.
A column from a source flagged 'no export' is excluded and the audit log records the decision; false-allow count = 0 in the rights-matrix test.
Export of 1,000,000 ledger rows streams to completion with peak browser JS heap growth below a budget recorded in the test (proposed 256 MB); elapsed time recorded.
Export of <= 100,000 rows completes in <= 5 s on the reference machine (proposed).

capabilities.inputs: Computed-value records from analytics, ledger and risk services: value (decimal), unit, currency, scale, formula id + version, input references, adjustments, as_of, availability_time, computed_at, code version, missingness reason; raw source references (SEC accession number + XBRL concept + period + unit; ESEF filing id + concept; ledger event ids; broker execution ids; market-data quote ids with source and timestamps; FX rate records).
capabilities.outputs: Inspector tree view; recompute verdict (match / mismatch with diff); links to source documents; exported tree (CSV/XLSX/JSON).
capabilities.behavior: Every displayed financial number is rendered from a computed-value record or a raw record; numbers without lineage cannot be displayed as real data and test fixtures carry an unmistakable label (TRM-03, DAT-05). The formula registry is versioned; changing a formula creates a new version and old values keep their version id. The inspector shows formula, substituted inputs with units, and adjustments; expansion recurses until raw records. Recompute re-evaluates from stored inputs with the recorded formula version using decimal arithmetic and compares exactly. Edge cases: zero/negative denominators produce 'not meaningful' with reason (Ch 11: a P/E with negative earnings is not an ordinary ranking number); missing inputs show their missingness reason; FX conversions show rate, provider and timestamp; restatements show which filing version was available at the as-of time and whether a later restatement exists; trailing figures use only reports available at decision time (Ch 11). Paper-desk scope first: cash, reserved and eligible funds, realized/unrealized P&L, fees, exposure, protected proceeds, session required return. Research scope next: market cap, EV, P/E, margins, YoY and sequential growth. India: if no lawful automated source for Indian fundamentals is configured, values show 'source not licensed/unavailable' instead of being computed from improvised inputs.

analytics_definitions: Market capitalization (currency) = last price (currency/share) x shares outstanding (shares), with share-count source and date shown.

Enterprise value (currency) = market cap + total debt + preferred equity + non-controlling interests - cash and equivalents, using the documented treatment version (Ch 11 requires a documented treatment of debt, cash, minority interests and preferred equity).
P/E (x) = price / diluted EPS (TTM); if EPS_TTM <= 0 then 'NM' (not meaningful).
TTM flow = sum of the last four quarterly values available at as-of t, or FY + current YTD - prior-year YTD, with the constituent periods listed.
YoY growth = X_t / X_(t-4q) - 1; sequential growth = X_t / X_(t-1q) - 1; undefined when the denominator <= 0.
Unrealized P&L (currency) = sum over lots of qty x (mark - cost basis); realized P&L = proceeds - cost basis - fees.
Session required return = goal / seed - 1 (e.g., 10,000 / 1 - 1 = 9,999 = 999,900%, Ch 22).
Reproducibility check: recomputed value == displayed stored value (exact decimal equality at stored scale).

If lineage is missing for any displayed number, the cell renders as 'no lineage' instead of the number.
acceptance_criteria: Every numeric cell in Overview, Risk, Sessions, Orders and Instrument workspaces opens an inspector (automated DOM scan finds 0 value cells without a lineage id).
Recompute equals the displayed value exactly for 100% of a 1,000-value sample from fixtures and deterministic replay.
P/E with EPS_TTM <= 0 displays 'NM' with reason and is excluded from numeric ranking.
A TTM value lists its constituent periods and filing dates, and uses only filings available at the as-of time (PIT test with a restated filing).
FX-converted values show rate, provider and timestamp.
Session example seed 1 USD, goal 10,000 USD shows required return 999,900% with the formula.
Each US fundamental input links to its EDGAR filing (accession) and XBRL concept; each EU input sourced from ESEF links to its filing on filings.xbrl.org.
Inspector export (JSON) round-trips to an identical tree.
Inspector opens in <= 200 ms p95 for cached trees on the reference machine (proposed).
capabilities.verification_procedure: 1) Golden tests per formula with hand-computed expected decimals. 2) Deterministic market replay (Ch 1 acceptance) and reconstruction of every displayed number from the event history. 3) Manual cross-check of a sample of US issuers against EDGAR companyconcept responses. 4) Mutation test: alter one stored input in a copy and assert recompute mismatch is detected and flagged. 5) PIT test using a restated filing fixture. 6) DOM scan for lineage ids on all value cells.

capabilities.outputs: Frozen panel state with as-of time and suppressed-update counter; refreshed snapshots; AS-OF labelled panels; gap-recovery events in diagnostics.
capabilities.behavior: Client keeps a normalized store fed by sequenced events; on any gap (received seq != last + 1) it discards incrementals and fetches a fresh snapshot before applying more (Ch 22). Pause stops applying events to that panel's view (the store keeps updating for other panels and for risk-relevant indicators); the panel shows FROZEN with time and a suppressed-update counter. Resume = snapshot + subsequent events. Manual refresh scopes: panel, layout, all. Global 'pause all motion/flash' preference. As-of mode issues point-in-time queries using availability times so no later-available data leaks into the view; datasets without PIT support show 'as-of not supported'. Frozen or as-of values are never used as execution prices: the order ticket fetches its own fresh quote and the server re-checks freshness before transmission (Ch 11). Safety indicators (mode, stop state, reconciliation alerts) are never frozen.

capabilities.user_workflow: 1) Owner (or a schedule) requests work from a role, e.g. 'extract guidance changes from AAPL 10-Q'. 2) Scheduler builds a job envelope (job_id, role, schema_version, input artifact hashes, allowed tools, deadline, token/cost allowance, retry budget, expected output type) and shows it in the Agents screen before the first paid call. 3) Job runs; the owner sees live state (queued, running, waiting_approval, succeeded, failed, expired, cancelled) with turns used, tool calls, cost so far. 4) On completion the typed output is validated and attached to evidence; on expiry the output is marked research-only and can never attach to an order intent. 5) Owner can inspect the envelope, the trace and the reason for any stop.

reference_scope.module_or_feature: Subagent depth, concurrency and spend caps
reference_scope.supporting_quote: a subagent can spawn subagents of its own, so one prompt can grow into a tree of agents. You can cap that growth in three ways: how deeply subagents nest, how many run at once, and how much the whole query spends.

capabilities.inputs: Job request (role, task text or structured task), input artifact references (dataset version ids, document ids with content hashes), role capability manifest version, policy snapshot (deadlines, caps), relevance window for trading-relevant jobs.
capabilities.outputs: Job envelope record; job state transitions (event-sourced); typed output validated against the role's JSON schema (e.g. contracts/research_proposal.schema.json); terminal status with reason code (succeeded, schema_invalid, exceeded_turns, exceeded_tool_calls, deadline_expired, budget_exhausted, cancelled_by_owner, provider_unavailable, denied_by_policy).
capabilities.behavior: Every model-driven unit of work is a job with the fields named in chapter 19: job_id, role, schema_version, input artifact hashes, allowed tools, deadline, token/cost allowance, retry budget and expected output type. The scheduler (deterministic code, not a model) enforces: max_turns (model calls per job), max_tool_calls, wall-clock deadline, per-role concurrency, global concurrency, and spawn_depth=0 for all worker roles (workers cannot create workers; only the scheduler creates jobs, from an owner request or an approved schedule). Equivalent jobs are deduplicated by a key over role, schema version, prompt template hash and sorted input hashes. Retries honour the retry budget and provider retry-after headers and never retry spend-limit errors. A job that exceeds any cap is stopped, its partial output is retained as evidence but marked partial, and no further provider calls are made. Trading-relevant jobs carry a relevance_end timestamp; outputs produced after it are tagged research_only and the order-intent service rejects them. If a third-party agent framework is used, its own caps are configured as defence in depth: OpenAI Agents SDK max_turns (never None); Claude Agent SDK maxTurns, maxBudgetUsd and CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH / CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS, plus the bare name 'Agent' in disallowedTools so that no subagent can be spawned at all (the Claude permissions page states that in dontAsk mode tools such as Agent that need no approval still run unless removed by a bare-name deny rule). The scheduler's caps are authoritative because the Claude Agent SDK documents its cost fields as client-side estimates and its spend cap can end a query at a cost at or above the cap.

capabilities.inputs: Budget policy (per job, per role per day, global per day and month, per provider), versioned price table (model id, input/output/cache prices per million tokens, tool fees, effective date, source URL), token counts from provider count endpoints or local tokenizer, provider usage fields per response, provider cost reports.
capabilities.outputs: Admission decision per paid call (admit/deny with reason), reservations and settlements ledger, spend dashboards, daily reconciliation report (internal estimate vs provider-reported cost), alerts at thresholds, all-in P&L cost allocation feed (chapter 26 economic ledger).
capabilities.behavior: Paid calls are disabled until the owner sets a non-zero budget. Every paid call passes a reservation check: the maximum possible cost (all input priced at the highest applicable input rate, including cache-write rates, plus max_output_tokens at the output rate plus fixed tool fees) is reserved against the job, role, daily and monthly budgets atomically in one store; the OpenAI cookbook notes its lock protects only one Python process and that workers sharing a budget need a shared store that checks and reserves in a single operation. After the response, actual cost is computed from usage fields and the unused reservation is released; if the outcome cannot be confirmed (interrupted stream, timeout), the reservation stays consumed until reconciliation. Provider-side limits are configured at or below the internal global cap as a backstop: Anthropic organization spend limit (cannot exceed the tier cap) or non-default workspace spend limit (spend limits cannot be set on the default workspace); OpenAI organization or project hard limit, whose enforcement OpenAI states is not instantaneous. The fetched Anthropic page does not state enforcement latency (unverified). Provider spend-limit responses map to budget_exhausted and are never retried: Anthropic tier spend cap = HTTP 429 rate_limit_error with error.details.error_code enforced_spend_limit_reached and no retry-after header; Anthropic self-set limit = HTTP 400 invalid_request_error with message starting 'You have reached your specified API usage limits' (or '... workspace API usage limits'); OpenAI = HTTP 429 with organization_spend_limit_exceeded or project_spend_limit_exceeded. Because the Anthropic spend-cap 429 shares the rate_limit_error type with ordinary rate limits, the adapter classifies by error_code and retry-after presence, not by status code. Daily, internal estimates are reconciled against provider cost reports (Anthropic cost_report, daily granularity only, data typically within 5 minutes of request completion); discrepancies above tolerance raise an alert and freeze budget increases until explained. Costs flow into the all-in P&L with a stable allocation rule (chapter 26).

capabilities.inputs: Role definitions, signed capability manifests (role -> tool -> argument schema/constraints -> data-rights classes -> rate limits), tool registry (name, server, version, read/write classification, owner-assigned trust), job envelope.
capabilities.outputs: Allow/deny decision per tool call with rule id; denial log; per-role privilege surface report; manifest version history with signatures.
capabilities.behavior: Default deny. A tool gateway process (not the model, not the agent framework's prompt) mediates every tool call: it checks the job's role manifest, validates arguments against the tool's input schema and the manifest's constraints (allowed dataset ids, date ranges, hostnames, max result sizes), applies per-tool rate limits, and checks the data-rights class of any content the tool would return into model context. No LLM role has an order-submission, order-modification, policy-change, credential-read or stop-latch-clear tool; the planner emits proposal objects only (chapter 19/20). Read tools prefer narrow functions (e.g. get_filing_section(cik, accession, item)) over open-ended ones (shell, arbitrary URL fetch), per OWASP LLM06. Code execution for research runs in an isolated sandbox with no production credentials, read-only dataset mounts and an egress allowlist (chapter 23). MCP servers, if used, are registered with explicit trust; their tool annotations are not trusted for authorization. If the Claude Agent SDK is used as a secondary layer: allowedTools plus permissionMode 'dontAsk', and bare-name disallowedTools for every tool that must not exist in context (including 'Agent'), because the permissions page states that in dontAsk mode calls that need no approval in default mode (read-only Bash commands, Agent, file reads inside working directories) still run whether or not they are listed. bypassPermissions is prohibited because allowed_tools does not constrain it. Checks that must run on every call use a PreToolUse hook or our own gateway, because auto-approved tools never reach canUseTool. Manifest changes require owner signature and apply to future jobs only.

capabilities.title: Human-in-the-loop approval queue binding owner decisions to exact proposals
capabilities.user_workflow: 1) A planner or research job emits a proposal (allocation change, order intent, parameter change, budget increase request) as a typed object, never an executable command. 2) The proposal appears in an Approvals queue with evidence links, assumptions, downside scenarios, the deterministic pre-trade check result (and broker what-if margin/commission preview where available), and an expiry. 3) Owner approves, rejects, or asks for a revised proposal; approval requires an authenticated session and reauthentication for policy or capital changes. 4) An approved order intent still passes the independent risk supervisor before the execution service sends it. 5) Expired or superseded proposals close automatically; the agent may not re-raise a rejected proposal repeatedly.

capabilities.inputs: Typed proposal objects (proposal_id, job_id, kind, payload, evidence refs, assumptions, invalidation conditions, expiry), current state version (positions, cash, policy version), deterministic pre-trade check results, optional broker what-if preview (IBKR Order.WhatIf flag).
capabilities.outputs: Approval decision records (approve/reject/expire/supersede) with owner identity, auth method, timestamp, payload hash, state version; approved order intents forwarded to risk supervisor; notifications.
capabilities.behavior: Proposals are immutable; any modification creates a new proposal. Approval binds to SHA-256 of the canonical payload, the state version at review time, and an expiry; at execution the service recomputes the hash and checks the state version and expiry, refusing if any differ (prevents approve-then-swap and stale approvals). Approval does not bypass deterministic limits: the risk supervisor re-checks every approved intent and can still reject. Policy, capital, permission and code changes are never approvable through the agent queue; they go through the signed policy registry with reauthentication (chapter 20/23). The queue is durable: a paused agent run (e.g. OpenAI Agents SDK RunState serialized with state.to_json(), or our own job state) can wait for approval across restarts; serialized state is deserialized only from trusted storage. Notifications are advisory; a missed notification leaves existing limits intact and the proposal expires. Repeated identical proposals after rejection are suppressed for a cool-down. Override and rejection rates are tracked (NIST AI 600-1 MS-4.2-004 analogue).

capabilities.title: Owner intervention controls: pause roles, cancel jobs, disable model-dependent decisions, red stop with order cancel
capabilities.user_workflow: 1) Owner sees a controls panel: Pause role, Cancel job, Disable model-dependent decisions (model kill), and the global red stop. 2) Each control states its effect before activation (e.g. red stop cancels unexecuted entry orders; it does not liquidate unless the separate liquidation policy is chosen, chapter 22). 3) After activation the panel shows progress: jobs stopped, provider calls aborted, orders cancelled/confirmed. 4) Clearing a latch requires owner authentication, a fresh state version and passing preflight; no agent or optional worker can clear it.

MANAGE 2.4: Mechanisms are in place and applied, and responsibilities are assigned and understood, to supersede, disengage, or deactivate AI systems that demonstrate performance or outcomes inconsistent with intended use.
Establish and regularly review specific criteria that warrants the deactivation of GAI systems in accordance with set risk tolerances and appetites.
This method will cancel ALL open orders including those placed directly from TWS.

capabilities.inputs: Owner control commands (authenticated), automatic trigger conditions (loss budget breach, reconciliation mismatch, unknown order, model drift, budget exhaustion, injection detection), current jobs/orders state.
capabilities.outputs: Persisted latches (role_paused, model_decisions_disabled, trading_stop) with versions; cancellation results per job and per order; incident record.
capabilities.behavior: Four separate, independently testable controls. (a) Pause role: scheduler admits no new jobs for that role; running jobs finish or are cancelled per owner choice. (b) Cancel job: abort in-flight provider calls (framework abort controller or HTTP cancellation), mark output partial, release no reservation until reconciliation. (c) Disable model-dependent decisions: all strategies flagged model-dependent stop proposing new entries; deterministic stops, reconciliation and risk reduction continue (chapter 26 model-outage runbook). (d) Red stop (trading): persists an aggregate latch first, then cancels unexecuted entry orders through the broker adapter (per-order cancels, or IBKR reqGlobalCancel where the owner accepts that it also cancels orders placed directly from TWS), then reconciles until every order is in a final state. Each order carries strategy artifact hash, job_id/proposal_id and session id so the source of every order can be identified (analogue of the RTS 6 Art. 12 requirement to identify the algorithm, trader, desk or client responsible for each order; SEBI requires all algo orders to be tagged with an exchange-provided unique identifier to establish an audit trail). Latches are stored durably and re-applied on restart before any component starts. Automatic triggers can only tighten; only the owner can loosen. Deactivation criteria are written down and reviewed (NIST MG-2.4-004).

latch_persistence = latch_state_after_restart == latch_state_before_restart (boolean; must be true)

capabilities.inputs: Untrusted content (SEC filings, exchange announcements, news, web pages, transcripts, owner uploads, tool and sub-agent outputs), each with provenance (source id, URL, retrieval time, content hash).
capabilities.outputs: Model context with untrusted content delimited and tagged; injection-detection flags (informational); evidence records; red-team suite results.
capabilities.behavior: Primary defences are architectural, not textual: (1) tool authority comes only from the signed role manifest and the job envelope, never from content (see tool allowlist record); (2) no role that reads untrusted content has a write-capable tool; (3) outputs are typed and validated by deterministic code (schema, numeric ranges, instrument identity, timestamp plausibility) before any downstream use (OWASP LLM05 Improper Output Handling); (4) numerical claims used in calculations are re-extracted by typed parsers from cited spans (chapter 11); (5) secrets never enter context (see secrets record). Secondary layers: untrusted content placed in clearly delimited data blocks with provenance tags; instruction-pattern screening (logged, not a boundary); sub-agent and tool outputs treated as untrusted (the Claude Agent SDK scan only neutralizes or marks patterns and never removes text, so it is not a boundary); HTML rendered as text in the terminal (chapter 23). Owner uploads are also untrusted. A held-out injection corpus (filings and news with embedded instructions, hidden text, homoglyphs, instructions in tables/footnotes, tool-output injections) runs on every model, prompt or tool change.

Fetched 2026-10-22, it lists API Stable 1050.02 (released Sep 9 2026) and Latest 1051.01 (released Sep 29 2026), recommends TWS/IB Gateway 1050.02 or higher, and describes package contents: Stable 1050.02 for Windows includes the Java, C++, C#/.NET, ActiveX and DDE APIs; Stable 1050.02 for Mac/Linux includes the Java and Posix C++ API source; the Latest 1051.01 packages 'additionally' include the Python API. The page does not list Python in Stable, so a Python adapter pins Latest unless an inspected Stable installer is shown to contain the Python client. Artifacts are platform installers linked from the page (for example tws-api-stable-macos-arm.dmg, tws-api-stable-macosx-x64.dmg, tws-api-stable-linux-x64.sh, tws-api-stable-windows-x64.exe, and the same names with 'latest'). The Mac/Linux install page still describes twsapi_macunix.<Major>.<Minor>.zip extracted to ~/IBJts with source/pythonclient and API_VersionNum.txt, so it may be out of date. The Python client is installed from the extracted source (the install page shows cd ~/IBJts/source/pythonclient then python3 -m pip install ., as a fix when python3 setup.py install fails). Minimum Python 3.11.0, Java 21, C++14. After the protobuf migration, C++ clients should link statically. TWS API 10.40 added a Python-only synchronous wrapper (TWSSyncWrapper, https://www.interactivebrokers.com/docs/tws-api/sync-doc/introduction.md). From API 10.44, tick types 5 and 71 return Decimal sizes. Host builds fetched 2026-10-22 from IBKR's version.json manifests: IB Gateway and TWS standalone Latest 10.51.1d (built 2026-10-20 16:53:27) and Stable 10.50.1f (built 2026-10-05 16:18:53). The IB Gateway download page says neither build updates automatically. IBKR recommends offline TWS (the online version auto-updates) and the same TWS and API version. An out-of-date host returns error 503. PyPI 'ibapi' JSON shows only 9.81.1 and 9.81.1.post1 (uploaded 2020-12-06), author 'IBG LLC', licence 'IB API Non-Commercial License or the IB API Commercial License'. Because IBKR disclaims pip distribution and that package is about six years older than current releases, the adapter must reject a PyPI-sourced ibapi. Licence: per the 2026-08-03 changelog, 'TWS API 10.49+ is released under the GNU General Public License (GPL)'; the GPL version was not stated on any fetched page. The architecture introduction page still says 'The TWS API is a BSD implementation', and the PyPI ibapi metadata names a non-commercial/commercial licence, so IBKR's own pages disagree; the licence file shipped inside the pinned installer is the deciding artifact. Implementation: install the SDK from a private artifact store at a pinned SHA-256, record the licence file it ships with, refuse order entry when the imported module path or hash differs from the pin, and log API version, host build and server version at every connect.

capabilities.behavior: Default ports, all user-modifiable: TWS live 7496, TWS paper 7497, IB Gateway live 4001, IB Gateway paper 4002 (DDE socket-bridge and RTD connection-parameter pages; IBKR Campus lesson). Because ports can be changed, the adapter must not infer mode from the port. It requires all of: (a) the configured port matches the mode profile, (b) the managed-account list delivered at handshake equals the expected account id from the deployment record, and (c) a credential profile separated per mode. Required host settings: 'Enable ActiveX and Socket Clients', Read-Only API disabled only when order entry is approved (Read-Only is on by default and blocks all API orders), and the socket port verified. Trusted-IP or localhost settings let the host accept connections automatically; untrusted IPs are denied. Connection: eConnect opens TCP. Error 502 means the OS could not open the socket (most commonly host not running with the API enabled or a different socket port; across a network also a firewall, antivirus or an IP missing from Trusted IPs). Error 501 means already connected; 504 means not connected. A version handshake follows. Do not create the EReader before the connection exists. The host then sends the accessible account numbers, the next valid order id and the connection time; requests sent before nextValidId may be dropped. Each host instance accepts up to 32 API clients. Connecting with a clientId already in use triggers an EReader exception (broken-api-socket-connection.md). Login is manual in the host GUI; IBKR does not support headless TWS or IB Gateway. IB Gateway lacks TWS's trading tools and monitoring GUI but still needs a GUI login window, consumes 'about 40% fewer resources', and is identical to TWS from the API's view. TWS locks after inactivity for IBHK users. Paper accounts: each live account structure has a paper account with unique credentials. A paper account needs an approved and funded live account and is created within about 24 hours. Residents of India and Japan must log in with paper credentials. The Web API and third-party platforms always require paper credentials. A username can be logged into only one trading application at a time; create extra usernames for parallel use. If the TWS/IBGW username is also used to log in to Client Portal, the host cannot reconnect automatically after the next disconnection (for example the server reset), so Client Portal needs a different username. IBKR Canada does not allow API orders for Canadian-listed products (tws-api-limitations.md); add this to eligibility policy.

reference_scope.supporting_quote: The Order ID is a client-managed identifier used to track, modify, and cancel orders. As a result, it must be strictly increasing.
It is necessary to use an order ID with new orders which is greater than all previous order IDs used to place an order.
The next valid identifier is persistent between TWS sessions. ... the order sequence Id can only be reset if there are no active API orders.
the mapping between the permID (unique account-wide) and API Order ID (specific to an API client).
Connecting without using the Master Client ID will mean only trades on the connected Client ID will be returning from calls to the openOrder or execDetails functions.
Requests all current open orders in associated accounts at the current moment. ... Open orders are returned once; this function does not initiate a subscription.
Requests status updates about future orders placed from TWS. Can only be used with client ID 0.
The process of order binding from the API cancels/resubmits an order working on an exchange. This may affect the order's place in the exchange queue.
This method will cancel ALL open orders including those placed directly from TWS.
EClient.reqCompletedOrders allows users to request all orders for the given day that are no longer modifiable.
permId int64 The Host order identifier. ... orderRef string The order reference. Intended for institutional customers only
103 Duplicate order ID. An order was placed with an order ID that is less than or equal to the order ID of a previous order from this client

capabilities.inputs: Approved intent (local intent id, payload hash); persisted id allocator state per (host username, clientId); nextValidId callbacks; openOrder/orderStatus/orderBound callbacks.
capabilities.outputs: Durable identity map {intent_id, account, clientId, orderId, permId, orderRef, replacement chain}; anomaly events (duplicate id, id regression, external order).
capabilities.behavior: orderId is client-managed and must be strictly increasing and greater than every earlier order id used by that client. Error 103 'Duplicate order ID' fires when an id is less than or equal to an earlier id from this client (error-codes.md). nextValidId is called once on initial connection, and reqIds() requests it again (order-id.md). IBKR says it is often recommended to request it once at the start of the session and increment locally. The sequence persists across TWS sessions and can be reset in API settings only when no API orders are active. Market-data request ids do not consume order ids, but two active requests cannot share an id. The Execution object says orderId 'May not be unique to an account'. permId is the host identifier, 'unique account-wide', and is 0 for trades originating outside IB. API orders are bound to the submitting clientId; only that client, on a session with the same username, can modify one, by re-sending placeOrder with the same orderId. IBKR advises modifying only price, size and tif (DAY to IOC) and otherwise cancelling and re-entering. The Master Client ID setting lets one connection receive orders and executions from other API clients; clientId 0 also receives TWS and FIX orders. reqOpenOrders from client 0 binds manual TWS orders and fires the orderBound callback, which reports the mapping between permID and API order ID. Binding is rejected in Read-Only mode and cancels/resubmits the working order, which may lose queue priority. reqAllOpenOrders is a one-shot snapshot that does not bind. reqAutoOpenOrders(autoBind) works for client 0 only. Open-order requests never return cancelled or fully filled orders; reqCompletedOrders returns the day's orders that are no longer modifiable (executed, rejected or cancelled). Its parameters were not documented on the fetched page; bind to the pinned SDK signature. reqGlobalCancel cancels ALL open orders, including manual TWS orders. Implementation: allocate next_order_id = max(last nextValidId, persisted max + 1) inside the outbox transaction; use (account, permId) as the durable broker key once permId is non-zero; carry the local intent id in orderRef only if confirmed usable for this account type (the Order reference says orderRef is 'Intended for institutional customers only', while the Execution object calls it user-customizable).

capabilities.title: Normalizing orderStatus, openOrder and order errors into intent, transmission and economic states
capabilities.user_workflow: 1) The adapter receives orderStatus, openOrder and error callbacks. 2) It deduplicates them and maps each to the book's local states (SUBMIT_PENDING, ACKNOWLEDGED, PARTIALLY_FILLED, CANCEL_PENDING, FILLED, CANCELED, REJECTED, UNKNOWN). 3) Economic state (fills, fees) comes only from executions. 4) The owner sees in the blotter why an order was capped, held, rejected or cancelled.

reference_scope.supporting_quote: Gives the up-to-date information of an order every time it changes. Often there are duplicate orderStatus messages.
PendingCancel ... At this point, your order is not confirmed canceled. You may still receive an execution while your cancellation request is pending.
Cancelled: Indicates that the balance of your order has been confirmed canceled by the system. This could occur unexpectedly when the destination has rejected your order.
If an order is subject to price checks the client may receive status (cancelled) + Error (202) via IBApi.EWrapper.orderStatus and IBApi::EWrapper::error.
EWrapper.openOrder (orderId, contract, order, orderState) ... Feeds in currently open orders. ... EWrapper.openOrderEnd () Notifies the end of the open orders' reception.
customers will typically need to acknowledge a precautionary message and manually transmit the orders through the Trader Workstation.
Enable "Bypass Order Precautions for API orders".
2102 Unable to modify this order as it is still being processed. ... 104 Can't modify a filled order. ... 201 Order rejected – Reason:

capabilities.inputs: orderStatus(orderId, status, filled, remaining, avgFillPrice, permId, parentId, lastFillPrice, clientId, whyHeld, mktCapPrice); openOrder(orderId, contract, order, orderState incl. status, warningText, rejectReason, completedStatus); error(reqId/orderId, code, message).
capabilities.outputs: Deduplicated order-state transition events with cause codes; blotter rows; alerts for unknown statuses.
capabilities.behavior: IBKR statuses: Inactive, PendingSubmit, PreSubmitted (accepted but not yet elected), Submitted (working), Filled, PendingCancel and PreCancelled (cancel not yet confirmed; executions can still arrive), Cancelled (can happen unexpectedly when the destination rejects), WarnState. Duplicate orderStatus messages are normal. Mapping: PendingSubmit to SUBMIT_PENDING; PreSubmitted and Submitted to ACKNOWLEDGED, or PARTIALLY_FILLED when filled > 0; PendingCancel and PreCancelled to CANCEL_PENDING; Filled to FILLED_STATUS (the economic close needs executions); Cancelled to CANCELED, or REJECTED when an error 201 or 202 for that order came first; WarnState to ACKNOWLEDGED with a warning; Inactive and any unknown string to UNKNOWN with an alert. Rejections and cancels: error 201 'Order rejected – Reason:'. Size or price checks can produce a large-size reject (201) or status Cancelled plus 202 when the price is too far through the market. openOrder warningText can warn about price capping; orderStatus.mktCapPrice gives the capped price. whyHeld = 'locate' marks a short sale held for locate; error 404 means shares are not available for short sale and the order is held. Modify and cancel errors: 104 (filled), 105 (mismatch), 2102 (still processing), 135 and 10147 (not found), 136, 161 and 10148 (not cancellable). Error 2109 means outsideRth was ignored. Order precautions: TWS may require manual acknowledgement unless the API precaution bypasses are enabled. The adapter's own pre-trade checks must not depend on IBKR precautions; the bypass setting is an explicit owner decision. Positions and cash come from executions, never from orderStatus.filled (book chapter 13).

reference_scope.supporting_quote: If a correction to an execution is published it will be received as an additional IBApi.EWrapper.execDetails callback with all parameters identical except for the execID ... The execID will differ only in the digits after the final period.
Each partial fill has a separate ExecId. ... an ExecId ending in ".02" would be a correction of a previous execution with an ExecId ending in ".01".
When an order is filled either fully or partially, the IBApi.EWrapper.execDetails and IBApi.EWrapper.commissionReport events will deliver IBApi.Execution and IBApi.CommissionAndFeesReport objects.
execId string the execution's id this commission belongs to. commissionAndFees double the combined cost of commissions and fees. currency ... realizedPNL double the realized profit and loss
By default, only those executions occurring since midnight for that particular account will be delivered. ... The IB Gateway is limited to only executions from the current trading day since midnight.
Requests current day's (since midnight) executions and commission report matching the filter. Only the current day's executions can be retrieved.

permId int64 The TWS order identifier. The PermId can be 0 for trades originating outside IB. ... isPriceRevisionPending bool Indicates the price the order executed as may be changed.
An unset value is the maximum value of a given data type. So the Unset Double value will appear like 1.7976931348623157E308

capabilities.outputs: Append-only executions journal with correction links; fee records per execId and currency; derived position and cash deltas; history-gap flags.
capabilities.behavior: Live path: each full or partial fill delivers execDetails and a CommissionAndFeesReport (fields execId, commissionAndFees, currency, realizedPNL, bondYield, yieldRedemptionDate). The docs give no ordering or latency guarantee between the two, so join by execId and accept either arrival order. The docs name the callback both commissionReport (text) and commissionAndFeesReport (code); bind to the name in the pinned SDK. Unset doubles (1.7976931348623157E308), for example realizedPNL, map to null. Execution fields include orderId (not account-unique), clientId, execId, time (server time string), acctNumber, exchange, side (BOT/SLD), shares, price (excluding commissions), permId (0 for trades outside IB), isLiquidation, cumQty, avgPrice, orderRef, lastLiquidity, isPriceRevisionPending, submitter (field names per the Execution reference; the narrative Execution page uses older names such as Liquidation and pendingPriceRevision). Corrections arrive as another execDetails identical except for the execId digits after the final period ('.02' corrects '.01'); the correction replaces the earlier record and is not additive. Combo per-leg executions can carry a 5-segment execId. Backfill: reqExecutions with an empty filter returns all available executions, then execDetailsEnd. By default only executions since midnight are returned. The execution-details introduction says 7 days are available when TWS's Trade Log setting 'Show trades for ...' is raised, and that IB Gateway returns only the current day since midnight. The request page says only the current day can be retrieved, and the receive page says 'the last 24 hours'. The ExecutionFilter reference allows lastNDays up to 7 and specificDates within the past week. These official statements conflict, so the adapter treats history beyond the current day as unavailable unless verified on the pinned host. Without the master client id (or client 0), execDetails returns only that clientId's trades. Longer history: Flex Queries in Client Portal cover the four previous calendar years plus the current year. Paper statements are available by logging into Client Portal with the paper login (aboutpapertradingaccounts.htm). The Web API /iserver/account/trades covers up to 7 days via its days parameter and returns only the current day when days is omitted.

capabilities.title: Connectivity loss and restore handling (1100/1101/1102/1300/2110, farm codes, socket EOF) and host-side order resubmission
capabilities.user_workflow: 1) When the host reports loss of connectivity to IBKR, the adapter blocks new entries, marks in-flight intents UNKNOWN and shows 'broker connectivity lost'. 2) On restore it resubscribes market data if data was lost and reconciles orders and executions. 3) It returns to READY only after reconciliation passes. 4) Scheduled IBKR resets show as maintenance, not incidents.

reference_scope.supporting_quote: Error code 2104, 2106, and 2158 all generally state that farm connection is OK. ... There is no issue with the connection, and it is a sign you connected successfully.
Once a connection fails for any reason, the EWrapper.connectionClosed function will be called. This function can be used to build reconnection logic or affirm a system disconnect.
When this setting is checked, all orders received while connectivity is lost will be saved and automatically resubmitted when connectivity is restored.

capabilities.inputs: error(code, message) stream including system codes; connectionClosed; isConnected; reset calendar from System Status.
capabilities.outputs: Normalized connectivity state (READY, UPSTREAM_DOWN, SOCKET_DOWN, RECONCILING, MAINTENANCE_WINDOW); actions (block entries, resubscribe, reconcile); owner alerts by severity.
capabilities.behavior: Codes. 1100: host lost connectivity to IB (internet, nightly reset or competing session). 1101: restored, market data lost, all market-data requests must be resubmitted. 1102: restored, data maintained. 1300: socket port changed during an active connection; reconnect on the new port. 2110: host-server connectivity broken, restored automatically, usually during the nightly reset. 2103/2105: market or historical data farm disconnected (outside the reset, usually an ISP problem). 2104/2106/2158: farm OK (informational). 2107/2108: farm inactive but available on demand (normal). 2119: farm connecting. 10197: no market data during a competing paper/live session. Socket failures: connectionClosed fires; Java reports 507, C# reports -1; the Python path must treat EReader exceptions and connectionClosed as SOCKET_DOWN. Resets: the platform runs 24/7 except reset windows. Sunday to Friday: North America 00:15-01:45 ET, Europe 06:25-07:45 CET, APAC 04:45-06:05 HKT and 20:15-21:15 HKT. Saturday: 00:00-02:00 ET in all regions. APAC reset time in HKT is one hour later when North American daylight saving time is not in effect. The reset period is when the account 'may be unavailable for a brief period'; login and order management may be interrupted; existing native orders operate normally, but execution reports and simulated orders are delayed until the reset completes. Host-side resubmission: 'Maintain and resubmit orders when connection is restored' is on by default. Orders received while connectivity is lost are saved and resubmitted automatically on restore, and deleted if TWS is closed. So an order the adapter believes failed may still be transmitted later. Therefore: (1) block new entries on 1100 or 2110 (book chapter 24); (2) mark any order sent within an owner-set guard interval before loss as UNKNOWN; (3) on 1101/1102 reconcile via reqAllOpenOrders, reqCompletedOrders and reqExecutions before READY; (4) the owner decides whether to disable the resubmission setting, and the adapter records the attested setting in the session record.

capabilities.title: Broker-aware request pacing, market-data line budget and historical-data limits
capabilities.user_workflow: 1) The adapter reads the owner's market-data line allowance (default 100) from configuration. 2) It derives the request budget and schedules entries, cancels, queries and subscriptions in separate bounded queues, reserving capacity for cancels and reconciliation. 3) It shows live budget usage and any IBKR pacing error.

reference_scope.supporting_quote: The maximum number of API requests that can be submitted are equivalent to your Maximum Market Data Lines divided by 2, per second. By default, all users maintain 100 market data lines ... 50 requests per second.
If the setting is checked, TWS will notify the user they surpassed the pacing limit using error code 100. If the pacing limits are broken 3 times, the API session will terminate
the greater value of: USD monthly commissions divided by 8; USD equity multiplied by 100 divided by $1,000,000 (rounded down to the nearest integer); 100
Market data lines dictate how much market data can be retrieved simultaneously from a given user. This Includes all data pulled through Trader Workstation watchlist and the API.

Making identical historical data requests within 15 seconds. Making six or more historical data requests for the same Contract, Exchange and Tick Type within two seconds. Making more than 60 requests within any ten minute period.
Max number (3) of market depth requests has been reached. Note: TWS currently limits users to a maximum of 3 distinct market depth requests.
Interactive Brokers as a whole maintains an order pacing limitation. This is known as the Order Efficiency Ratio. ... will effect those who submit thousands of orders without regular execution.

Interactive Brokers currently enforces a global request rate limit of 10 requests per second for each authenticated username ... When a rate limit is exceeded, the Web API will return a 429 Too Many Requests status code.

capabilities.inputs: Configured market-data line allowance L (owner-attested; Ctrl+Alt+= or Cmd+Opt+'+' in TWS shows usage); request stream by class; error codes 100, 101, 162, 309, 420.
capabilities.outputs: Scheduled request emissions; budget-usage metrics; pacing violation events.
capabilities.behavior: TWS API: requests per second = market-data lines / 2. The default is 100 lines, so 50 requests/s; 200 lines (via commissions or Quote Booster) gives 100/s. Only the initial request of a streaming subscription counts. Above 50 requests/s some orders may be queued and delayed; IBKR suggests FIX instead, where the IB Gateway FIX limit is 250 messages/s. Host setting 'Reject messages above maximum allowed message rate vs applying pacing': when checked, error 100 is returned and the third violation terminates the session (BrokenPipe on macOS/Linux); when unchecked, the host paces requests itself. Error 100 text says 50 messages/second. Line allocation after the first month = max(USD monthly commissions/8, floor(USD equity*100/1,000,000), 100). Lines are shared between the TWS watchlist and all API connections for the username; exceeding them gives error 101. Market depth: at most 3 distinct depth requests (309). Historical data, bars of 30 s or less: no identical requests within 15 s, no 6 or more requests for the same contract/exchange/tick type within 2 s, no more than 60 requests in any 10 minutes; BID_ASK counts twice; IBKR says these limits apply to all clients and cannot be modified. Unavailable history includes bars of 30 s or less older than six months, expired futures older than two years from expiry, expired options, FOPs, warrants and structured products, securities that are no longer trading, and Time & Sales beyond 3 years. Historical volume is filtered and differs from real-time volume. Regulatory snapshots are limited to 1 request per minute (streaming-data.md). The firm-wide Order Efficiency Ratio also applies; the IBKR article giving its formula was not retrieved. Web API (if used): 10 requests/s per username, per-endpoint limits (the pacing table lists /iserver/orders and /iserver/trades at 1 req/5 secs and /tickle at 1 req/sec), HTTP 429 and a 10-minute IP penalty box. Implementation: token buckets per class drawing on one shared host budget, a reserved share for cancels and reconciliation, the historical-request rule set, and 'reject' mode on the host so violations are visible rather than silently delayed (owner choice).

capabilities.title: Daily auto-restart, weekly re-authentication and 2FA constraints for unattended paper operation
capabilities.user_workflow: 1) Owner sets 'Never lock' and 'Auto restart' in IB Gateway Lock and Exit settings, with a restart time outside market hours and outside IBKR reset windows. 2) After each auto-restart the adapter reconnects, reconciles and resumes. 3) Once a week (or after a Saturday reset) the adapter detects that a login is needed, enters AUTH_REQUIRED, notifies the owner and keeps research running. 4) Owner logs in manually with a supported 2FA method; the adapter reconciles and waits for an explicit green start if the stop latch is set.

reference_scope.supporting_quote: For API users, it is recommended to choose "Never lock Trader Workstation" and "Auto restart". ... The weekly authentication cycle starts on every Monday.

Beginning in version 974+ both applications offer an autorestart feature ... can potentially run from Sunday to Sunday without re-authenticating. After the nightly server reset on Saturday night it will be necessary to again enter security credentials.
Two Factor Authentication (2FA) is required for all users ... Supported 2FA Methods: IB Key, Handy Key (Smart Phone applications), SMS / Text Messages, Digital Security Card+ (DSC+)
It is compulsory for TWS users to auto logoff/auto restart TWS daily and manually login TWS weekly. ... Windows Sleeping Mode also causes API disconnection.
all IBHK users cannot choose "Never Lock Trader Workstation" in TWS – Global Configuration – Lock and Exit. If there is inactivity, TWS will be locked and there will be API disconnection.
Interactive Brokers does not support an automated authentication process for Client Portal Gateway.

capabilities.behavior: TWS and IB Gateway are designed to restart daily, partly to re-download contract definitions. From version 974+, auto-restart lets them run from Sunday to Sunday without re-authenticating, but credentials are needed again after the Saturday-night server reset (IB Gateway page). The reauthentication page recommends 'Never lock Trader Workstation' and 'Auto restart' under Global Configuration > Lock and Exit, and says the weekly authentication cycle starts every Monday. The message 'Login failed = Soft token=0 received instead of expected permanent for zdc1.ibllc.com:4001 (SSL)' means a manual login is needed. The DDE best-practice page calls daily auto logoff/restart and weekly manual login compulsory and warns that Windows sleep breaks the API connection; a sleeping Mac host is likewise not continuous (book chapter 24). IBHK users lack 'Never lock' and 'Auto restart' in TWS and should use IB Gateway. 2FA is required for all users. Supported: IB Key, Handy Key, SMS, DSC+. Unsupported: Security Code Card, Temporary Security Code Card, Online Code Card. Headless TWS/IBGW is not supported and the Client Portal Gateway has no supported automated authentication. The adapter must therefore not drive the login GUI or store 2FA secrets (book chapter 12). Reset windows (System Status) bound the restart time, for example avoiding 00:15-01:45 ET Sunday to Friday in North America. After any restart: socket drops, reconnect, full reconciliation; READY only after checks; the stop latch persists (book chapter 13).

capabilities.behavior: IBKR cash account (Campus glossary): cash must cover cost plus commissions; 'No shorting of stock or futures day trading benefits'; 'Limited purchase and sale of options and multi-currency trading is allowed through Forex conversions'; sale proceeds become available when the transaction settles. The glossary's 'US stock – three days' example is outdated relative to current US settlement (verify against the book's settlement chapter), so settlement lags come from a dated per-market calendar, never from this glossary. A cash account can be upgraded to margin in Client Portal if eligibility requirements are met (the glossary does not describe a downgrade path); the adapter treats any AccountType other than the expected one as a blocking mismatch. Broker-side signals: error 426 ('You are not able to enter short position with Cash Account'); error 404 (shares not available to short, order held while locating); orderStatus.whyHeld='locate'. The shortable tick (>2.5: at least 1000 shares; >1.5: available if located; <=1.5: not available) is informational and never permission to short. The TWS API offers pre-borrow (secType SBL, exchange PREBORROW, MKT); the adapter rejects SBL entirely. Order.action allows BUY and SELL (SSHORT/SLONG institutional only). Paper accounts mirror the live account's configuration, so a paper account under a margin live account allows margin and shorting at IBKR; the adapter's local rules are the control. Owner option: create a limited-permission username without withdrawal access for the adapter (arranged through IBKR's account configuration team). Local rules (book chapter 13): SELL qty <= confirmed unreserved long qty; BUY notional + fees <= settled cash available under policy; any what-if preview showing a margin increase for a cash-policy account is rejected.

capabilities.behavior: Prerequisites: opened IBKR Pro account (demo accounts cannot subscribe), USD 500 plus subscription costs, subscriptions bought in Client Portal, and the Market Data API Acknowledgement signed (otherwise requests fail as 'not subscribed'). The API User Activity Certification is assigned to users with US Futures trading permissions who have used the API to submit trades (CME Rule 576); within it, a trader submitting API orders without manual approval should select 'generated & submitted by an automated system'. It does not apply to a stock-only username per its introduction page, but becomes relevant if futures permissions are enabled. Users default to Professional; the owner must update status if eligible. Subscriptions are per username, billed per calendar month and not pro-rated. Free on-platform TWS data may not be available through the API (error 10089 'API data requires subscription'). Paper: each live user can share data with one paper account. A paper session gets no data if the sharing live user is logged into Client Portal, so use another username. Simultaneous live and paper live-data requests give error 10197, and live wins. Regulatory snapshots are not available on paper. Data types: 1 Live, 2 Frozen (last data at close; needs the same subscriptions), 3 Delayed (free, 15-20 minutes delayed, tick ids 66-76), 4 Delayed Frozen. EWrapper.marketDataType reports the type actually delivered; IBKR returns the most recent data the subscriptions allow regardless of the requested type. Watchlist data are time-based aggregate snapshots, not tick-by-tick; a snapshot returns the most recent data from the past 11 seconds. A paid subscription is required for live API data (except delayed); OSE data is delayed-only via API. Labelling: every quote stored or displayed carries its delivered type; a delayed quote must never pass a freshness check meant for live execution prices (book chapters 1 and 11). Rights: the TWS API may not be used to disseminate market data to third parties without IBKR approval. No IBKR statement on storing market data or submitting it to cloud AI models was found; treat both as not permitted for exchange data until verified (book chapter 11 rule).
